taxonomy.design_provenance: Independent ANS design informed by supplied NOSLegal v4.02 workbook / v4 guide, Trilegal public evidence and SEBI primary sources. Not an internal Trilegal org chart.

model_rules.primary_practice: Optional presentation field; never an exclusive routing gate.
model_rules.level_4: Reserved for demonstrated routing need; no mandatory fourth tier.
model_rules.topic_tagging: Leaf topics are reusable independently of practice tree.
model_rules.unknown_values: Use null with a missing_reason, never fabricated OTHER labels.
model_rules.empty_arrays: No materially applicable value identified; distinct from not assessed.
model_rules.bare_acronyms: Resolve context: DP=depository participant or designated person; IP=institutional placement or investigation period; QIP of units != ICDR QIP.
model_rules.historical_context: Store framework version applicable to the event, not only the current family label.
model_rules.no_negative_inference: No tag means no assessed relevance, not proof of legal non-application.

legal_effect.definition: Establishes a new operative regulatory framework; not a title-based inference.
Changes text of an identified instrument/provision.
Replaces identified directions, subject to scope and savings.
Repeals an identified instrument; savings remain separate.
Repeals only identified provisions.
Rescinds specified circular directions; preserve scope and savings.
Collects existing requirements; does not itself prove substantive novelty.
Clarifies operation or meaning; record affected proposition.
Applies or interprets law with authority appropriate to document type.
Specifies implementation of an underlying rule.
Moves a compliance deadline later.
Postpones commencement/applicability of identified provisions.
Other timetable change, including acceleration.
Express exemption for identified parties, conduct or conditions.
Removes an identified exemption.
Adds a substantive duty.
Eliminates a substantive duty in the specified scope.
Reduces burden/restriction, with evidence of before and after.
Increases burden/restriction, with evidence.
Consultative proposal, not operative law.
Corrigendum or demonstrable correction; check substantive consequences.
Introduces or alters regulatory process.
Disposes of specified proceedings by settlement.
Order imposes a specific sanction or direction.
Stays an order/provision in identified scope.
Judicial/appellate setting aside of specified decision.
Returns a matter for further determination.
Dismisses proceeding/application/appeal, with disposition recorded.
Allows appeal/application or grants substantive relief.
Requires recovery, repayment or refund in identified scope.

Implement margin, position or other risk controls.
Respond to inquiry, notice or regulator.

Execute exit, redemption or winding-up action.
Informational/consolidation event without proven new duty.

operative_status.definition: Proposed text has no enacted legal effect.
Final provision whose commencement is later than as_of.
Effective within identified scope as of stated date.
Operation stayed by competent authority in stated scope.
Replaced in specified scope; preserve savings.
Repealed in specified scope; preserve savings.
Roll-up only where child events have different statuses; prohibited at atomic event level.

document_type.definition: Operational/regulatory directions; scope determined from text.

Non-binding proposed policy, including annexed draft circulars.
Authority and factual limitations must be captured.
Announcement; not a substitute for operative legal instrument.
Record issuer, SEBI adoption status and binding link.
Interpretive secondary material, not primary law.

authority_scope.definition: Binding scope subject to enabling authority and applicability.
Operative only for identified case/parties, with possible precedential relevance.

procedural_stage.definition: SAT, Supreme Court or writ review.

notification_importance.definition: Verified material action or prohibition for the subscribed population, effective now or within 2 business days, with credible risk of losing market access, breaching law or irreversible transaction harm. Requires reviewer approval.
Material new or changed eligibility, rights, obligations, transaction route or control; or material matched deadline within 10 business days. Not critical.
Meaningful procedural/reporting change, relevant interpretive decision, or material consultation without urgent action.
Narrow clarification, editorial correction or marginal change with limited workflow impact.
Consolidation with no verified substantive change, general publicity or selected case report without an identified action.

classification_contract.unit: Document version contains one or more scoped events. Classify events first; document tags are union for discovery only.
classification_contract.practice_fields: Primary may be null for an omnibus event; all matched primary/secondary practices have equal eligibility.
classification_contract.participants: Array of {participant_ref, entity_tags, role_tags, relation_to, applicability_basis}; bind sponsor/manager to the relevant vehicle.
classification_contract.instruments: Array of {instrument_ref, instrument_tags, attribute_tags}; keep attributes with their instrument.
classification_contract.framework_refs: Array of {family_id,version_id,provisions,relationship: operative_basis|affected|background}. Only substantive basis/affected links match normal subscriptions.
classification_contract.legal_effects: Array of {effect_id,target_document_id,target_version_id,target_provisions,effect_mode:actual|proposed,savings,source_locator}. Bare effects without target/evidence cannot establish change.
classification_contract.temporal: Per event/cohort: {as_of,operative_status,effective_from,effective_until,deadline,deadline_basis,conditions,savings}. EXTENDED/DEFERRED are changes, not perpetual statuses.
classification_contract.evidence: Per consequential label/claim: exact page/paragraph, short passage or character span, source version hash and fact/inference basis.
classification_contract.confidence: HIGH=operative passage directly supports labels; MEDIUM=contextual inference or broad consolidation; LOW=insufficient evidence, OCR uncertainty or ambiguous scope. Not calibrated probability.
classification_contract.importance: Separate editorial importance, personal relevance and deadline urgency; recompute at delivery using the user timezone/business calendar.
case_rules: Distinguish allegation, finding, admission, settlement and disposition.
A settlement without admission does not prove the allegation.
Do not automatically apply a case-specific order to all regulated entities.
classification_contract.jurisdiction: Array of {country_code: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, relationship: governing_law|asset_location|entity_domicile|offering_location}. IFSC is not a country code.
classification_contract.authority: Separate regulator/issuer enum SEBI|MCA|RBI|IFSCA|SAT|SUPREME_COURT|HIGH_COURT|NCLT|STOCK_EXCHANGE; preserve exact body/name and legal capacity. A court is an authority, not a SEBI department.
classification_contract.forum: Optional {forum_type: SEBI_AO|SEBI_BOARD_WTM|SAT|SUPREME_COURT|HIGH_COURT|NCLT|SPECIAL_COURT|OTHER_VERIFIED,forum_name,proceeding_reference}. OTHER_VERIFIED requires the exact verified name.
classification_contract.market_venue: Optional {venue_type: DOMESTIC_EXCHANGE|INDIA_IFSC|OVERSEAS_EXCHANGE|OTC,venue_name,country_code}. A venue does not alone determine regulatory jurisdiction.
classification_contract.department: Optional {department_id,raw_department,raw_division,attribution_basis: explicit_issuer|proceeding_reference|inferred_policy_owner,source_locator}; keep issuer and inferred owner in separate records.
classification_contract.no_action_rule: AC_NO_ACTION cannot coexist with a mandatory action within the same atomic event/population. Split recipient scope or separate consolidated historical actions from new duties.

routing_contract.subscription_storage: Separate user/profile table referencing stable tag IDs; no named lawyers in taxonomy.
routing_contract.subscription_groups: OR between groups; AND between populated families inside a group; OR within a family. All conditions must match the same event.
routing_contract.hierarchy: include_descendants=true by default; collect ancestor matches, never auto-match siblings.
routing_contract.primary_practice_weight: No hard gate and no automatic priority advantage over secondary practice.
routing_contract.exclusions: Apply to the event/group, not the entire document. Hard exclusions beat positive matches in that group. Explicit user-authored override group may opt back in.
routing_contract.mention_filter: Background citations, boilerplate legal powers and mailing-list addressees do not alone satisfy a substantive-interest subscription.
routing_contract.cross_practice: Optional suggestion; requires event evidence to assign, and a matching user subscription to deliver.
routing_contract.bundle: Combine multiple matched events from same document version in one message with all match reasons.
routing_contract.refresh: A new PDF hash at the same URL is a new source version. Compare content before notifying; do not re-alert on formatting alone.
routing_contract.reminders: Use event deadlines/cohort applicability and opted-in reminders; do not notify historical deadlines as upcoming.
routing_contract.channels: Digest default; immediate alerts only for matched HIGH/CRITICAL changes according to profile preference.

governance.ids: Permanent after V1 approval. Display names and parent placements may evolve; never reuse retired IDs.
governance.versioning: Semantic taxonomy versions and dated legal-framework versions are separate.
governance.changes: Owner reviews split/merge requests using routing evidence, recurrence and lawyer comprehensibility.
governance.review_cycle: Monthly during pilot; quarterly after stabilisation; source changes continuously.
governance.new_node_gate: Recurring regulatory concept with distinct lawyer interest that cannot be served adequately by existing facet conjunction.
governance.deprecation: Retain obsolete IDs and explicit replacements. Splits require review or subscription selection; no silent expansion.
governance.source_precedence: Official signed/Gazette text for legal effect; official landing page for posting metadata; current org chart for observed units; profile/deal dates for firm evidence.
governance.noslegal_input_issues: Guide has facet-count/tab-reference inconsistencies; workbook has missing Parent cells. Do not import its hierarchy mechanically.

evidence.supporting_text: For 4 sample dates in February 2022, the Noticee had not submitted correct Margin-utilised-for-Credit-Balance-Clients (MC) data (incorrect reporting value Rs. 47.13 lakh). The Noticee admitted the error was due to a back-office issue. The AO found the Noticee violated Clause 3.2 of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95 dated 26 September 2016.
evidence.extraction_note: All twenty-eight pages source-reviewed; funding, brokerage, gross-transfer and penalty tables visually checked.

events.title: Client funding beyond permitted debit period
events.summary: Client funding beyond permitted debit period
events.position: AO finds violation in all nine sampled instances (Rs.59.69 lakh funded). Rejects service-charge/minor-debit, technical-error and cheque explanations; does not accept absence of risk as a defence. Historical margin-trading-facility exception in quoted 2017 clause is preserved, not a new order duty.

parties.name: Jainam Broking Limited (Noticee)

updates.title: Alignment of SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal with FIRE Format
updates.summary: Circular aligning SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal with the FSB's FIRE format and introducing staged (lifecycle) incident reporting for all SEBI-regulated entities, without changing the pre-existing 6-hour/24-hour reporting timelines.

events.title: Alignment of SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal with the FSB's FIRE format and introduction of staged incident-lifecycle reporting
events.summary: Changes the format and lifecycle mechanics of an existing mandatory cyber-incident reporting process; does not change who must report, or the 6-hour/24-hour reporting timelines themselves.
events.position: Regulated entities must now report cyber incidents through the same portal using the FSB's FIRE format (standardised fields, definitions and incident classification), submitting reports in stages across the incident life cycle (initial notification, intermediate updates, final closure) and taking any necessary implementation steps, including amendments to their own bye-laws, rules or regulations.

updates.title: IT Resilience Index for Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs)
updates.summary: Introduction of a system-driven IT Resilience Index (ITRI) framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions, with half-yearly computation, board reporting, an Early Warning System, service-delivery monitoring and a phased operationalisation timetable to February 28, 2027.

events.title: Introduction of the IT Resilience Index (ITRI) framework for MIIs
events.summary: A new IT Resilience Index framework is stipulated for MIIs with system-driven half-yearly computation, board reporting, an Early Warning System and service-delivery monitoring, to be fully operationalised by February 28, 2027.
events.position: MIIs must compute a system-driven ITRI measuring robustness of their Critical Systems across nine weighted parameters, on a half-yearly basis within 60 days of each half-year end, report comparative analysis and corrective actions to SCOT and the Governing Board, develop an Early Warning System, and build systems (including consolidated dashboards) giving continuous visibility into service delivery.

actions.description: MIIs shall build system-driven ITRI computation without manual intervention, an Early Warning System, and systems providing continuous visibility into service delivery to market participants including consolidated dashboards.

MIIs shall compute ITRI half-yearly within 60 days of each half-year end and submit the comparative analysis of two consecutive half-years and corrective actions to their Standing Committee on Technology and Governing Board; the first submission is for the half-year ending March 31, 2027.

MIIs shall provide insights to their Governing Boards on the overall health of IT systems, route manual-intervention exceptions through SCOT, and formulate SOPs for monitoring availability and continuity of service delivery.

effects.description: Creates the IT Resilience Index framework for MIIs, including the parameter/weightage scheme, the requirement of system-driven computation, and the requirement to build an Early Warning System and continuous service-delivery visibility systems.

Introduces new recurring obligations for MIIs to compute ITRI half-yearly within 60 days of each half-year end and to report the comparative analysis and corrective actions to their SCOT and Governing Board.

commencement.raw_text: The circular contains no express commencement clause; Section E prescribes a phased operationalisation timetable instead.

MIIs shall submit the detailed Standard Operating Procedures to SEBI after review by SCOT.

MIIs shall compute ITRI within 60 days from the end of each half-year (recurring).

timing.raw_text: within a period of 60 days from the end of each half-year
conditions: rolling / recurring obligation

timing.raw_text: the first submission of ITRI computation under this framework shall be for the half-year ending March 31, 2027
conditions: computation due within 60 days of the half-year end

transitions.rule: MIIs must move from the beta version to full operationalisation of the ITRI framework, including the Early Warning System and Real Time Monitoring of Service Delivery, by February 28, 2027.

evidence.supporting_text: IT systems of MIIs are the backbone of the securities market; MIIs must ensure availability, reliability, performance and cyber resilience of their IT systems; a framework for oversight of IT-system resilience, early identification of weaknesses and timely corrective measures has been formulated.

evidence.locator: Section B, paragraphs 4-5.2 including the ITRI parameter/weightage table
evidence.supporting_text: Pursuant to discussion with SEBI's Technical Advisory Committee and the consultation paper dated March 25, 2026, SEBI decides to create the IT Resilience Index (ITRI); a system-driven framework for computing ITRI is stipulated for MIIs; ITRI measures robustness of Critical Systems (as defined in the referenced Master Circulars) with parameters and weightages Availability 20, Security 20, Integrity 10, Governance 10, Reliability and Monitoring 10, Business Continuity 10, Modularity and Flexibility 10, Scalability 5, Others 5 (total 100).
The Industry Standards Forum (ISF) of MIIs constituted by SEBI shall finalize sub-parameters and detailed measurement criteria for each ITRI parameter by November 30, 2026.

MIIs shall compute ITRI on a half-yearly basis within a period of 60 days from the end of each half-year and submit the comparative analysis of two consecutive half-years and corrective actions taken or proposed to their Standing Committee on Technology (SCOT) and the Governing Board; computation of ITRI shall be system-driven without manual intervention, and any exception requiring manual retrieval requires prior discussion with SCOT.

The ISF shall formulate baseline parameters, acceptable threshold scores and the SOP for calculating ITRI with an objective system-driven scoring methodology for comparability across MIIs; the framework functions as a self-operating model requiring MIIs to periodically compute ITRI and provide insights to their Governing Boards.
MIIs shall develop an Early Warning System to detect possible deterioration in any ITRI parameter leading to possible performance issues and a framework to remedy these.

In addition to existing continuous performance monitoring, MIIs shall build systems providing continuous visibility into service delivery to market participants, including consolidated dashboards, and shall formulate SOPs to monitor availability of systems and continuity of service delivery and flag any disruption or deviation.

Implementation timeline: MIIs have already implemented the beta version of the ITRI framework; MIIs shall operationalize the ITRI framework including the Early Warning System and Real Time Monitoring of Service Delivery by February 28, 2027; the detailed SOP after finalization of sub-parameters by ISF shall be submitted to SEBI after review by SCOT by January 31, 2027; the first submission of ITRI computation shall be for the half-year ending March 31, 2027.

MIIs are required to take necessary steps to put in place systems for implementation, including necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations, if any; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992.

updates.title: Framework for Calculation of Net Distributable Cash Flows for InvITs
updates.summary: SEBI amends the InvIT NDCF framework (Section F, Para 3.19 of Chapter 3 of the InvIT Master Circular) to allow add-back and distribution of major maintenance expense for road projects funded by external debt, subject to per-project unitholder approval (Regulation 22(5)), explanatory-statement disclosures, a statutory auditor certificate and periodic borrowing disclosures; effective immediately.

actions.description: Revise the NDCF computation at HoldCo/SPV level and Trust level to include the new add-back line item for debt-funded major maintenance expense for road projects, subject to Note 12.

Obtain unitholder approval under Regulation 22(5) of the InvIT Regulations (at least sixty per cent of votes cast in favour) for each project before adding back debt-funded major-maintenance payments; approval may be one-time or per specific expense, with fresh approval required for deviations prior to availing the debt.

Include in the explanatory statement to the unitholder-meeting notice the prescribed disclosures: project/SPV/HoldCo details, expense categories, year-wise and project-wise estimates per the latest valuation report, growth-impact disclaimer, present and future distribution impact, and funding alternatives.

Statutory auditor to certify that the major maintenance expenses are in line with the concession-agreement obligations and requirements and that the payments are funded by external borrowings; only auditor-certified payments may be added back for NDCF calculation (the auditor may rely on an independent expert).

Disclose in the financial results and the Annual, Half-yearly and Quarterly Reports: the Net Borrowing Ratio (Chapter 4) segregating major-maintenance borrowing, the NDCF-statement notes on major-maintenance borrowing raised and outstanding per project/SPV/HoldCo and the InvIT, and the debt maturity profile segregating major-maintenance borrowing.
Recognised stock exchanges to disseminate the contents of the circular on their websites.

evidence.supporting_text: Section F (Para 3.19) titled 'Framework for calculation of Net Distributable Cash Flows (NDCFs)' of Chapter 3 of the Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) dated July 11, 2025 provides the framework for computation of NDCF for SPV/Holdco and InvIT.

On a request from an industry association to review the NDCF computation to allow addition of debt-funded major maintenance expenses, and based on recommendations of the Hybrid Securities Advisory Committee (HySAC) and public consultation, the following changes are made in Section F (Para 3.19) of Chapter 3 of the Master Circular for InvITs.

Under Para 3.19, in Table S.No. (I.) 'Computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow at HoldCo/SPV Level', a new line item is added to allow add back of payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt (shown as '(+) Payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external borrowing subject to Note 12 below').

Under Para 3.19, in Table S.No. (II.) 'Computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow at Trust Level', the same new line item is added to allow add back of payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt, subject to Note 12.

In S. No. (III.) 'Notes/Other Rules', Note No. 4 and Note No. 6 are substituted. Note 4 deals with surplus cash available in InvITs/HoldCos/SPVs (10% withheld NDCF; surplus in a newly acquired HoldCo/SPV; any other reason excluding surplus due to a debt raise) and provides that surplus cash on account of payments made for major maintenance expenditure for road projects to the extent funded by external debt may be distributed subject to the conditions in Note 12 and adequate disclosures. Substituted Note 6 provides that no Trust or SPV can distribute any cash flows by obtaining external debt, except to the extent clarified in Notes 2, 7 and 12 (excluding working capital / OD facilities obtained for treasury / working-capital purposes and squared off within the quarter).

A new Note 12 is added: any payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt shall be added back subject to conditions - (i) 'Road Project' means a project in the 'Roads and bridges' infrastructure sub-sector as per the Ministry of Finance notification dated September 19, 2025 (including amendments/additions); (ii) 'Major maintenance expense' means non-routine maintenance expenditure on a road project in accordance with the obligations and requirements specified in the concession agreement; (iii) unitholder approval pursuant to Regulation 22(5) of the InvIT Regulations (votes cast in favour at least sixty per cent of total votes cast) shall be undertaken before adding back payments made for major maintenance expense for road projects funded by external borrowing, for each Project (whether held at InvIT or SPV/HoldCo level) for which the investment manager proposes to raise borrowing.

The explanatory statement to the notice convening the unitholder meeting shall disclose: (a) names and details of the projects/SPVs/Holdcos for which the major-maintenance debt is proposed or already raised (may be raised at Trust or SPV/HoldCo level); (b) categories of expenses treated as major maintenance; (c) indicative year-wise and project-wise estimates of the major-maintenance expenses per the latest valuation report; (d) possible impact on future growth potential of the InvIT (with a suggested disclaimer); (e) present and future impact on distributions to unitholders; (f) other funding alternatives if debt is not available in future.

(v) The unitholder approval may be taken on a one-time basis (for debt already availed or proposed for the entire project life cycle) or for a specific major maintenance expense; any deviation requiring additional debt from the previously approved proposal requires unitholder approval prior to availing the debt. (vi) A certificate of the statutory auditor shall be obtained certifying that the major maintenance expenses incurred are in line with the obligations and requirements stated under the concession agreements and that payments for such expenses are funded by external borrowings; only such auditor-certified payments will be allowed to be added back for NDCF calculation; the statutory auditor may rely on an independent expert.

(vii) Disclosures to be made as part of the financial results and the Annual, Half-yearly and Quarterly Reports of the InvIT: the Net Borrowing Ratio under Chapter 4 shall segregate the amount and percentage of borrowing taken for major maintenance expenses; the notes to the NDCF statement shall disclose, for each project/SPV/HoldCo and the InvIT, the aggregate borrowing raised in the period for major maintenance and the aggregate outstanding debt for major maintenance as on the date. (viii) The debt maturity profile required under the InvIT Regulations shall specifically segregate and highlight borrowing taken for major maintenance expenses.
This circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

OBPPs offering IFSCA-regulated products shall do so in the manner specified for SEBI-registered stock brokers operating within GIFT-IFSC and in compliance with FEMA, 1999, including Overseas Investment Rules and Liberalised Remittance Scheme limits.

Attaches new conduct and disclosure conditions to the added product categories (grievance-redressal mechanism, IFSCA-product FEMA/LRS compliance and labelling, 54EC-bond disclaimers and feature/purpose disclosures).

commencement.raw_text: The circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI's November 09, 2022 notification prescribed the OBPP framework under Regulation 51A of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021, further streamlined by subsequent circulars; based on stakeholder suggestions, this circular modifies Chapter XXI of the NCS Master Circular dated October 15, 2025 to permit OBPPs to offer IFSCA-regulated products/securities/services, to permit offering of bonds issued under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 or section 85 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and to change compliance-officer requirements for OBPPs.

Clause 5.2 of the NCS Master Circular is modified so that the permissible list for OBPP platforms includes, in addition to existing items, products/securities/services regulated by a financial sector regulator (SEBI, RBI, IRDAI, IFSCA or PFRDA) and bonds issued under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 or section 85 of the Income-tax Act, 2025; for financial-sector-regulator products they may be offered under a separate tab or other platform, are governed by that regulator's directions, require an OBPP-specified grievance-redressal mechanism, and for IFSCA products must be offered in the manner specified for SEBI-registered stock brokers operating within GIFT-IFSC in compliance with FEMA (including Overseas Investment Rules and LRS limits) and clearly labelled as international/overseas instruments; for 54EC bonds the OBPP must give a disclaimer that grievance redressal lies with the issuer and not SEBI, disclose the features (eligible issuers, lock-in, investment limit, non-transferability, tax features, application size, LODR listing-requirement exemption) and prominently disclose that the instruments are intended for investors seeking the associated tax benefits.

All other provisions of the NCS Master Circular remain unchanged; the circular shall come into force with immediate effect; the Stock Exchanges are directed to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations and bring the circular to the notice of stock brokers; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 55(1) of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021; issued by the General Manager, Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities, SEBI.

updates.title: Review of Inclusion of Historical Scenarios in Stress Testing for Commodity Derivatives Segment
updates.summary: Amendment to Part A (Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O of the Master Circular for the Commodity Derivatives Segment, reducing the stress-testing Z-score threshold from 10 to 5 for peak-historical-return scenarios, effective immediately.

events.title: Reduction of the stress-testing Z-score threshold from 10 to 5 (commodity derivatives)
events.summary: The Z-score threshold used to cap extreme price movements in peak-historical-return stress testing for commodity derivatives is reduced from 10 to 5.
events.position: Price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities; mean and sigma of returns over the applicable MPOR period across 15 years are still used for the Z-score calculation.

parties.name: Recognised Clearing Corporations having a Commodity Derivatives Segment
parties.scope: Clearing corporations that conduct standardized stress testing for their Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in the commodity derivatives segment and must apply the revised Z-score threshold.

actions.description: Clearing corporations having a commodity derivatives segment shall apply a Z-score of 5 (instead of 10) when capping extreme price movements in peak-historical-return standardized stress testing for the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund.

effects.description: Amends Part A (Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O of the Master Circular for the Commodity Derivatives Segment, replacing the Z-score threshold of 10 with 5 for capping extreme price movements in peak historical returns.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the Z-score value in Part A of paragraph 22 of Annexure O is changed; the mean-and-sigma methodology and the 15-year MPOR window are unchanged.

effects.description: Lowers the Z-score cap applied in peak-historical-return stress testing, reducing the severity of the historical stress scenario, stated to be for the objective of facilitating Ease of Doing Business.

commencement.raw_text: The circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

evidence.supporting_text: The SEBI Master Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/136 for Commodity Derivatives Segment dated August 04, 2023 prescribes Core Settlement Guarantee Fund norms; paragraph 22 of Annexure O, Part A (Historical Scenarios, Peak Historical Return) currently provides that price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 10 will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities.

Based on stakeholder representations, the recommendation of the Risk Management Review Committee and public comments, and with the objective of facilitating Ease of Doing Business, SEBI modifies Part A (with respect to Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O so that price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 (instead of 10) will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities.

The circular shall come into force with immediate effect; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018, and with the approval of the competent authority.

updates.title: Amendment to SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) Regulations, 2015 (“ILMDS Regulations”)
updates.summary: Circular specifying face-value denominations for privately placed municipal debt securities, inserting a two-step escrow account mechanism and permitted credit enhancement for pooled finance vehicle/SPV issuers, and relaxing financial-results submission timelines, under the ILMDS Regulations framework.

events.title: Specification of face value denominations for privately placed municipal debt securities under Regulation 22 of the ILMDS Regulations
events.summary: Specifies permitted private municipal-debt denominations and conditions under regulation 22; no claim is made that no earlier specification existed.
events.position: Privately placed municipal debt securities must have a face value of Rs. 1,00,000 or Rs. 10,000; a Rs. 10,000-denomination security must have fixed maturity and no structured obligations; and the exchange-traded lot must equal the security's face value.

Subject: Amendment to SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) Regulations, 2015 ('ILMDS Regulations').

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI constituted a Working Group in August 2024 on the regulatory framework for municipal debt securities. Further changes to the extant framework in respect of certain operational aspects are being specified through this circular.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Paragraph 2 (face value of municipal debt securities)
evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 22 of the ILMDS Regulations requires face value to be disclosed 'in the manner as specified by the Board'. events.title: Insertion of a two-step escrow account mechanism and permitted credit-enhancement structures for pooled finance vehicle/SPV municipal debt issuers
events.summary: Inserts two-step pooled-finance escrow and optional credit-enhancement provisions into the identified 2019 circular.
events.position: Constituent municipalities of a pooled finance vehicle/SPV must create the prescribed escrow accounts; the SPV must itself maintain an Interest payment account (funded to one year's interest obligation) and a Sinking fund account fed by the constituent municipalities' corresponding accounts; and the SPV may adopt specified credit-enhancement structures.

parties.name: Pooled finance vehicle / Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) issuers of municipal debt securities
parties.scope: SPVs/pooled finance vehicles set up under the Government's Pooled Finance Development Fund Scheme, which must maintain the new Interest payment account and Sinking fund account and may adopt specified credit-enhancement structures.

parties.name: Constituent municipalities of a pooled finance vehicle/SPV
parties.scope: Municipalities constituting the pooled finance vehicle, each required to create the escrow-related accounts and comply with the applicable requirements, and to transfer funds to the SPV's accounts per their inter-se agreement.

actions.description: Create and maintain the prescribed escrow-related accounts and comply with the applicable requirements as a constituent municipality of a pooled finance vehicle/SPV.

Maintain an Interest payment account (funded at all times to one year's interest obligation on the municipal debt securities) and a Sinking fund account, funded by transfers from the constituent municipalities' corresponding accounts.

Optionally adopt one or more specified forms of credit enhancement (additional cash collateral, state-government program equity, access to state finance commission devolutions, DFI/multilateral credit guarantee, or another appropriate structure) to enhance credit rating and investor protection.

effects.description: Inserts new paragraphs 4.1.5 and 4.1.6 into SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/CIR/P/134/2019, after paragraph 4.1.4.
target_provisions: Paragraph 4.1.4 (insertion point for new paragraphs 4.1.5 and 4.1.6)

effects.description: Adds substantive duties on pooled finance vehicle/SPV municipal debt issuers and their constituent municipalities to create and maintain a two-step escrow account structure (including a one-year interest-obligation reserve in the SPV's Interest payment account), and permits (without mandating) specified forms of credit enhancement.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall be applicable with immediate effect.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/CIR/P/134/2019 dated November 13, 2019 (the 'Circular') specifies the escrow payment mechanism for municipal debt issuers. New paragraphs 4.1.5 and 4.1.6 are inserted into the Circular after paragraph 4.1.4.

evidence.supporting_text: New paragraph 4.1.5: where the listed entity is a pooled finance vehicle/SPV under the Pooled Finance Development Fund Scheme, the constituent municipalities must create all the escrow-related accounts and comply with the applicable requirements. The SPV/pooled finance vehicle must additionally maintain its own 'Interest payment account' and 'Sinking fund account', funded by transfers from the constituent municipalities' corresponding accounts per their inter-se agreement, and must maintain an amount equal to one year's interest obligation in its Interest payment account throughout the securities' tenure.

events.title: Relaxation of timelines for submission of half-yearly unaudited and annual audited financial results by municipal debt issuers
events.summary: Lengthens two existing periodic financial-reporting deadlines for listed municipal debt issuers, citing the practical challenges municipalities face in data collection, interdepartmental coordination and meeting disclosure requirements.
events.position: Listed municipal debt issuers must submit half-yearly unaudited financial results within 60 days of the half-year end, and annual audited financial results within 90 days of the financial year end.

parties.name: Listed municipal debt security issuers (municipalities)
parties.scope: Municipalities that have listed municipal debt securities, who must submit half-yearly unaudited and annual audited financial results to the stock exchange within the relaxed timelines.

actions.description: Prepare and submit first-half-year unaudited results as soon as available, and in any event within sixty days of the first half-year end; submit annual audited results with audit report within ninety days of financial-year end.

effects.description: Amends paragraphs 2.1.1(a) and 2.1.2(a) of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/CIR/P/134/2019 to substitute longer submission timelines for half-yearly unaudited and annual audited financial results.

Extends the half-yearly unaudited financial-results submission deadline from 45 to 60 days after the half-year end, and the annual audited financial-results submission deadline from 60 to 90 days after the financial year end.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall be applicable with immediate effect.

deadlines.obligation: Prepare and submit first-half-year unaudited financial results as soon as available, no later than the specified outer period.

timing.raw_text: within sixty days of the end of the first half year
timing.anchor_event: End of the first half year
conditions: As soon as the results are available, subject to the sixty-day outer limit.

deadlines.obligation: Submit annual audited financial results, with audit report, to the stock exchange.

timing.raw_text: within ninety days from the end of the financial year

evidence.supporting_text: The 2019 Circular's paragraphs 2.1.1(a) and 2.1.2(a) previously required listed municipal-debt entities to submit half-yearly unaudited financial results within 45 days of the end of the first half-year, and annual audited financial results (with audit report) within 60 days of the financial year end. Considering the practical challenges municipalities face in data collection, interdepartmental coordination and meeting disclosure requirements, these timelines are relaxed: first-half-year unaudited results must now be prepared and submitted as soon as available, within 60 days of the end of the first half year, and annual audited results within 90 days of the financial year end.

updates.title: Consultation Paper on FPI Participation in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives (ETCDs)
updates.summary: Consultation paper (with attached draft circular) proposing to permit FPI participation in non-agricultural index derivatives and in non-cash (physically) settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, subject to a compulsory pre-tender-period square-off/transfer safeguard mechanism; comments due 1 September 2026.

evidence.supporting_text: FPI participation has boosted crude oil/natural gas options liquidity. Internationally (Japan OSE/TOCOM, China QFIs, US CME, EU ICE) foreign investors trade physically settled commodity derivatives with delivery-capacity safeguards. In India FPIs cannot take/make delivery (no permanent establishment; GST-registration burden even via a delegated TM), so SEBI proposes permitting non-cash based non-agri derivative trading conditional on FPIs squaring off/rolling over before the tender period.

evidence.supporting_text: FPIs may take positions in non-cash non-agri commodity derivatives, compulsorily squaring off/rolling over by T-3 (close of market hours); if not done voluntarily by T-1, the position devolves automatically post-close on T-1 to the designated TM/TCM's proprietary account at Closing/Daily Settlement Price via a pre-agreed tripartite (FPI-PCM-TM) or bipartite (FPI-TCM) agreement, treated as a Normal Market trade (attracting SEBI turnover fees, CTT, stamp duty, GST); PCM informs the TM of the open position by T-2 EOD for margin arrangement; no fresh FPI position increase is allowed on T-1 in the near-month contract; the TM/TCM gets up to T+2 trading days to reduce any resulting position-limit breach; a Proprietary Risk Absorption Charge, disclosed at onboarding, may be levied on the FPI for the involuntary transfer, without prejudice to other position-limit penalties.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

updates.title: Certification Requirements for Distribution of Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs)
updates.summary: Circular amending paragraph 21.10 of the MF Master Circular: introduces a new NISM Series-V-D certification for SIF distribution (also covering MF distribution), sunsets the prior NISM Series XIII requirement for SIF distribution after 21 September 2026 subject to a transitional savings provision, leaves the MF-only NISM Series V-A requirement unchanged, and assigns AMFI/AMCs a distributor-compliance-ensuring duty; effective immediately.

events.title: Revision of MF Master Circular paragraph 21.10: new NISM Series-V-D certification for SIF distribution, sunset of NISM Series XIII requirement with transitional savings
events.summary: Replaces the SIF-distribution certification pathway (previously 'NISM Series XIII') with a dedicated 'NISM Series-V-D' certification that also covers MF distribution, while leaving the MF-only 'NISM Series V-A' pathway unchanged and providing a cohort-specific transition for existing NISM Series XIII holders.
events.position: SIF distribution now requires a dedicated 'NISM Series-V-D' certification (which also covers MF distribution); the NISM Series XIII pathway for SIF distribution ceases to apply after 21 September 2026, subject to a savings provision for existing valid Series XIII holders until their certification's expiry; MF-only distribution continues to require NISM Series V-A, unchanged.

parties.name: Persons/entities distributing SIF and/or Mutual Fund products (distributors and agents)
parties.scope: The direct subject of the certification requirement: persons/entities employed or engaged in the sale/distribution of SIF products (new NISM Series-V-D requirement) and, separately, those distributing only Mutual Fund products (continuing NISM Series V-A requirement, unchanged).

parties.name: Asset Management Companies (AMCs)
parties.scope: Explicitly assigned a duty (with AMFI) to ensure compliance with the certification requirements by distributors and agents (paragraph 21.10.5).

parties.name: Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
parties.scope: Industry self-regulatory association explicitly assigned (with AMCs) a duty to ensure compliance with the certification requirements by distributors and agents (paragraph 21.10.5). No entity_type or role tag in the v1.1 taxonomy corresponds to a mutual-fund self-regulatory/industry association; left untagged rather than forcing an ill-fitting tag (see uncertainty U001).

actions.description: Hold valid NISM Series-V-D for SIF distribution, subject to paragraph 21.10.4: qualifying valid Series XIII obtained on/before 21 September 2026 remains usable until its expiry with continuing valid Series V-A.
Continue to hold a valid 'NISM Series V-A - Mutual Fund Distributors Certification' where distributing only Mutual Fund products (unchanged requirement).
Ensure compliance with the revised certification requirements by distributors and agents.
Distributors relying on grandfathered valid Series XIII obtained on/before 21 September 2026 must continue to hold valid Series V-A during the saved period until their Series XIII expiry.

effects.description: Modifies paragraph 21.10 of the MF Master Circular dated 20 March 2026, restating the certification requirements for SIF/MF distribution.

Introduces a new mandatory 'NISM Series-V-D - Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors Certification' for any person distributing SIF products, which also qualifies the holder to distribute Mutual Fund products without separately holding NISM Series V-A.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Subject to paragraph 21.10.4: qualifying Series XIII holders are exempt from Series-V-D until their existing certificate expires and must keep valid Series V-A during that period.

effects.description: Removes the prior requirement of holding 'NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification' for SIF distribution, effective after 21 September 2026, subject to the transitional savings provision for existing valid certificate holders.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Paragraph 21.10.4 preserves the position of distributors holding a valid NISM Series XIII certification obtained on or before 21 September 2026 until that certification's own expiry.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

transitions.rule: Not required to obtain the 'NISM Series-V-D' certification until expiry of their existing NISM Series XIII certification, provided they continue to hold a valid 'NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors Certification' during that period.

updates.title: Operationalisation of freezing of holdings of promoter and promoter group including their associates (promoter holdings) at the ISIN level under Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018
updates.summary: Operational framework and system enhancements by depositories to give effect to the ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during buy-backs under Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the Buy-back Regulations, with compliance duties on listed companies, exchanges, merchant bankers and RTAs.

events.title: Operational framework for the ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during buy-back
events.summary: The depositories must build and operate an ISIN-level freeze mechanism for promoter holdings during buy-backs, and market participants must comply with it.
events.position: Depositories must establish an operational framework and system enhancements to freeze promoter and promoter-group holdings at ISIN level from the buy-back resolution date until closing of the offer, with defined carve-outs, and issue operational guidelines; listed companies issue freezing instructions in a prescribed format; exchanges, merchant bankers and RTAs ensure compliance.

parties.name: All Listed Companies undertaking buy-back
parties.scope: Listed companies must issue freezing instructions to depositories in the prescribed format and ensure compliance with the operational framework.

parties.name: All Depositories
parties.scope: Depositories must build the operational framework and system enhancements for the ISIN-level freeze and issue operational guidelines / communiques.

parties.name: Recognised Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Stock exchanges are addressees required to ensure compliance with the circular and the depositories' operational framework.

parties.name: Registered Merchant Bankers
parties.scope: Merchant bankers managing the buy-back are required to ensure compliance with the circular and the operational framework.

parties.name: Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
parties.scope: RTAs are required to ensure compliance with the circular and the operational framework issued by the depositories.

parties.name: Promoter and promoter group (including associates) of the company undertaking buy-back
parties.scope: Promoter holdings are frozen at ISIN level from the resolution date until closing of the offer, subject to the tender-offer and encumbrance-invocation carve-outs.

actions.description: Depositories shall put in place the operational framework and necessary system enhancements for the ISIN-level freeze and issue the necessary operational guidelines / communiques.
Listed companies shall issue instructions to the depositories for freezing of promoter holdings in the format provided in the operational framework.
Listed companies, recognised stock exchanges, depositories, merchant bankers and RTAs shall ensure compliance with this circular and with the operational framework issued by the depositories.

effects.description: Operationalises Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the Buy-back Regulations by directing the depositories to establish the operational framework and system enhancements needed to give effect to the ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Freeze does not apply to shares tendered in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of pre-buy-back encumbrances is allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to Board-specified conditions.

effects.description: Sets the procedural content the depositories' operational framework must cover: freezing-instruction format for listed companies, ISIN-level freeze modalities, tender-offer tendering, encumbrance invocation/release, and other operational and system requirements.

commencement.raw_text: This Circular shall come into force with immediate effect from date of issuance of this circular.

deadlines.obligation: The Depositories shall ensure the operational framework and the necessary system enhancements are put in place.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI by notification dated July 01, 2026 amended the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 inserting Regulation 24(i)(ea), under which promoter holdings shall remain frozen at ISIN level from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till closing of the offer, while permitting tendering of shares in a tender-offer buy-back and invocation of encumbrances created prior to the commencement of the buy-back period.

To operationalise the amendment, the Depositories shall put in place an operational framework including necessary system enhancements and issue operational guidelines / communiques; the framework shall provide for the format of freezing instructions by listed companies, operational modalities for the ISIN-level freeze, for permitting tendering in tender-offer buy-backs, for permitting invocation or release of pre-buy-back encumbrances with the freeze continuing on invoked/released securities, and any other necessary operational procedures or system requirements.
The Depositories shall ensure that the operational framework and the necessary system enhancements are put in place before August 01, 2026.

Listed Companies, Recognised Stock Exchanges, Depositories, Merchant Bankers and Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents shall ensure compliance with this circular and the operational framework issued by the Depositories.

This circular shall come into force with immediate effect from the date of issuance of this circular; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Section 26(3) of the Depositories Act, 1996.

updates.title: Intraday borrowing facility availed by mutual funds
updates.summary: Conditions governing intraday borrowings by mutual funds - permitted purposes, quantum limits, AMC repayment responsibility, mandatory board-approved policy, record keeping and cost allocation - effective September 1, 2026.

events.title: Conditions for intraday borrowing by mutual funds
events.summary: Mutual funds may now avail intraday borrowings for specified purposes subject to quantum limits and AMC controls, replacing the earlier borrowing guidance.
events.position: Intraday borrowings are permitted for unitholder pay-outs, scheme pay-in, MTM/forex settlement and repayment of existing borrowings, limited to guaranteed and sighted non-guaranteed receivables; AMCs must ensure end-of-day repayment, obtain board approval for a published policy, keep scheme-wise records, and bear the cost and any shortfall.

parties.name: All Mutual Funds
parties.scope: Mutual funds permitted to avail intraday borrowings for the specified purposes and subject to the quantum limits.

parties.name: Asset Management Companies
parties.scope: AMCs bear responsibility for end-of-day repayment, regulatory-limit compliance, policy implementation, scheme-wise record keeping and the cost of borrowing and of any shortfall.

parties.name: Trustee Companies / Boards of Trustees of Mutual Funds
parties.scope: Boards of Trustees, together with Boards of the AMC, must approve the policy for use of the intraday borrowing facility.

actions.description: Boards of the AMC and Trustees shall approve the policy for use of the intraday borrowing facility, which shall be published on the AMC website and include approval processes and monitoring mechanism.
AMCs shall maintain scheme-wise records detailing the underlying liquidity mismatch and the expected source of repayment for each intraday borrowing.
AMCs shall ensure intraday borrowings are repaid by end of day and that any borrowing converted to overnight borrowing stays within regulatory limits and permitted purposes under Regulation 42(1).

effects.description: Supersedes the mutual fund borrowing guidelines in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated March 20, 2026 and SEBI Circular dated March 25, 2026, for intraday borrowings.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Paragraphs 11.10 and 17.7 of the Master Circular and Fourth Schedule clauses 6 and 7 continue to apply.

effects.description: Introduces conditions on the newly permitted intraday borrowing facility: permitted purposes, quantum limits, end-of-day repayment responsibility, mandatory board-approved and published policy, scheme-wise record keeping, and AMC bearing of cost and shortfall.

commencement.raw_text: This circular shall come into effect from September 1, 2026.

evidence.supporting_text: To address liquidity mismatches from differing market settlement timings, SEBI by Gazette Notification No. CG-MH-E-07072026-274229 dated July 3, 2026 amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 to permit intraday borrowings by mutual funds for purposes specified in this circular.

In supersession of the guidelines on borrowings of mutual funds specified in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated March 20, 2026 and of SEBI Circular No. HO/(92)2026-IMD-POD-2/I/7885/2026 dated March 25, 2026, intraday borrowings by mutual funds shall be subject to the conditions that follow.

Mutual Funds may avail intraday borrowings for unitholder pay-outs (redemptions, IDCW, interest), pay-in for scheme investments, MTM and forex settlement obligations, and repayment of existing borrowings; the quantum is limited to guaranteed receivables and to sighted non-guaranteed receivables to be received by end of day, with additional borrowing by AMCs solely for redemption and other unitholder pay-outs under Regulation 42(1) of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

AMCs are responsible for ensuring intraday borrowings are repaid by end of day and that any conversion to overnight borrowing stays within regulatory limits and permitted purposes under Regulation 42(1); Boards of the AMC and Trustees shall approve the policy for use of the facility, which shall be published on the AMC website and include approval processes and monitoring mechanism; AMCs shall maintain scheme-wise records of the underlying liquidity mismatch and expected source of repayment.

AMCs shall ensure compliance with clauses 6 and 7 of the Fourth Schedule of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 and para 17.7 of the Master Circular; in line with para 11.10 of the Master Circular the cost of intraday borrowing, and any loss or cost from an unforeseen event or delay in receiving funds from receivables, shall be borne by the AMC.

This circular shall come into effect from September 1, 2026; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 42(2) and Regulation 84 of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

events.title: Revised IPF contribution and interest/income utilization norms for depositories
events.summary: Depositories must plough back at least 95% (not 100%) of IPF interest/income and may use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses.
events.position: At least 95% of the interest or income received every year from IPF investments shall be contributed to the IPF; at least 95% of interest or income from IPF received every year shall be ploughed back to the IPF; a maximum of 5% may be utilized during the financial year for dedicated IPF Trust employees' expenses and other administrative and statutory expenses (taxes, audit fees, charity commissioner's fee), with excess expenses borne by the depository and non-utilised amounts ploughed back.

topics.name: Use and monitoring of issue proceeds

parties.name: All Depositories
parties.scope: Depositories must contribute at least 95% of IPF investment income to the IPF, plough back at least 95% of interest/income received, and may use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses, bearing any excess.

actions.description: Depositories shall contribute at least 95% of annual IPF investment income to the IPF, plough back at least 95% of interest/income received, restrict utilisation for specified expenses to a maximum of 5%, bear any excess expenses and plough back unutilised amounts.
Depositories shall take necessary steps and put in place necessary systems for implementation and make necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations wherever applicable.

effects.description: Amends clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 of the December 03, 2024 Master Circular for Depositories with revised contribution and utilisation norms for IPF interest and income.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the two identified clauses are modified; the balance of paragraph 4.46 and the Master Circular is unaffected.

effects.description: Replaces the requirement that 100% of IPF interest or income be treated as corpus with a requirement to plough back at least 95% and a permission to use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses.

commencement.raw_text: Applicability: The provisions of the circular shall be applicable with effect from September 01, 2026.

evidence.supporting_text: Paragraph 4.46 of Section 4 of SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/168 for Depositories dated December 03, 2024 prescribes comprehensive IPF guidelines; paragraph 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) currently provides that, to strengthen the corpus, 100% of interest or income from the IPF shall be treated as corpus of the IPF.

Following SMAC recommendations, public consultation comments and internal deliberations, and to bring uniformity with stock exchanges, clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 of the December 03, 2024 Master Circular for Depositories are modified: under Contribution to IPF, at least 95% of the interest or income received every year from IPF investments shall be contributed to the IPF; under Utilization, at least 95% of interest or income from IPF received every year shall be ploughed back to the IPF, and a maximum of 5% of such interest or income may be utilized for expenses of dedicated IPF Trust employees and other administrative and statutory expenses (taxes, audit fees, charity commissioner's fee) during the financial year, with excess expenses borne by the depository and unutilised amounts ploughed back.

Applicability: the provisions of the circular shall be applicable with effect from September 01, 2026; the MIIs are directed to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations wherever applicable and bring the circular to the notice of market participants.

updates.title: Handling of Client’s Unpaid Securities by Trading Members
updates.summary: SEBI amends Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers, replacing the framework for handling clients' unpaid securities with a CUSPA-based auto-pledge regime (46.1-46.11) and an exceptional-circumstances pledge-extension mechanism (46.12-46.14), with staggered commencement.

topics.name: Protection of client money and securities

events.title: Revised Paragraph 46.1-46.11: CUSPA auto-pledge framework for clients' unpaid securities
events.summary: Paragraph 46.1-46.11 is replaced with a CUSPA-based auto-pledge regime for clients' unpaid securities, with new client-communication, policy, daily pledge-value, invocation and depository auto-release mechanics and a re-pledging prohibition.
events.position: Revised Paragraph 46.1-46.11 as set out in Paragraph 3 of the circular, built around the client unpaid securities pledgee account (CUSPA).

actions.description: Open a client unpaid securities pledgee account (CUSPA) and implement pay-out of unpaid securities to the client's demat account followed by auto-pledge (without specific client instruction) with reason 'unpaid' in favour of CUSPA.
After pledge creation, send the client an email/SMS informing of the funds obligation and the TM's right to sell the securities on the client's failure to meet the obligation.

Formulate and maintain a policy (standalone or within the Risk Management Policy) for handling unpaid securities, communicate it to all clients before implementation, and include processes, reasons, manner and timing for invocation/release and liquidation and a maximum client payment window not exceeding five trading days from pay-out.

On a daily basis determine the maximum value of securities that may remain pledged per the exchanges' operational guidelines and release the pledge on any excess quantity on or before the next trading day; do not allow the client exposure on the basis of CUSPA-pledged unpaid securities.

On client default within the prescribed timeline, invoke the pledge per the policy and liquidate the unpaid securities after reasonable prior notice, sell using the client's Unique Client Code, and credit any surplus after settling the obligation to the client's ledger.

Verify early-pay-in block details against the client-level obligation on invocation, and automatically release the CUSPA pledge at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out where it is neither invoked nor released within five trading days.

Issue operational guidelines for implementation within 30 days of the circular in consultation with depositories, disseminate the circular to members/participants and on websites, and amend the relevant Bye-laws, Rules and Regulations.

effects.description: Amends Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers dated 17 June 2025 by substituting revised sub-paragraphs 46.1 to 46.11 for the handling of clients' unpaid securities.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Amendment is only to the extent of Paragraph 3 of the circular; all other Master Circular provisions continue to apply.

effects.description: Sets the end-to-end procedure for pay-out, auto-pledge to CUSPA, client communication, TM policy, daily maximum-pledge-value determination and excess release, invocation and liquidation, depository verification, and automatic release at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out.

Introduces the requirement to open a dedicated CUSPA account, to auto-pledge with reason 'unpaid', to maintain and pre-communicate a handling policy with a five-trading-day maximum client payment window, and prohibits pledging/transferring CUSPA securities to Banks/NBFCs for raising funds.

evidence.supporting_text: Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers dated June 17, 2025 specifies provisions on Handling of Client's Securities by Trading Members (TM)/Clearing Members (CM); these provisions were introduced vide SEBI Circular Nos. CIR/HO/MIRSD/DOP/CIR/P/2019/75 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/153 dated June 20, 2019 and November 11, 2022; since then there have been regulatory developments such as mandatory pay-out of securities directly to clients' demat accounts and changes in market practice.
In order to enhance ease of doing business for stockbrokers and ease of investing for clients, it has been decided to amend Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular as under.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.1-46.2 (Creation of pledge for unpaid securities)
evidence.supporting_text: For trades not under margin trading facility, pay-out of unpaid securities is made directly to the client's demat account followed by creation of an auto-pledge (without specific client instruction) with reason 'unpaid' in favour of a 'client unpaid securities pledgee account (CUSPA)' opened by the TM; after pledge creation the TM must send an email/SMS informing the client of the funds obligation and the TM's right to sell the securities on the client's failure to meet the obligation.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.3-46.5 (Policy by TM for handling unpaid securities)
evidence.supporting_text: The TM must formulate and maintain a policy (standalone or part of its Risk Management Policy) for handling unpaid securities and communicate it to all clients prior to implementation; the policy must set out processes, reasons, manner and timing for invocation/release of pledge and liquidation, and must specify the maximum period - not exceeding five trading days from the pay-out date - within which the client must meet the payment obligation; while CUSPA-pledged unpaid securities may be counted for reporting client margin collection to the Clearing Corporation, the TM must not allow the client exposure on the basis of such securities.

During the period the client's funds obligation continues, the TM must, on a daily basis, determine the maximum value of securities that may remain pledged per the exchanges' operational guidelines (based on ledger balance, overall margin obligations or other specified factors); if the value of pledged securities exceeds this maximum, the TM must release the pledge on the excess quantity on or before the next trading day.

If the client fails to meet the payment obligation within the prescribed timeline, the TM must, per its policy, invoke the pledge and liquidate the unpaid securities after giving the client reasonable notice; on invocation the securities are blocked for early pay-in in the client's demat account with a trail in the TM's CUSPA account, the depositories verify the block details against the client-level obligation, the securities are sold with the client's Unique Client Code, and any surplus after settling the obligation is credited to the client's ledger.

If the pledge on unpaid securities is neither invoked nor released within five trading days after pay-out, the depositories automatically release it at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out and the securities become free balance for the client; the TM may request release any time before auto-release.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.11 (Prohibition on further pledging/transferring CUSPA securities)
evidence.supporting_text: Securities pledged in favour of the TM's CUSPA must not be pledged or transferred to Banks/NBFCs for raising funds.
Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular stands amended to the extent of Paragraph 3 as detailed above; all other provisions specified in the Master Circular continue to remain applicable.
Stock exchanges must issue operational guidelines for implementation of the provisions of this circular, in consultation with depositories, within 30 days from the date of issuance of this circular.
The amended provisions of Paragraph 46.1 to 46.11 of the Master Circular come into force with effect from three months from the date of issuance of operational guidelines by stock exchanges.

Stock exchanges/depositories are directed to bring the circular to the notice of their members/participants and disseminate it on their websites, make necessary amendments to relevant Bye-laws, Rules and Regulations, and have in place appropriate systems and arrangements to effect the provisions.

evidence.supporting_text: Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers dated June 17, 2025 specifies provisions on Handling of Client's Securities by Trading Members (TM)/Clearing Members (CM); these provisions were introduced vide SEBI Circular Nos. CIR/HO/MIRSD/DOP/CIR/P/2019/75 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/153 dated June 20, 2019 and November 11, 2022; since then there have been regulatory developments such as mandatory pay-out of securities directly to clients' demat accounts and changes in market practice.
In order to enhance ease of doing business for stockbrokers and ease of investing for clients, it has been decided to amend Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular as under.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.12 (Extension of pledge in exceptional circumstances)
evidence.supporting_text: In exceptional circumstances where the unpaid pledged securities cannot be liquidated within 5 trading days after pay-out due to (a) the security being in lower circuit with only sellers, (b) suspension or trading halt due to surveillance or other reasons, or (c) any other valid reasons recognized by MIIs including unforeseen circumstances beyond the TM's control, the TM may make a request by 6 PM on the fifth trading day after pay-out to extend the pledge by up to one additional calendar week; if the conditions continue, further extensions of similar period may be sought; once the circumstances no longer exist the TM must not seek any further extension.

On each extension of pledge the TM must send a communication to the client; failure by the TM to request a pledge extension within the stipulated timeframe results in automatic system-based release of the pledged securities.
Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular stands amended to the extent of Paragraph 3 as detailed above; all other provisions specified in the Master Circular continue to remain applicable.
The amended provisions of Paragraph 46.12 to 46.14 of the Master Circular come into force with effect from six months from the date of issuance of this circular.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 29(7) governs liquidation and distribution after liabilities; 29(10A) enables inoperative tagging subject to specified conditions; 29(11) requires surrender upon winding up. This circular specifies the modalities.

An AIF/scheme may retain proceeds beyond the applicable liquidation/dissolution period if at least one listed ground is satisfied. Ground 3.1 requires demonstrable litigation notice/demand, including official communications from stated authorities/court or investor/counterparty relating to potential liability; SCNs, reassessment notices and investigation summons can qualify without a crystallised demand.

The retention and inoperative-status facility also applies to VCFs registered under the erstwhile SEBI VCF Regulations 1996. Tagged legacy VCFs have the same regulatory framework described in paragraphs 12–14.

updates.title: Norms for Base Price, Price Bands, Call Auction in pre-open session and Close-out procedure for Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)
updates.summary: Revised ETF trading-mechanism norms - T-1 day Closing Price base price, category-wise dynamic/fixed price bands with cooling-off, a specific close-out procedure for Overnight/Liquid ETFs and a pre-open-session call auction for Commodity ETFs - effective September 1, 2026, with a joint Stock Exchange-AMC NAV-base-price step from April 01, 2027.

events.title: Revised ETF norms - base price, dynamic/fixed price bands, close-out procedure and Commodity ETF pre-open call auction
events.summary: ETFs move from a fixed +20% price band on a T-2 day NAV base price to a T-1 day Closing Price base price with dynamic (Equity/Debt, Commodity) or fixed (+5% Overnight/Liquid) price bands, a specific close-out procedure and a Commodity ETF pre-open call auction.
events.position: Base price is the T-1 day Closing Price (last 30-minute VWAP), with LTP and latest closing NAV fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment; Equity/Debt ETFs (other than Overnight/Liquid) have dynamic bands (initial +10%, flexed to +20% after cooling-off, 5% per flex, max two per direction, no sliding, cross-exchange); Overnight/Liquid ETFs have a fixed +5% band; Commodity ETFs have dynamic bands (initial +6%, flexed by 3%, DPL relaxation in 3% stages, no cap); Overnight/Liquid ETF close-out is the higher of the highest recorded price up to auction/close-out and 5% above the latest closing price; a pre-open-session call auction is introduced for Commodity (Gold/Silver) ETFs.

parties.name: Recognized Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Stock exchanges compute the ETF base price, operate the dynamic/fixed price bands and cooling-off, conduct the Commodity ETF pre-open call auction, apply the close-out procedure and (with AMCs) implement the T-1 day closing NAV base price by April 01, 2027.

parties.name: Recognized Clearing Corporations
parties.scope: Clearing corporations apply the ETF close-out and auction/proceeds procedures and make consequential rule amendments.

parties.name: Asset Management Companies of Mutual Funds
parties.scope: AMCs of Mutual Funds jointly with Stock Exchanges must address the operational challenges to implement use of T-1 day closing NAV as the ETF base price with effect from April 01, 2027.

actions.description: MIIs shall put in place systems to implement the revised ETF base-price, price-band, cooling-off, close-out and Commodity ETF pre-open call-auction norms and make necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations.

Stock exchanges shall determine the ETF base price as the T-1 day Closing Price (with the specified fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment) and operate the dynamic/fixed price bands and cooling-off periods per ETF category.

effects.description: Supplements and modifies the ETF-related price-band, close-out, auction and pre-open call-auction provisions of the Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations (Chapter 1 paragraphs 2.3.1, 2.5, 17.1; Chapter 3 paragraphs 2.1-2.3).
effects.savings_or_limitations: For ETFs other than Overnight/Liquid ETFs the existing Chapter 3 paragraph 2.1 close-out provisions and the existing Auction and Proceeds provisions (paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3) continue to apply.

effects.description: Sets the ETF base-price, dynamic/fixed price-band, cooling-off, cross-exchange flex, close-out and Commodity ETF pre-open call-auction procedures.

commencement.raw_text: Applicability: The provisions of the circular shall come into effect from 1st September, 2026.

deadlines.obligation: Stock Exchanges and AMCs of Mutual Funds shall jointly address the operational challenges to implement use of the T-1 day closing NAV of the ETF as the base price.

transitions.affected_cohort: All ETFs (Equity, Debt, Commodity, Overnight, Liquid)
transitions.condition: The T-1 day Closing Price is adopted as the base price 'to start with', pending resolution of operational challenges in using the T-1 day closing NAV.
transitions.rule: Stock Exchanges and AMCs must jointly implement use of the T-1 day closing NAV of the ETF as the base price with effect from April 01, 2027.

evidence.supporting_text: Paragraph 2.3.1 of Chapter 1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024 prescribes scrip-wise price bands of up to 20% for scrips without derivatives, and paragraph 2.5 prescribes dynamic price bands for scrips with derivatives; currently ETFs have a fixed price band of +20% (except +5% for Overnight ETFs) on a base price equal to T-2 day NAV; based on a Working Group and SMAC recommendations, public consultation and stakeholder discussion, revised norms are provided.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 4-7 (base price, price bands, close-out, call auction)
evidence.supporting_text: Base price for ETFs is T-1 day Closing Price (last 30-minute VWAP), with LTP and latest closing NAV fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment; Stock Exchanges and AMCs shall jointly address operational challenges to implement use of T-1 day closing NAV as base price with effect from April 01, 2027. Price bands: Equity/Debt ETFs (other than Overnight/Liquid) have dynamic bands with an initial +10% flexed up to +20% after cooling-off (15 or 5 minutes), flexed by 5% for at most two instances per direction, no sliding, cross-exchange applicability; Overnight and Liquid ETFs have a fixed +5% band; Commodity (Gold/Silver) ETFs have dynamic bands with an initial +6% flexed by 3%, with DPL relaxation in 3% stages, cooling-off, no cap and no restriction on number of flexes. Close-out for Overnight/Liquid ETFs is the higher of the highest recorded price up to the auction/close-out date and 5% above the latest available closing price; other ETFs keep the existing Chapter 3 paragraph 2.1 provisions, and existing Auction and Proceeds provisions (paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3) continue. A call auction in the pre-open session is introduced for Commodity ETFs (Gold/Silver), using the mechanism at paragraph 17.1 of Chapter 1 of the Master Circular.

Applicability: the provisions of the circular shall come into effect from 1st September, 2026; all MIIs are advised to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations and publicise the circular; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018.
