updates.title: Relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements
updates.summary: One-time relaxation from the penal provisions of the LODR compliance Master Circular for listed entities whose Minimum Public Shareholding compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026, with a direction to stock exchanges and depositories not to take penal action and to withdraw actions already initiated.

topics.name: Minimum public shareholding / minimum public offer

events.title: One-time relaxation from Master Circular penal provisions for MPS non-compliance
events.summary: Penal enforcement of MPS non-compliance under the LODR compliance Master Circular is suspended for a defined cohort and window.
events.position: For listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026, those penal provisions do not apply for non-compliance during that period, and penal actions initiated since April 1, 2026 may be withdrawn.

topics.name: Minimum public shareholding / minimum public offer

Stock exchanges shall bring the circular to the notice of all listed entities, disseminate it on their website, and make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for implementation, if necessary.

effects.description: Grants a one-time exemption from the applicability of the penal provisions of the July 11, 2023 LODR compliance Master Circular for the specified cohort of listed entities.

effects.description: Directs recognised stock exchanges and depositories not to take penal action (fines, freezing of promoter shareholding, other consequential actions) against the specified cohort during the window, and permits withdrawal of penal actions already initiated since April 1, 2026.

transitions.affected_cohort: Listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026
transitions.condition: Penal actions may already have been initiated by stock exchanges or depositories against such entities for MPS non-compliance during April 1, 2026 till the date of the circular.
transitions.rule: Such already-initiated penal actions may be withdrawn, and no further penal action is to be taken against the cohort for non-compliance during the window.

evidence.supporting_text: The SEBI Master Circular dated July 11, 2023 for compliance with the LODR Regulations prescribes the procedure for recognised stock exchanges and depositories in respect of listed entities not complying with MPS requirements, including levy of fines, freezing of promoter shareholding and other consequential actions; an industry body has represented the difficulties faced by listed entities in achieving MPS compliance owing to capital-market volatility from geopolitical tensions.

Considering the representation and prevailing market conditions, SEBI grants a one-time relaxation from applicability of the penal provisions under the Master Circular for listed entities whose due date for MPS compliance falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026; recognised stock exchanges and depositories are advised not to take any penal action against such entities for non-compliance during that period, and any penal actions initiated by them against such entities for MPS non-compliance during April 1, 2026 till date may be withdrawn.

The circular is applicable with immediate effect; the stock exchanges are advised to bring the circular to the notice of listed entities and disseminate it on their website, and to make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for implementation, if necessary.

updates.summary: Settlement order disposing adjudication proceedings against KTIL's managing director for an alleged failure to maintain a Structured Digital Database (SDD) under regulation 3(5) of the PIT Regulations, settled on payment of Rs. 23,42,600 without admission or denial.

updates.summary: Circular extending the MII Capacity Planning and Real Time Performance Monitoring framework (previously applicable to other segments) to the Commodity Derivatives Segment of Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations, with tailored capacity/escalation thresholds, a Board-approved policy-submission deadline, and supersession of the prior single-clause capacity requirement; the circular itself takes effect 3 months after issuance.

updates.title: Consultation Paper on Measures towards Ease of Doing Business for REITs and InvITs
updates.summary: Consultation paper proposing four distinct 'ease of doing business' measures for REITs/InvITs: (1) preserving SPV status for InvIT SPVs after concession-period end, subject to exit/reacquisition and disclosure conditions; (2) widening REIT/InvIT liquid-mutual-fund investment eligibility (CRV>=10, Class A-I or B-I); (3) permitting privately listed InvITs to invest up to 10% of asset value in pure greenfield projects, aligning with publicly listed InvITs; and (4) expanding permitted end-uses of borrowing above the 49% Net Borrowings threshold to include specified capex, road-sector major maintenance, and conditioned debt refinancing. Comments due 26 February 2026.

events.title: Proposal to allow InvIT SPVs to retain SPV status after concession-period end/termination, subject to exit/reacquisition and disclosure conditions
events.summary: Proposes to expand the SPV definition so that concession-period end/termination does not itself disqualify an entity from SPV status, subject to a one-year exit/reacquisition condition and enhanced annual-report disclosures.
events.position: A company/LLP holding a PPP project would not lose SPV status merely because the concession agreement concluded or was terminated, provided the Investment Manager exits the investment or acquires a new infrastructure project within one year of the latest of (a) concession completion/termination, (b) conclusion of pending claims/litigation, or (c) completion of the defect liability period, and provided specified InvIT-level and SPV-level annual-report disclosures are made in the interim.

parties.name: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
parties.scope: InvITs holding infrastructure projects through SPVs whose concession period has ended/terminated; the proposal would let such SPVs retain their SPV status subject to conditions.

parties.name: Investment Manager of the InvIT
parties.scope: Would bear the proposed exit/reacquisition-within-one-year obligation and the InvIT/SPV-level annual-report disclosure duties for such SPVs.

actions.description: If adopted: exit (sale/liquidation/winding-up) the SPV investment, or acquire a new infrastructure project in it, within one year of the latest triggering event.

If adopted, manager reports trust-level gross/net investment breakup and each affected SPV’s project/end-date/vesting certificate, grouped audited carrying assets/liabilities/reserves, contingent liabilities, outstanding debt/repayment schedule, claims/litigation/assessments/contractual duties/defect period, asset sufficiency and funding plan if inadequate, and exit/new-project strategy with steps taken and expected completion. These disclosures continue while the InvIT holds the SPV.

effects.description: Proposes a proviso to the InvIT Regulations' SPV definition (Regulation 2(1)(zy)) preserving SPV status after PPP concession-period end/termination, subject to a one-year exit/reacquisition condition and enhanced disclosures.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Proposal only; subject to public comment (due 26 February 2026) and Board finalisation.

deadlines.obligation: If adopted: exit the SPV investment or acquire a new infrastructure project in it.

timing.raw_text: within one year from ... whichever is later
timing.anchor_event: The latest of: concession completion/termination, conclusion of pending claims/litigation, or completion of the defect liability period.

evidence.supporting_text: Consultation Paper on Measures towards Ease of Doing Business for REITs and InvITs, issued by the Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities - POD II, dated 5 February 2026.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.locator: Contents page (four matters and comment deadline)
evidence.supporting_text: Lists four matters for consultation: (1) Continuing investment in SPV post end of concession period (InvITs); (2) Expanding the scope of investment in liquid mutual fund schemes (both REITs and InvITs); (3) Alignment of investment conditions for Private InvIT with Public InvIT re: greenfield projects (InvITs); (4) Expanding the scope of permitted use of fresh borrowings for InvITs where Net Borrowings exceeds 49% (InvITs). States 'Comments on the Consultation paper (CP) may be sent by February 26, 2026'.
evidence.quote: Comments on the Consultation paper (CP) may be sent by February 26, 2026
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Objective is to seek comments/views/suggestions on various ease-of-doing-business measures for REITs and InvITs; proposals based on inputs from the Indian REITs Association (IRA), Bharat InvITs Association (BIA), and recommendations of the Hybrid Securities Advisory Committee (HYSAC).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Under the InvIT Regulations, InvITs hold infrastructure projects via HoldCo/SPV; on expiry/termination of a concession period, the SPV's concession rights cease though the InvIT may remain invested in it. Industry associations requested clarification whether such an SPV (no longer holding any infrastructure project) still qualifies as an 'SPV' under the InvIT Regulations.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 2(1)(zy) of the InvIT Regulations defines 'SPV' as a company/LLP in which the InvIT/HoldCo holds controlling interest and >=51% equity, which holds >=90% of its assets directly in infrastructure projects and does not invest in other SPVs, and is not engaged in any activity other than those pertaining/incidental to the underlying infrastructure projects.
evidence.quote: which holds not less than ninety per cent. of its assets directly in infrastructure projects and does not invest in other SPVs
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Upon expiry/termination of the concession agreement, the InvIT continues to hold SPVs lacking an eligible/completed-and-revenue-generating infrastructure project; commercial/practical constraints (statutory/contractual obligations, litigation, defect-liability periods) prevent immediate divestment or winding-up, causing negative cash flows requiring NDCF adjustment at the Trust level; industry requested clarification that such entities remain classified as SPVs.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI's consideration: upon expiry/termination, the SPV's infrastructure-project interest ceases and it may no longer meet the 90% qualifying criterion, yet the InvIT may need to continue holding it due to continuing statutory/contractual obligations that make immediate winding-up difficult.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed new proviso to the SPV definition: conclusion/termination of a PPP concession agreement shall not affect the entity's status as an SPV, subject to conditions specified by the Board.
evidence.quote: the conclusion or termination of the concession agreement with the public concessioning authority shall not affect the status as an SPV and such company or LLP, shall continue to be classified as an SPV, subject to fulfillment of the conditions specified by the Board.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed condition: the Investment Manager shall either exit the SPV investment (sale/liquidation/winding-up) or acquire a new infrastructure project in it, within one year of the latest of: (a) completion/termination of the concession agreement, (b) conclusion of all pending claims/litigation, or (c) completion of the defect liability period.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

events.summary: Aligns private-InvIT investment conditions with public-InvIT conditions by permitting a limited greenfield-project allowance for private InvITs, mirroring the existing public-InvIT allowance.
events.position: Would add Regulation 18(5)(b)(i) to the permitted residual-20% investments in Regulation 18(4), enabling up to 10% of InvIT asset value in pure greenfield projects while retaining the 80% eligible-infrastructure requirement.

evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Under Regulation 18 of the InvIT Regulations, a publicly listed InvIT may invest up to 10% of asset value in pure greenfield (under-construction) projects, but a privately listed InvIT cannot; market participants requested parity. Regulation 14(2)/14(4) govern private/public InvIT fundraising respectively; Regulation 18(4) requires >=80% investment in 'eligible infrastructure projects' for private InvITs (with un-invested funds only in listed sub-clause instruments); Regulation 18(5) sets the public-InvIT 80%/20% split (completed-and-revenue-generating vs. under-construction, capped at 10%).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: A privately listed InvIT must invest >=80% in 'eligible infrastructure projects' (which excludes pure greenfield/50-50-test-failing projects) with the balance 20% restricted to money-market/other-investment avenues (no under-construction-project category); a publicly listed InvIT must invest >=80% in completed/revenue-generating projects with up to 10% of the balance 20% permitted in pure greenfield projects. Retail investors participate in public InvITs (1-unit lot size) while only institutional/body-corporate investors participate in private InvITs (Rs. 25 lakh minimum lot), yet only the (retail-facing) public InvIT currently has any greenfield allowance.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed amendment to Regulation 18(4) of the InvIT Regulations to add sub-clause (i) among the permitted un-invested-fund instruments, facilitating privately listed InvITs to invest up to 10% of InvIT asset value in pure greenfield projects, aligning with publicly listed InvITs.

events.title: Proposal to expand permitted end-uses of fresh borrowing above the 49% Net Borrowings threshold to include specified capex, road-sector major maintenance, and qualifying debt refinancing
events.summary: Expands the permitted end-uses of borrowing above the 49% Net Borrowings threshold beyond acquisition/development of infrastructure projects, clarifying that specified capex, road-sector major maintenance, and conditioned debt refinancing all qualify.
events.position: If adopted, assess additional borrowing above 49% net borrowings for: asset-performance/capacity capex; non-routine major maintenance required by the concession for Roads and bridges projects as defined by the September 19, 2025 Ministry of Finance notification; or refinancing originally permitted-purpose debt. Refinancing must not increase aggregate consolidated borrowings/deferred payments net of cash/equivalents and may refinance principal only, excluding accumulated interest and all fees/charges. No increase to the existing leverage ceiling or waiver of other conditions is proposed.

Refinancing must not increase aggregate consolidated borrowings/deferred payments net of cash/equivalents and may refinance principal only, excluding accumulated interest and all fees/charges. No increase to the existing leverage ceiling or waiver of other conditions is proposed.

effects.savings_or_limitations: Refinancing use is conditioned on no increase in aggregate Net Borrowings and on refinancing only the principal portion of debt; proposal only, subject to public comment (due 26 February 2026) and Board finalisation.

evidence.supporting_text: Objective is to seek comments/views/suggestions on various ease-of-doing-business measures for REITs and InvITs; proposals based on inputs from the Indian REITs Association (IRA), Bharat InvITs Association (BIA), and recommendations of the Hybrid Securities Advisory Committee (HYSAC).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii) of the InvIT Regulations requires that where Net Borrowings (aggregate consolidated borrowings/deferred payments of InvIT, HoldCo, SPV(s), net of cash) exceed 49% of InvIT asset value, further borrowing be utilised only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects (also requiring 'AAA' issuer credit rating, a 6-distribution track record, and unitholder approval); BIA requested clarification that refinancing and improvement/major-maintenance/capacity-augmentation borrowing qualify as permitted use.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: BIA represented that refinancing of SPV/HoldCo-level acquisition debt at the InvIT level, and refinancing of existing InvIT/SPV/HoldCo debt due to maturity or better terms, does not change the original development-related end-use of the debt being refinanced and should qualify as permitted use.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: BIA represented that capital expenditure/major-maintenance (MM) borrowing to enhance asset performance or meet concession-mandated requirements should also qualify as 'development'; MM expense is not eligible for capitalisation for road-sector InvITs under applicable accounting principles (unlike renewable/airport assets), creating a need for clarity on its treatment under Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI's consideration accepts that: refinancing of newly acquired SPV/HoldCo debt and of maturing/repriced InvIT/SPV/HoldCo debt does not change the underlying development-related end-use; capex for asset performance/capacity augmentation is 'development' and hence already permitted; and MM expense for road projects specifically warrants an express clarification given its non-capitalisable accounting treatment.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed enabling amendment to Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii) ('utilize the funds only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects or such other purpose as may be specified by the Board from time to time'), specifying permitted end-uses: (i) capex for asset performance/capacity augmentation; (ii) Major Maintenance expense for Road Projects (both terms defined); and (iii) refinancing of debt originally availed for a Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii)-permitted purpose, subject to no increase in aggregate Net Borrowings and refinancing of principal only.
evidence.quote: utilize the funds only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects or such other purpose as may be specified by the Board from time to time
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Comments invited on: (a) permitting capex borrowings; (b) permitting Major Maintenance-expense borrowings for the road sector; and (c) permitting refinancing of debt, all under Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii).

updates.title: Mandating periodic disclosure requirements- Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs)
updates.summary: Mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosures for Securitised Debt Instruments by the trustee of the special purpose distinct entity, in the Annexure I / II formats, to the Board and the listing stock exchange within 30 days of each half-year end, effective March 31, 2026.

events.title: Mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosures for SDIs by the trustee of the SPDE
events.summary: The trustee of an SPDE must make half-yearly pool-level disclosures for SDIs in the prescribed Annexure I / II formats to the Board and the listing stock exchange within 30 days of each half-year end.
events.position: The Trustee of a special purpose distinct entity shall submit the Annexure I (loan / listed debt / credit facility exposures) or Annexure II (other exposures) disclosures on a half-yearly basis to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed, within 30 days from the end of March or September; Annexure III provides computation illustrations.

parties.name: Special purpose distinct entities (SPDEs) that have issued SDIs
parties.scope: The securitisation vehicle on whose behalf the trustee makes the half-yearly disclosures; Regulation 11B binds the SPDE and the trustee.

parties.name: Trustee of the special purpose distinct entity
parties.scope: The trustee is the actor required to submit the Annexure I / II disclosures half-yearly to the Board and the stock exchange within 30 days from the end of March or September.

parties.name: Recognised Stock Exchanges where SDIs are listed
parties.scope: Stock exchanges where the SDIs are listed are addressees and recipients of the half-yearly disclosures.

actions.description: The Trustee of the SPDE shall submit the Annexure I or Annexure II half-yearly disclosures to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed.
The disclosures shall be made within 30 days from the end of March or September on a recurring half-yearly basis, in the prescribed formats.

effects.description: Specifies the manner of the half-yearly information-furnishing duty under Regulation 11B of the SDI Regulations, 2008 by prescribing the Annexure I / II disclosure formats, the recipients (Board and listing stock exchange) and the 30-day timeline.
Introduces the specific mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosure obligation on the trustee of the SPDE, with the detailed formats in Annexures I and II and the illustrations in Annexure III.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall be effective from March 31, 2026.

deadlines.obligation: The Trustee of the SPDE shall submit the half-yearly SDI disclosures to the Board and the listing stock exchange.

timing.raw_text: within 30 days from the end of March or September
timing.anchor_event: end of March or September (each half-year)
conditions: recurring half-yearly obligation

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 11B of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008 (last amended on May 05, 2025) mandates a special purpose distinct entity and the trustee to furnish information to the Board on a half-yearly basis, in the manner as may be specified by the Board.

Pursuant to discussions with stakeholders, it is decided that the Trustee of a special purpose distinct entity shall submit the disclosures set out in Annexure I and Annexure II on a half-yearly basis to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed, within 30 days from the end of March or September; Annexure I applies to SDIs backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures, Annexure II to SDIs backed by other exposures, and Annexure III provides illustrations of weighted average maturity, weighted average rating and average default rate.

The provisions of this circular shall be effective from March 31, 2026; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulations 11B and 48 of the SDI Regulations, 2008 to protect the interests of investors and to develop and regulate the securities market.

evidence.locator: Annexure I (disclosure format - securitisation of loan / listed debt / credit facility exposures)
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure I prescribes the half-yearly disclosure format for SDIs backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures, covering maturity characteristics of underlying assets, Minimum Retention Requirement, credit quality (overdue distribution, security cover, rating-wise distribution, default and recovery rates, LTV and DTI frequency distributions, prepayment, top-up loans, expected credit loss, recovery actions, utilisation of credit enhancement and liquidity facility), amendments, other pool characteristics and Minimum Holding Period.

evidence.locator: Annexure II (disclosure format - securitisation of other exposures)
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure II prescribes the half-yearly disclosure format for SDIs backed by other exposures, covering maturity characteristics, Minimum Retention Requirement, credit quality (deviations in collections, obligor default, prepayment, recovery actions, utilisation of credit enhancement and liquidity facility), amendments, other information and Minimum Holding Period.
Annexure III sets out illustrations for computing the weighted average maturity of the underlying assets, the weighted average rating of the pool and the average (moving average) default rate.

events.title: Periodic KYC, consent controls and record retention
events.summary: Periodic KYC, consent controls and record retention in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: The custodian obtains confirmation of changed KYC documents. For high-risk jurisdictions, government Category I FPIs are reviewed every three years; other Category I and Category II FPIs annually. For other jurisdictions, Category I and regulated Category II FPIs are reviewed every three years; other Category II FPIs annually. GS-FPIs follow the bank KYC periodicity prescribed by RBI. KRAs secure BO/SMO data using need-to-know authentication. The FPI may choose consent controls, with one mandatory and two optional email addresses and default consent set to Yes. Modified KYC is sent unsolicited to intermediaries that previously uploaded, downloaded or modified the record, including where consent is Yes. Inform the KRA of account closure to delink the intermediary. Retain original KYC for at least five years after cessation of transactions, and longer until pending litigation or proceedings end.

events.title: KYC verification methods and acceptable proofs
events.summary: KYC verification methods and acceptable proofs in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: Verification against originals or authorised attestation suffices without additional self-certification. Authorised officials of multinational or RBI-regulated banks may certify digital copies through authenticated free-format SWIFT. Foreign-language documents require English translation; names and addresses must match and each address needs proof. An authorised custodian may complete forms under a power of attorney. In-person verification does not apply to non-individuals; individuals may use webcam verification. Reliable information from public regulator, exchange, SRO or registrar sources may be attested by an authorised intermediary official. Individual identity proof requires government photo identification. Address proofs include government/regulator records, utility bills no older than two months, bank statements no older than three months, and appropriately notarised, apostilled or consularised custodian powers of attorney. Multilateral institutions may use their constitutive documents. Separate address proof is unnecessary if valid address information is already in the identity proof.

events.summary: Investor-group equity limits and exemptions in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: Depositories capture investor-group details and monitor end-of-day demat holdings. An individual FPI and relatives under the Companies Act are grouped. Include holdings across custodians; the group may request aggregate holdings. IBRD, IDA, MIGA and IFC have the stated World Bank exemption. Federal/provincial entities with different beneficial owners are treated separately. Other foreign-government agencies with a common investor group are grouped unless an applicable treaty, agreement or Central Government order supplies an exemption.

events.title: Red flags, purchase halts and proportionate disinvestment
events.summary: Red flags, purchase halts and proportionate disinvestment in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: When headroom is 3% or less for an FPI, NRI or sectoral cap, the depository raises a red flag, publishes available shares daily and informs exchanges. A breach stops purchases by the affected FPI, NRI or all-foreign-investor cohort. Net buyers proportionately divest the excess only to domestic investors within five trading days after settlement. Table 5 illustrates 1,000 purchases against capacity of 600, allocating the excess 400 as 40/100/20/72/48/60/60. Custodian T+1 data identifies an end-of-day breach; affected T+1 buyers also receive the stated five-trading-day disposal period. The holiday examples retain T+2/T+3/T+4/T+8 settlement labels as source illustrations; this paper does not thereby amend other settlement rules. Later headroom does not waive the required sale. Trades are not annulled; failures are referred to SEBI.

events.title: Offmarket transfers, to-be-listed shares, warrants and primary allotment
events.summary: Offmarket transfers, to-be-listed shares, warrants and primary allotment in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: The draft permits DDP-approved off-market transfers between same-PAN MIM accounts; a one-time IFSC relocation after due diligence without prejudicing tax treatment; and sales of unlisted, illiquid, suspended or delisted shares at FEMA-compliant prices. To-be-listed equity may be acquired through IPOs, FPOs, rights issues, private placements and involuntary scheme actions. Listed or unlisted warrants are permitted where their underlying shares are listed or to be listed. RTAs use PAN for the individual FPI below-10% check and obtain depository group validation within the issue procedure. Same-PAN MIM bids with different beneficiary/client/DP IDs need not be treated as multiple bids. Rights-entitlement transfers use market price or fair value.

events.title: Corporate-debt eligibility, RFQ and investment-limit auctions
events.summary: Corporate-debt eligibility, RFQ and investment-limit auctions in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: Government securities, debt, currency derivatives and IRFs follow the referenced RBI directions. To-be-listed corporate debt is not subject to the end-use restriction otherwise applicable to unlisted debt; if it is not listed within 30 days or the applicable end-use condition fails, dispose of it immediately to a domestic investor or the issuer. At least 10% of quarterly secondary corporate-debt trade value must use RFQ quotes. Debt mutual fund holdings count towards corporate-debt limits. CDIL is available on tap until 95% utilisation; above that, stop purchases and auction unutilised limits. Auctions alternate BSE/NSE on the second trading day after intimation if at least INR 100 crore is free, or on the sixteenth day after fifteen consecutive trading days below that amount. Auction hours are 15:30–17:30; minimum bid and tick are INR 1 crore; maximum bid is 10% of the offered limit; allocation is by price-time priority and the fee is the higher of INR 1,000 and the bid amount. Use allocated limits within ten trading days. Sale/redemption permits two-trading-day reinvestment; unused limits return to the pool. Subsequent auctions are every twelve trading days subject to availability. Below 92% utilisation, on-tap access resumes; recrossing 95% does not revive the earlier reinvestment facility. Obsolete 3.8.3.4/3.8.3.7 cross-references remain disclosed as draft defects.

events.title: Interest-rate futures position limits
events.summary: Interest-rate futures position limits in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: For eligible Category I/II FPIs other than individuals, family offices and corporates, aggregate IRF net-long positions are capped at INR 5,000 crore and each FPI at INR 1,800 crore. Net shorts are not counted in that aggregate; the government-securities investment limit is separate. Other Category I/II FPIs use trading-member position limits; Category II individuals, family offices and corporates use client limits. For the 8–11-year maturity bucket, the trading-member limit is the higher of 10% of open interest and INR 12 billion; the client limit is the higher of 3% and INR 4 billion. For 4–8 and 11–15 years, the corresponding amounts are INR 6 billion and INR 2 billion. Gross short IRFs may not exceed long government-securities and IRF positions. Exchanges enforce limits, publish aggregate net-long positions daily and issue 90%-utilisation alerts. A breaching FPI squares off excess within five trading days or contract expiry, whichever is earlier.

events.title: Voluntary write-off, escrow sale and IPEF reporting
events.summary: Voluntary write-off, escrow sale and IPEF reporting in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: An FPI with invalid registration or intending surrender that cannot sell may request write-off. It authorises waiver of all beneficial rights; the custodian extinguishes the holding in its books, reports a NIL-proceeds sale to SEBI/RBI, freezes the demat account and follows the surrender-NOC process. Monetary corporate benefits go to IPEF within 30 days of receipt; non-monetary benefits accumulate. Transfer written-off or deemed-written-off securities to an exchange-empanelled broker escrow within 30 days, using the sole listing exchange or otherwise NSE. The broker attempts sale at market prices; listed equity uses the regular platform, excluding the block window. Proceeds net of brokerage and statutory charges go to IPEF. The exchange monitors the broker, replaces it if needed, and reports quarterly under Annexure I within 15 days, including custodian, ISIN, quantities, movements, proceeds and IPEF transfers.

events.title: FPI granular ownership-disclosure triggers and exemptions
events.summary: FPI granular ownership-disclosure triggers and exemptions in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: Require full natural-person ownership/control/economic-interest disclosure without thresholds where more than 50% of Indian equity AUM is in a single corporate group (33% for the specified IFSC paragraph 7 route, tested separately for each segregated portfolio), or combined Indian-equity holdings exceed INR 50,000 crore across the FPI/group and ODI subscribers with more than 50% common ownership or common control. Count direct equity and ODI exposure without counting the underlying twice. Exemptions cover government investors, DDP-validated public retail funds, qualifying ETFs with less than 50% India-related exposure and qualifying listed entities, regulated pooled schemes meeting the less-than-25%-global-AUM group or less-than-50%-global-AUM Indian-equity tests, statutory restrictions while they last, new FPIs for 90 calendar days after first Indian-equity settlement, and wind-down to NIL within 180 days after surrender intimation. Qualifying university funds/endowments require less than 25% India exposure, global AUM above INR 10,000 crore, non-profit tax filings and an eligible jurisdiction. Deduct exempt group members for the INR 50,000 crore test; only the remaining non-exempt members disclose if still above it. Stop look-through at exempt entities. DDPs/custodians validate under a public SOP.

events.title: FPI granular-disclosure cures, invalidity and voting restrictions
events.summary: FPI granular-disclosure cures, invalidity and voting restrictions in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: For concentration breaches, allow ten trading days to realign and prohibit fresh corporate-group equity purchases for 30 calendar days. The INR 50,000 crore group-size breach allows 90 calendar days to realign, with purchases blocked until below the threshold. A fresh breach after realignment restarts the cure. If the breach persists, disclose to the DDP within 30 trading days after the cure period. Non-disclosure invalidates registration, stops purchases and starts 180 calendar days for liquidation; a segregated-portfolio concentration failure affects only that portfolio. Investee companies restrict voting to the lower of actual holdings and holdings corresponding to 50% of the FPI equity AUM. Update disclosures while above the trigger. Depositories freeze accounts and maintain group information with exchange systems. DDPs report non-disclosing and exempt FPIs quarterly within 15 calendar days.

events.title: ODI issuance, hedging and investment clubbing
events.summary: ODI issuance, hedging and investment clubbing in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: ODI issuers use a dedicated non-proprietary FPI registration with an ODI suffix and the same PAN; adding the suffix is not a name change. Government-security underlying ODIs have the stated dedicated-registration exemption. Do not issue ODIs with derivative underlyings or hedge them through Indian exchange derivatives; maintain a one-to-one hedge in the same underlying security throughout. A non-proprietary index with less than 20% Indian components is not an ODI even if hedged onshore; an onshore-hedged custom basket is always an ODI. Synthetic shorts are prohibited. Document the relationship between the FATF-regulated investment manager and subscriber. Club subscribers with more than 50% common ownership or common control; aggregate direct FPI and ODI underlying-company holdings.

events.title: ODI granular disclosure triggers, exemptions and apex-company test
events.summary: ODI granular disclosure triggers, exemptions and apex-company test in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: The issuer collects natural-person ownership/control/economic-interest information without thresholds when a subscriber has more than 50% of equity ODI exposure through that issuer in one group, or combined Indian-equity/FPI/ODI holdings exceed INR 50,000 crore for the more-than-50%-common-ownership or common-control group. Avoid double counting underlying assets. Depositories, DDPs, custodians and issuers maintain a public SOP. Exemptions cover governments, validated public retail funds, qualifying ETFs with less than 50% India exposure and eligible listed entities, regulated pooled schemes meeting the less-than-25%-global-group or less-than-50%-global-India tests, statutory restrictions, and qualifying university funds/endowments with less than 25% India exposure, global AUM above INR 10,000 crore and non-profit tax status. Deduct exempt entities for the size test and stop look-through at them. Do not import the FPI new-registration or wind-down exemptions into the ODI list. The promoterless-apex exemption requires non-apex holdings no more than 50% and combined concentrated non-exempt FPI/ODI apex stakes below 3%. Track daily and publish before next-day trading; prospective positions receive ten trading days to realign or disclose only if the 3% trigger persists.

events.title: ODI cure periods, disclosures, ineligibility and monitoring
events.summary: ODI cure periods, disclosures, ineligibility and monitoring in the draft FPI master circular.
events.position: Allow ten trading days for concentration realignment, with no fresh group ODIs for 30 calendar days. Size breaches receive 90 calendar days, with no new positions until below INR 50,000 crore. Depositories publish lists and issuers enforce restrictions. A repeated breach after realignment restarts the cure. Collect granular disclosures within 30 trading days after the cure period; the issuer forwards them to depositories within five trading days after receipt. Non-disclosure makes the subscriber ineligible across issuers: redeem all positions within 180 calendar days, publish the ineligibility and stop issuance. Forward changes in collected details within 30 days. Depositories maintain positions and disclosure data, identify breaches, notify issuers and monitor filing timelines and non-compliance.

actions.description: For RPTs above INR 1 crore, provide the applicable information to the Audit Committee and, where shareholder approval is sought, in the shareholder explanatory statement; use Annexure-13A in the intermediate-value tier and the RPT Industry Standards outside it.
From the effective date, follow the prescribed Annexure-13A format and applicable RPT Industry Standards to comply with Part A and Part B of Section III-B.
The counterparty annual consolidated turnover percentage represented by the proposed RPT may be provided on a voluntary basis in the Annexure-13A information for the Audit Committee and shareholders.

Where Annexure-13A applies, give the audit committee transaction type, material terms/particulars, related-party identity/relationship and interest, specified tenure, value and percentage of prior-year listed-entity consolidated turnover; if a subsidiary is involved, additionally give its standalone turnover percentage. Include listed-entity-interest justification, relied-on valuation/external report and other relevant information.

For loans, inter-corporate deposits, advances or investments by the listed entity/subsidiary, provide funds source, financing indebtedness nature/cost/tenure (subject only to the specified listed-financial-entity exception), applicable covenants/tenure/interest/repayment and secured status/security, and ultimate beneficiary use.

Where shareholder approval is sought under the applicable Annexure tier, explanatory statement includes summary of management information to the audit committee, transaction-interest justification, relevant financing details, statement making relied-on valuation/external reports available through shareholders’ registered email addresses, and other relevant information, in addition to Companies Act requirements.

updates.title: Review of Block Deal Framework
updates.summary: Revised Block Deal Framework - two block deal windows with defined reference prices, a +3% price range, a INR 25 crore minimum order size, a mandatory-delivery / no-square-off rule and same-day dissemination - applicable also to the optional T+0 settlement cycle, from the 60th day of issuance.

events.title: Revised Block Deal Framework - windows, reference prices, price range and order size
events.summary: The Block Deal Framework is revised with new window timings, reference-price bases, a +3% price range, a INR 25 crore minimum order size and a mandatory-delivery rule, applied also to the T+0 window.
events.position: Two block deal windows (Morning 08:45-09:00 at previous day close; Afternoon 02:05-02:20 PM at 01:45-02:00 PM cash VWAP), orders within +3% of the reference price, minimum order size INR 25 crore, every trade must result in delivery and cannot be squared off or reversed, block deal details disseminated to the public the same day after market hours, and normal-segment trading/settlement/surveillance/risk measures applied to block deal windows, including under the optional T+0 settlement cycle.

parties.name: Recognized Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Stock exchanges operate the block deal windows, set the reference prices, compute and disseminate the afternoon VWAP, enforce the price range and order-size limits and disseminate block deal details.

parties.name: Recognized Clearing Corporations
parties.scope: Clearing corporations ensure that settlement, surveillance and risk-containment measures for the normal segment apply to block deal windows, including under the T+0 cycle.

parties.name: Depositories
parties.scope: Depositories ensure appropriate trading and settlement practices for block deal windows and make consequential rule amendments.

actions.description: MIIs shall take necessary steps and put in place necessary systems for implementation and make necessary amendments to the relevant byelaws, rules and regulations wherever required.

MIIs shall ensure that all trading and settlement practices and surveillance and risk-containment measures applicable to the normal trading segment are applied and implemented for the Block Deal windows.

Stock exchanges shall disseminate block deal information (scrip name, client name, quantity, traded price, etc.) to the general public on the same day after market hours, and shall disseminate the applicable afternoon-window VWAP between 02:00-02:05 PM.

effects.description: Modifies paragraph 1.2 of Chapter 1 of the December 30, 2024 Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations and paragraph 3.5 of the December 10, 2024 T+0 circular, replacing them with the revised Block Deal Framework parameters.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Modification is limited to the identified paragraphs; other provisions of both instruments are unaffected.

effects.description: Sets the operational rules for block deals: window timings, reference-price computation, +3% price range, INR 25 crore minimum order size, mandatory delivery with no square-off/reversal, same-day dissemination, and extension of normal-segment surveillance and risk-containment measures.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of the circular shall be applicable from the 60th day of issuance of the circular.

evidence.supporting_text: Paragraph 1.2 of Chapter 1 of SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD-PoD2/CIR/P/2024/00181 dated December 30, 2024 for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations, and paragraph 3.5 of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2024/172 dated December 10, 2024 (T+0 rolling settlement enhancement), stand modified; the modification follows a Working Group, Secondary Market Advisory Committee deliberations and public comments.

Revised framework: exchanges may set trading hours 08:45 AM-05:00 PM and provide a separate block deal window(s); a Morning Block Deal Window operates 08:45-09:00 with reference price = previous day closing price, and an Afternoon Block Deal Window operates 02:05 PM-02:20 PM with reference price = VWAP of cash-segment trades executed 01:45-02:00 PM (exchanges compute and disseminate the VWAP between 02:00-02:05 PM); orders must be within +3% of the applicable reference price subject to surveillance measures and price bands; minimum order size for block deal windows is INR 25 crore; every trade must result in delivery and shall not be squared off or reversed; exchanges disseminate block deal details to the public on the same day after market hours; the provisions also apply to the block deal window under the optional T+0 settlement cycle.

Stock Exchanges, Clearing Corporations and Depositories shall ensure that all trading and settlement practices and surveillance and risk-containment measures applicable to the normal trading segment are also applicable and implemented for the Block Deal windows.

Applicability: the provisions of the circular shall be applicable from the 60th day of issuance of the circular; all MIIs are advised to put systems in place, amend byelaws/rules/regulations and publicise the circular; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018 and Section 26(3) of the Depositories Act, 1996 read with Regulation 97 of the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018.

updates.title: Measures for Enhancing Trading Convenience and Strengthening Risk Monitoring in Equity Derivatives
updates.summary: A package of equity-derivatives measures: FutEq Open Interest measurement and a redefined single-stock MWPL with stricter ban-period and intraday-monitoring rules and recalibrated entity limits (5.1-5.4, 5.8); new PAN-level index options and category-wise index futures position limits with a July-December 2025 glide path (5.5, Annexure-1); extension of the pre-open session to derivatives (5.6); and prudential eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices (5.7). Phased implementation from July 01, 2025 to December 06, 2025.

events.title: Single-stock F&O risk framework - FutEq Open Interest, redefined MWPL, ban-period rule, intraday MWPL monitoring and recalibrated entity-level limits
events.summary: Single-stock F&O risk controls move to FutEq OI, a delivery-linked MWPL formula, a stricter ban-period rule, mandatory intraday MWPL monitoring and recalibrated entity-level limits.
events.position: Open Interest is measured as portfolio-level net Delta-adjusted FutEq OI; MWPL for single stocks is the lower of 15% of free float and 65x Average Daily Delivery Value across Clearing Corporations, floored at 10% of free float, recalculated quarterly; the 95%-of-MWPL ban test is applied to FutEq OI and any trading during a ban period must reduce end-of-day FutEq OI; Stock Exchanges perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times per session; entity-level single-stock limits are recalibrated to the new MWPL (Client/NRI 10%, TM proprietary 20%, TM proprietary+client / FPI Cat I / MF 30%, FPI Cat II tiers 20% / 10%).

parties.name: Stock Exchanges (equity derivatives segment)
parties.scope: Stock Exchanges compute FutEq OI and MWPL, run ban-period and intraday-utilisation monitoring, apply index and single-stock position limits, extend the pre-open session, apply non-benchmark-index eligibility criteria and prepare joint SOPs with SEBI.

parties.name: Clearing Corporations (equity derivatives segment)
parties.scope: Clearing Corporations disseminate FutEq OI, provide Average Daily Delivery Value inputs for MWPL, monitor positions and prepare joint SOPs with SEBI.

parties.name: Foreign Portfolio Investors (Category I and Category II) trading equity derivatives
parties.scope: FPI category-wise position limits for index futures and single stocks are recalibrated; FPIs must report cash / securities holdings for additional-exposure monitoring.

parties.name: Mutual Funds trading equity derivatives
parties.scope: Mutual Fund position limits for index and single-stock derivatives are recalibrated to the new formulation.

parties.name: Trading Members and their clients in the equity derivatives segment
parties.scope: Trading members (proprietary and proprietary+client) and clients are subject to the recalibrated index and single-stock position limits and the ban-period FutEq OI reduction rule.

actions.description: Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations shall compute FutEq OI and the redefined MWPL, apply the FutEq-OI-based ban-period test and the end-of-day FutEq OI reduction rule, and apply the recalibrated entity-level single-stock position limits.

Stock Exchanges shall perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times during each trading session, take actions such as Additional Surveillance Margin on breach of limits, and report significant utilisation / breach of MWPL to SEBI in the fortnightly Surveillance meeting.

Clearing Corporations / Stock Exchanges shall prepare joint SOPs in consultation with SEBI for monitoring end-of-day delta positions, intraday MWPL utilisation and top-entity concentration, with the associated penalty structure.

effects.description: Modifies Clauses 3.3.2.1.1 (MWPL), 3.3.2.1.2.1 (ban-period test), 3.3.2 and 4.3.2 (single-stock entity limits) of Chapter 5 of the December 30, 2024 Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Passive increases in FutEq OI from scrip movement and sign changes are not treated as breaches / acceptable reductions respectively; para 5.1 (FutEq OI) is already implemented.

effects.description: Tightens and re-bases the single-stock derivatives risk controls: a delivery-linked MWPL formula with a floor, a stricter end-of-day FutEq OI reduction rule during ban periods, mandatory intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring, and recalibrated entity-level position limits.

commencement.raw_text: Effective From October 01, 2025 (per the phased implementation table for measures 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8; measure 5.1 is already implemented and measure 5.4 is effective November 03, 2025)

deadlines.obligation: Measure 5.4 (intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring for single stocks) becomes effective.

Stock Exchanges / Clearing Corporations shall prepare a joint Standard Operating Procedure in consultation with SEBI for monitoring positions and the associated penalty / additional-surveillance-margin framework.

timing.raw_text: within one month / 30 days from the date of the circular

transitions.affected_cohort: Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations and single-stock F&O participants
transitions.condition: Measure 5.1 (FutEq Open Interest measurement) is already implemented at the date of the circular; measures 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8 take effect October 01, 2025 and measure 5.4 takes effect November 03, 2025.
transitions.rule: The single-stock risk-framework measures are phased in on the stated dates, generally aligned with the monthly compliance mock sessions on the first Saturday of the month.

evidence.supporting_text: Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations provide the platform, products, risk management and surveillance for the derivatives market; Regulation 28(2) read with Part-C of Schedule II of the SECC Regulations, 2018 treats risk management, surveillance and product development as core functions; SEBI deliberated with an Expert Working Group on derivatives, issued a consultation paper on February 24, 2025, examined comments and deliberated in the Secondary Market Advisory Committee, and has decided to put in place measures to strengthen the equity derivatives framework, with implementation timelines at paragraph 6.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 5.1-5.4 (OI formulation, MWPL, ban-period, intraday monitoring)
evidence.supporting_text: Open Interest is to be measured at portfolio level as net Delta-adjusted (Future Equivalent, FutEq) open positions across futures and options for an underlying; Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL) for single stocks is redefined as the lower of 15% of free float and 65x Average Daily Delivery Value across Clearing Corporations with a floor of 10% of free float, recalculated every three months; once market-wide FutEq OI exceeds 95% of MWPL the scrip enters a ban period and any trading by an entity must reduce its FutEq OI on an end-of-day basis (passive increases and sign changes are not acceptable reductions); Stock Exchanges shall perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times per session and take actions (e.g. Additional Surveillance Margin) and report significant utilisation to SEBI; Clearing Corporations / Stock Exchanges shall prepare joint SOPs in consultation with SEBI within one month / 30 days of the circular.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 5.5-5.8 (index position limits, glide path, pre-open session, non-benchmark index eligibility, single-stock entity limits)
evidence.supporting_text: Index options: net end-of-day FutEq OI limit of Rs. 1,500 cr and gross FutEq OI limit of Rs. 10,000 cr at PAN level, with a glide path from July 01, 2025 to December 05, 2025 (T / T+1 intimation and position-reduction mechanics) and normal implementation from December 06, 2025; index futures: category-wise limits (FPI Category I / MF / TM proprietary / clients - higher of 15% of futures OI or Rs. 500 cr; FPI Category II tiers - 10% or 5% or Rs. 500 cr), measured on gross notional, effective July 01, 2025, with passive-breach protection; additional exposure permitted subject to short/long index positions not exceeding stock / cash holdings; pre-open session extended to current-month (and, in the last five days before expiry, next-month) single-stock and index futures from December 06, 2025; new prudential eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices (minimum 14 constituents, top weight <=20%, top-three combined <=45%, descending weights) from November 03, 2025, evaluated each calendar quarter; individual entity-level combined futures-and-options position limits for single stocks recalibrated to the new MWPL definition (Client/NRI 10%, TM proprietary 20%, TM proprietary+client / FPI Cat I / MF 30%, FPI Cat II tiers 20% / 10%) from October 01, 2025.

events.title: Prudential eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices from November 03, 2025 (para 5.7)
events.summary: New constituent-count and weight-concentration prudential criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices, evaluated quarterly.
events.position: Before introducing derivatives on a non-benchmark index a Stock Exchange must ensure: minimum 14 constituents; top constituent weight <= 20%; combined weight of top three constituents <= 45%; and each other constituent's weight lower than the higher-weighted constituents (descending structure). updates.title: Simplification of operational process and clarifying regarding the cash flow disclosure in Corporate Bond Database pursuant to review of Request for Quote (RFQ) Platform framework.
updates.summary: Two changes pursuant to the RFQ platform review: (1) simplified yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform (new clause 9, Chapter XXII of the NCS Master Circular); and (2) a new requirement for debt issuers to disclose and keep updated the cash flow schedule in the centralized corporate bond database (new paragraph 57, Annex-XIV-A). Effective from August 18, 2025.

events.title: Simplified yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform (new clause 9, Chapter XXII)
events.summary: Yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform now uses scheduled due dates without day-count adjustment.
events.position: For yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform, cash flow dates for interest / dividend / redemption are not adjusted for day count convention and are based on the due date of payment as per the cash flow schedule, not the actual date of payment.

parties.name: Recognised Stock Exchanges operating the RFQ platform
parties.scope: Stock exchanges operate the RFQ platform and must implement the simplified yield-to-price computation and publicise the circular.

actions.description: Stock exchanges shall implement the simplified yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform and make necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations.

effects.description: Inserts a new clause 9 in Chapter XXII of the NCS Master Circular prescribing the simplified yield-to-price computation basis for RFQ-platform trades.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Confined to yield-to-price computation for RFQ-platform trades; other trade-execution and settlement provisions of Chapter XXII are unaffected.

effects.description: Sets the computation rule: cash flow dates are not adjusted for day count convention and are based on the due date per the cash flow schedule rather than the payment date.

commencement.raw_text: This circular shall come into force with effect from August 18, 2025

evidence.supporting_text: Chapter XXII of the SEBI NCS Master Circular dated May 22, 2024 stipulates trade execution and settlement of trades on the RFQ platform; to simplify yield-to-price computation for non-convertible securities, cash flow dates for payment of interest / dividend / redemption for securities traded on the RFQ platform shall, for yield-to-price computation, not be adjusted for day count convention and shall be based on the due date of payment as per the cash flow schedule and not the date of payment; a new clause 9 to that effect is inserted in Chapter XXII of the NCS Master Circular.

The disclosure requirement is applicable for prospective issuances of debt securities and for the residual maturity of ISINs already listed; the circular shall come into force with effect from August 18, 2025.

events.title: Cash flow schedule disclosure in the centralized corporate bond database (new paragraph 57, Annex-XIV-A)

events.position: Issuers must provide the cash flow schedule for interest / dividend / redemption in the centralized corporate bond database at ISIN activation in a prescribed format (particulars, due date, payment date as per day count convention), and update any change within one working day; applicable to prospective issuances and to the residual maturity of ISINs already listed.

parties.name: Issuers of listed Non-convertible Securities / SDIs / Municipal Debt Securities / Commercial Paper

evidence.supporting_text: Clause 3.3.34 of Schedule I of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021 requires issuers to disclose cash flow with the date of interest / dividend / redemption payment per day count convention in the offer document; Chapter XIV of the NCS Master Circular requires issuers to submit and update information in the centralized database at ISIN activation and post-listing, but the cash flow schedule is not currently captured; a new paragraph 57 is inserted in Annex-XIV-A requiring issuers to provide the cash flow schedule for interest / dividend / redemption in the centralized corporate bond database at ISIN activation in a prescribed format (particulars, due date, payment date as per day count convention), and to update any change within one working day.

The disclosure requirement is applicable for prospective issuances of debt securities and for the residual maturity of ISINs already listed; the circular shall come into force with effect from August 18, 2025.

Meet the same qualification and certification requirements prescribed for full-time IAs.
Maintain arms-length separation, segregate IA services from other activities and avoid conflicts of interest.
Provide the required undertaking concerning arms-length separation and segregation.

effects.description: Clarifies eligible and ineligible outside activities for part-time IA registration.

commencement.raw_text: date of this circular

evidence.supporting_text: Part-time IA eligibility is defined by unrelated permitted work; equivalent IA qualifications/certifications, segregation, a minimum 10-font disclaimer for other services, disclosure of other activities and conflict avoidance are required; eligible professional examples are conditioned by Intermediaries Regulation 16A prohibitions.

effects.description: Establishes a single, comprehensive Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities, structured into four Parts (Objectives and Standards; Guidelines; Compliance Formats; Annexures and References) and graded across five RE-category tiers.

This framework supersedes 21 pre-existing SEBI cybersecurity circulars/guidelines (Table 1, R001-R021) and 22 cybersecurity-related letters/advisories to named MIIs/AMFI (Table 2, R022-R043), per the two-tier implementation glide path (January 1, 2025 for six categories with a pre-existing circular; April 1, 2025 for other REs).

events.title: Annual categorisation and highest-category rule
events.summary: Annual categorisation and highest-category rule.
events.position: Set the CSCRF category at the start of the financial year using the previous year’s data, retain it throughout that year and have it validated at compliance submission. Apply the highest category where multiple registrations exist. For CSCRF, the MII category includes KRAs and QRTAs. AIF AUM/VCF aggregate corpus thresholds are self below ₹100 crore, small ₹100–<500 crore, mid ₹500–<1,000 crore and qualified at least ₹1,000 crore. Brokers with up to 10,000 active UCC clients are self only without IBT/algo; with IBT/algo they are small; above 10,000–50,000 small, above 50,000–500,000 mid, above 500,000 qualified; QSB categorisation also applies. Custodian AUC is small below ₹1 lakh crore, mid ₹1–<10 lakh crore and qualified at least ₹10 lakh crore. Institutional DPs are qualified, other DPs mid; DDPs take the higher DP/custodian category. CIS, CRAs and non-excluded DTs are self; non-individual IAs small. Merchant bankers in conglomerate/systemically important groups are qualified, issue-management and the stated public-transaction activities mid, others small; listed merchant bankers also intimate exchanges. MF/AMC AUM is small below ₹10,000 crore, mid ₹10,000–<1 lakh crore, qualified at least ₹1 lakh crore. PMS is self below ₹1,000 crore, small ₹1,000–<3,000 crore, mid at least ₹3,000 crore. RTA folios are small 10,000–<1 crore, mid 1–<2 crore and QRTAs MII. Do not infer a QRTA threshold not stated here.

events.title: Excluded submission cohorts and special bank certificates

events.position: Individual IAs, FPIs, FVCIs, LPCCs, REITs, InvITs, vault managers, RTAs below 10,000 folios and DTs with no new listed-debt issuer client in the preceding three financial years are excluded from CSCRF compliance submission as stated. Exclusion from submission must not be expanded into an unqualified exemption from every substantive requirement.

events.position: Identify organisational context, dependencies and legal requirements. Leadership establishes cyber roles, resources and accountability; obtain confidentiality/integrity agreements before access and provide role-appropriate training. MIIs/qualified REs appoint a CISO reporting directly to MD/CEO at least at CTO/CIO level, with capability and timely incident communication; other categories designate a senior officer. CII-specific roles follow NCIIPC. Comply with relevant SEBI and government cyber/data/IT laws and permit regulatory audits, inspection and IT-resource access including vendor resources. SEBI’s inspection/search/seizure powers are regulator powers, not instructions to REs to conduct seizures. Guideline budget and employment-program suggestions remain recommendations, subject to mandatory parent standards.

events.title: Risk strategy, oversight and periodic risk assessment
events.summary: Risk strategy, oversight and periodic risk assessment.
events.position: Review risk strategy and performance; integrate cybersecurity with enterprise risk, set appetite/tolerance, maintain a risk register and test scenarios with IT oversight. Risk assessments are half-yearly for MIIs and annual for qualified/mid-size REs. Consider assets, vendors, privacy, quantum threats, likelihood and impact and prioritise responses. Detailed non-small/self guidelines include ISO 27005 guidance, detection/response/containment metrics, fraud monitoring and Annex E scenarios. Quantum measures are indicative: inventories and priorities, migration strategy, skills/policy/proof of concept, exploration of PQC/QKD and crypto agility; the source does not mandate implementation of every example.

events.title: Critical systems, hosted services and outsourcing responsibility
events.summary: Critical systems, hosted services and outsourcing responsibility.
events.position: Critical systems include core-impact and regulatory-data systems, connected devices, internet/client-facing and ancillary access/maintenance systems on premises or cloud. Maintain third-party identification, contracts, monitoring, joint recovery tests, concentration assessments and equal security standards. Hosted services require Tier-4-equivalent arrangements, cloud/audit equivalence, VAPT summaries, readable India copies where offshore, no kill switch and express contractual responsibility division. REs remain accountable for outsourced critical activities, background checks and NDAs. MIIs/qualified REs obtain vendor certifications where they lack control; MIIs remain responsible for NEAT/BOLT applications, not users. Non-small/self concentration reviews and exchanges’/depositories’ broker/DP vendor-concentration duties apply as stated. Annex F outsourcing and Annex J cloud circulars are referenced frameworks, not newly superseded instruments.

events.title: Identity, privilege, authentication and access logs
events.summary: Identity, privilege, authentication and access logs.
events.position: Maintain identity lifecycle, purpose/time/need-to-know access, least privilege, segregation, maker-checker, unique logs and physical/logical access policies; rank alone gives no access right. Revoke leavers/dormant/excess rights, lock failed logins and use MFA for untrusted access to trusted critical systems. Retain access logs at least two years, with six months online and the balance archived. Review access and privileged activity quarterly for MIIs/qualified and half-yearly for others. MII/qualified zero-trust and unused/delegated-token reviews are quarterly. Non-small/self requirements add privileged access management, password and internet controls, no alteration of own logs, network segmentation, web/email/DNS controls and allow-listing. All apply password complexity and deletion of unused generic IDs; more detailed password lifecycle/hash controls have the narrower applicability stated.

events.title: Endpoint, mobile and API controls
events.summary: Endpoint, mobile and API controls.
events.position: Apply endpoint protection/detection, signatures and intrusion prevention; disable PowerShell/local administrator access by default except authorised use, review directory backdoors, test priority weaknesses and control removable media. MII domain controllers are patched on release with quarterly review, minimal software/administrators and no direct Internet access. Secure APIs with discovery, authentication, rate/throttle controls, OWASP risks and allow-lists; MIIs are responsible for their APIs consumed by REs. Mandatory mobile clauses a–l cover root/cloak/emulator safeguards, qualified exploration of jailbreak blocking, device/network checks, anti-malware/tamper/runtime signatures and published checksum, screen/voice warnings, reauthentication, sensitive-data/memory/SQL/encrypted-database controls. events.title: Data protection, nonproduction separation and source-code assurance
events.summary: Data protection, nonproduction separation and source-code assurance.
events.position: Protect data at rest/transit, classify it, maintain availability and leak controls, separate production and nonproduction and preserve integrity. Non-small/self guidelines require encryption including cloud in-use controls and full-disk/file encryption where possible. Customer-app security and real-time capacity planning apply except self. All protect backups/PII, avoid sensitive client-side HTML/cookie storage, renew certificates and use migration-integrity SOPs. MIIs/qualified REs separate environments and tests, address OWASP/SANS weaknesses and obtain critical source code or equivalent escrow including patches, vulnerability SLAs, vendor assessment and support. DevSecOps remains recommended. Annex H/I measures are illustrative except valid TLS expressly required for Internet pages with sensitive information; preserve equivalent-control audit requirements.

events.title: Maintenance, remote working and severity-based patching
events.summary: Maintenance, remote working and severity-based patching.
events.position: Approve/log maintenance and remote access, assess vendor/remote risks and use severity-based OEM patches tested in an equivalent nonproduction environment before PDC/DR. Non-small/self remote-work controls include trusted devices, MAC/IP and host integrity and continuous alerts. Replace critical end-of-life/end-of-support systems; legacy virtual patching requires documented legitimate constraints and lasts at most six months. MIIs/qualified REs maintain an annually approved patch policy and quarterly compliance reports, test post-patch capacity and patch PDC/DR high severity within one week, moderate within two weeks and low within one month; emergencies follow the OEM clock.

events.title: VAPT scope, frequency and reporting
events.summary: VAPT scope, frequency and reporting.
events.position: Use CERT-In-empanelled auditors for VAPT of all critical infrastructure, network/security, servers, databases, applications, LAN/WAN/public IP and web resources, including precommissioning and connected critical systems. Protected/CII systems complete VAPT including closure/revalidation once each financial-year half; other REs undertake at least annual VAPT commencing in the first quarter. Category change must not create an audit gap. Submit the IT-approved report and MD/CEO declaration within one month of completion, close findings within three months of report submission and revalidate within five months of completion. Separately obtain committee approval for observations open three months after the activity and close before the next exercise; retain these distinct triggers. Qualified/mid brokers/DPs notify vendor and exchange/depository about vulnerable core COTS. Annex A captures RE/category/rationale, auditor/CERT/no-conflict declarations, approved exclusions, tools, scopes and VA/PT risk/closure summaries. The detailed URL/CVE/CWE/EPSS/SSVC/impact/remediation report is submitted only when SEBI seeks it. Annex L’s ten testing categories and technical method references define scope, not imported foreign law.

events.position: Audit 100% of critical and 25% of noncritical systems. MIIs/qualified REs and mid/small REs offering IBT/algo are audited at least twice yearly; remaining non-self REs annually. events.title: Audit formats, evidence and auditor independence
events.summary: Audit formats, evidence and auditor independence.
events.position: Use prescribed formats, signatory ownership declarations, committee minutes, scope/method/tools and control-level findings. Cover PDC/DR/NDR/colo/cloud/vendors and prior observations; record tests, risk/CIA, RCA, impact, management deadlines, exceptions, repeats over three audits and documentary evidence/version/samples. Correct similar configurations as well as the detected instance. Auditor must be CERT-In empanelled, have experienced resources and no conflict or auditee consulting in the preceding two years, use licensed VAPT tools and sign an NDA before audit; audit data and reports must never leave India. Three-year BFS/securities experience and certifications are preferences where stated. Explain criticality/sampling and NCIIPC-specific CII scope. Mandatory guidelines require implementation with evidenced deviations; nonmandatory guidelines must be audited for equivalent or stronger controls. Secure evidence with the RE and verify prior closure. Do not convert recommended external audit references into new legal frameworks.

events.title: Incident notification channels and clocks
events.summary: Incident notification channels and clocks.
events.position: Email SEBI and CERT-In about CERT-In-specified incidents within six hours of noticing, detecting or being brought to knowledge. events.title: Incident severity, regulatory review and forensic audit
events.summary: Incident severity, regulatory review and forensic audit.
events.position: Categorise incidents using the low/medium/high/critical examples; any operational or service impact must be high or critical. Severity here is separate from ANS importance. High/critical incidents at MII/qualified/mid REs go to HPSC-CS; other stated cohorts go to SEBI internal review. Reviewers may change severity, recommend remediation/timeframes and require implementation audit. Forensics is mandatory for all high/critical incidents, and for low/medium incidents where RCA is inconclusive or SEBI/HPSC directs. Submit forensic report at most 75 days from incident reporting, with issue-fixing timelines; closure follows IT review. Deficient reports may receive up to 15 additional days from deficiency notice at SEBI’s discretion; this is not an entitlement. events.title: Cyber Capability Index assessment and evidence
events.summary: Cyber Capability Index assessment and evidence.
events.position: MIIs obtain third-party CCI assessment half-yearly; qualified REs self-assess annually. Use the prescribed identity/category/rationale/period and signed ownership form; auditors verify MII implementation evidence. events.position: Use the signed report and five-domain weighted method, with zero denominators scored zero.
