updates.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) - Framework for Small and Medium REITs (SM REITs)
updates.summary: Non-binding SEBI FAQ (38 questions) explaining the SEBI (REIT) Regulations, 2014 framework for Small and Medium REITs (Chapter VIB): asset size, multi-scheme structure and segregation, SPV ownership, Investment Manager eligibility and fees, related-party-transaction bar, public issue and offer-document process, investment conditions, carried-interest prohibition, delisting/winding-up, change in control, migration of fractional real estate structures and exemptions, leverage and naming.

events.title: Non-binding FAQ clarifying the SEBI (REIT) Regulations framework for Small and Medium REITs
events.summary: Explains existing SM REIT provisions of the REIT Regulations; creates no new obligation and changes no rule.
events.position: The FAQ's plain-language explanations of the SM REIT framework (asset size, scheme structure, Investment Manager eligibility and fees, related-party bar, public issue, investment conditions, carried interest prohibition, delisting/winding-up, change in control, migration exemptions, leverage and naming), each expressly subject to the actual text of the Regulations.

parties.name: SM REITs and their schemes (each scheme holding real estate assets via wholly owned SPVs)
parties.scope: Subject of the framework being explained: reduced asset size (>= 50 cr, <= 500 cr per scheme), multi-scheme structure with segregation, SPV sole/direct ownership, 95% completed-revenue-generating investment condition, related-party-transaction bar, delisting/winding-up, minimum unit price and naming rules.

parties.name: Investment Manager of a SM REIT
parties.scope: Must be an India-incorporated company meeting Regulation 26J(2)(d) eligibility; discloses and (for changes) obtains unitholder approval for fees; segregates SM REIT activity; applies for delisting; undertakes migration; cannot transfer its own or related-party assets; carried interest not allowed.

parties.name: Trustee of a SM REIT
parties.scope: Together with the Investment Manager ensures segregation and ring-fencing of each scheme's assets and accounts; fee payment by the SM REIT to the Trustee for SM REIT activities is permitted.

parties.name: Unitholders of a scheme of a SM REIT
parties.scope: Approve changes in Investment Manager fees (>=1.5x threshold), extension of the no-asset delisting period, change in control / change of Investment Manager; each scheme has its own unitholders; minimum unit price rupees ten lakhs.

parties.name: Merchant banker associated with the SM REIT scheme public issue
parties.scope: Appointed for the public issue of scheme units through the stock-exchange platform; carries out marketing after the draft offer document is filed and made public; hosts the draft offer document for the 21-day comment period.

effects.description: Clarifies, on a non-binding basis, concepts and provisions of the SEBI (REIT) Regulations, 2014 relating to Small and Medium REITs - asset size, scheme structure and segregation, SPV ownership, Investment Manager eligibility and fees, related-party transactions, the public issue and offer-document process, investment conditions and expense ratio, carried interest, delisting and winding-up, change in control, migration of fractional real estate structures and the associated exemptions, leverage and naming.

transitions.affected_cohort: Existing fractional real estate persons, entities or structures in existence as on the date of notification of the SM REIT framework (8 March 2024), migrating into a SM REIT
transitions.condition: The applicant applies for registration within six months of the notification and completes migration within six months of the grant of registration
transitions.rule: As clarified by the FAQ, the Investment Manager's five per cent minimum unitholding requirement (for units issued against swapped securities allotted before 8 March 2024) and the Regulation 26P(2) asset-size and minimum-200-unitholder requirements do not apply to such migration.

evidence.supporting_text: Document titled 'Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) - Framework for Small and Medium REITs (SM REITs)', issued on June 18, 2024. Disclaimer: this is not a legal document; the FAQs offer only a simplistic explanation/clarification of terms/concepts related to the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 ('REIT Regulations') and should not be regarded as an interpretation of law nor a binding opinion/guidance from SEBI; for full particulars refer to the Acts/Regulations/Circulars on the SEBI website.

Existing REITs must have assets of at least rupees 500 crores; the SM REIT framework allows a reduced asset value of rupees 50 crores. A single SM REIT can launch multiple schemes (similar to mutual funds), each holding different real estate assets and each with its own set of unitholders, unlike the single-pool existing REIT structure.

Any company, including a real estate developer, that satisfies the Investment Manager eligibility conditions under Regulation 26J(2)(d) can act as the Investment Manager of a SM REIT; however, if a developer is the Investment Manager it cannot transfer its own assets to the SM REIT because the SM REIT framework does not permit related party transactions.

The REIT Regulations do not restrict who may be a tenant, but a SM REIT shall not enter into any transaction with related parties (term defined in Regulation 2(1)(zo)); a developer may be a tenant if not a related party. The Investment Manager may launch multiple schemes under a single SM REIT provided the assets, bank accounts, investment/demat accounts and books of accounts of each scheme are segregated and ring-fenced.

A 'scheme' is a distinct and separate scheme of a SM REIT for owning real estate assets through special purpose vehicles (SPVs), structurally similar to distinct schemes in a mutual fund, with segregation/ring-fencing of scheme assets and accounts. A single scheme can invest in multiple SPVs; each SPV must directly and solely own all assets acquired by the scheme of which it is a wholly owned subsidiary; multiple SPVs cannot jointly own a single property.

There is no limit on the number of real estate assets a single SPV can hold; the collective value of assets under a single scheme must be at least rupees fifty crores and not exceed rupees five hundred crores. Multiple schemes may exist under a SM REIT with no cap on the collective value of assets across schemes (e.g. three schemes of rupees 450 crores each, totalling rupees 1350 crores, is permitted).

For the purpose of SM REITs (Chapter VIB), the definition of 'SPV' under Regulation 26H(f) applies (per Regulation 26H). A SM REIT cannot acquire any asset from an entity within the definition of 'related party'; warehousing a property in a related entity of the Investment Manager, or an AIF Category II fund whose Investment Manager is a group company of the SM REIT's Investment Manager selling assets to the SM REIT, is not permitted.

There is no guideline capping the Investment Manager's fees as on the date of the FAQ; at the initial offer of the scheme the Investment Manager must disclose the fees charged to the scheme, and any change in the Investment Manager's fees requires unitholder approval where votes cast in favour are not less than one and a half times the votes cast against.

The Investment Manager must apply for delisting of the scheme's units if there are no projects or assets under the scheme for a period exceeding six months (extendable by a further six months with unitholder approval as specified in Regulation 26ZM); the scheme is subject to delisting and winding up if all assets are gradually sold and proceeds distributed. Prior approval of SEBI and of unitholders is required for a shareholding change in the Investment Manager amounting to a change in control ('change in control' defined in Regulation 2(1)(g)) and for any change in the Investment Manager by removal or otherwise.

The REIT Regulations do not restrict the shareholders or promoters of the Investment Manager, but the Investment Manager must be a company incorporated in India and meet the eligibility criteria, and its shareholding pattern and other prescribed details must be submitted to SEBI at the time of the registration application. The REIT Regulations do not envisage a separate distributor; the public issue of scheme units is made through the stock exchange platform with appointment of a merchant banker. The draft scheme offer document, once filed with SEBI, must be hosted for public comments on the websites of SEBI, designated stock exchanges and associated merchant bankers for a minimum period of twenty-one days; marketing by the merchant banker is permitted after the draft is filed and made public, and public communications must not be misleading.

The scheme offer document must disclose the total expense ratio; the REIT Regulations do not prescribe a threshold ratio of 'Other Expenses' to Asset Cost, nor a minimum cap rate (net rental yield), but the scheme must invest at least ninety-five per cent of the value of the scheme's assets in completed and revenue-generating properties. The Investment Manager must use the book building platform of the stock exchanges to accept bids; a fixed-price issue is not envisaged. Migration of existing fractional real estate structures is not mandatory if the structure does not fall within the REIT definition; an applicant must undertake due migration of existing structures and submit a migration plan with the registration application; the SM REIT's trademark, brand name, website and other communication media must be used exclusively for SM REIT activities.

The SM REIT's trademark, brand name and website must be used exclusively for the SM REIT and cannot be used for other SEBI-regulated entities such as an AIF. On migration, the Investment Manager's five per cent minimum unitholding is exempt for units issued against a swap of securities allotted prior to the notification of the SM REIT framework (March 08, 2024), subject to the applicant applying for registration within six months of the notification and completing migration within six months of the grant of registration; the Regulation 26P(2) asset-size and minimum-200-unitholder requirements are likewise not applicable to such migration. The REIT Regulations prescribe no approval threshold from existing security holders for migration, which must follow the extant legal and contractual rights (including drag-along, buy-back, buy-out or redemption).

The Investment Manager (or its group company) must segregate its SM REIT management activity from its other activities, and must have adequate infrastructure and sufficient key personnel; while doing other activities it must comply with the exclusive-use rule for the SM REIT's trademark, brand name, website and communication media. Performance-linked fees such as 'carried interest' are not allowed for SM REITs.

Any asset falling under 'infrastructure' cannot be treated as 'real estate' or 'property' for SM REIT purposes, so a warehousing facility classified as infrastructure cannot be held by a SM REIT unless it is common infrastructure forming part of composite real estate projects, industrial parks and SEZ. The scheme must invest at least ninety-five per cent of the value of its assets in completed and revenue-generating properties, with up to five per cent in unencumbered liquid assets; tenant security deposits do not form part of scheme assets; reserves created out of profits may be distributed; where reserves/other investments exceed five per cent the Investment Manager must reallocate to maintain the ninety-five per cent threshold. The total expense ratio encompasses all annual operating expenses, including management, advisory, trustee and audit fees, and must be disclosed in the scheme offer document.

Residential properties can be held by a SM REIT if they satisfy the definition of 'real estate'/'property' in Regulation 2(1)(zi) and are completed and revenue-generating; under-construction or non-revenue-generating properties and vacant land cannot be held. The Investment Manager may undertake facility and property management of SM REIT properties directly (or through appointed agents), but not through a related party; payment of fees by the SM REIT to the Investment Manager and Trustee for carrying out SM REIT activities is permitted.

The value of real estate assets in each scheme of a SM REIT must remain at least fifty crore rupees, and the Investment Manager must apply for delisting to SEBI and the stock exchanges if there are no assets under the scheme for a period exceeding six months (extendable by six months with unitholder approval). The minimum price of each unit of a scheme is rupees ten lakhs; on migration, existing structures must align investment value to multiples of rupees ten lakhs before migration, for example by inter-se sale/purchase, by SPV buy-back or redemption of a portion of existing securities, or by establishing a trust to consolidate odd-value units and dispose of them in the market within one year of migration, distributing net proceeds to the affected holders.

For convertible debentures issued by an existing SPV being migrated to a SM REIT, the applicant may convert them to equity of the SPV before migration; if not converted, they may be swapped for units of the scheme of SM REIT (which then holds the convertible debentures), and the existing debenture holders receive scheme units. Borrowings made by the SPV through convertible debentures held by the scheme of SM REIT are not included in the leverage limit under Regulation 26U(5), which applies at scheme level. An applicant seeking registration as a SM REIT may apply under a name that is not suggestive of Government of India patronage; the proposed name must not contain the words 'India', 'Indian', 'National' or 'Bharat' etc.

updates.title: Modification in Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism
updates.summary: Modification of the OFS-to-Employees framework so that employees place their T+1-day bids at the cut-off price of T day (rather than T+1 day), effective from the 30th day after issuance.

events.title: Employee OFS bids to be placed at cut-off price of T day (was T+1 day)
events.summary: The price reference for employee OFS bids shifts from the T+1-day cut-off to the T-day cut-off.
events.position: Employees shall place bids only at cut-off price of T day; the allotment price shall be based on the cut-off of the T day, subject to discount, if any. OFS to employees remains on T+1 day.

parties.name: Recognized Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Stock exchanges operating the OFS mechanism must implement the revised employee bid-price reference and related system changes.

parties.name: Recognized Clearing Corporations
parties.scope: Clearing corporations as MIIs directed to put systems in place and amend rules for implementation.

parties.name: Depositories
parties.scope: Depositories as MIIs directed to put systems in place and amend rules for implementation.

parties.name: Employees bidding in the OFS 'Employee' category
parties.scope: Employees bidding in an OFS: the price reference for their T+1-day bids changes from the T+1-day cut-off to the T-day cut-off.

actions.description: MIIs shall take necessary steps and put in place necessary systems for implementation and make necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations wherever required.
MIIs shall bring the provisions of this circular to the notice of market participants, including investors, and disseminate it on their website.

effects.description: Amends paragraph 5(vi) of the January 23, 2024 OFS-to-employees framework circular so that the employee bid price and allotment price reference is the T-day cut-off rather than the T+1-day cut-off.
effects.savings_or_limitations: All other provisions of the Master Circular (R001) and of the January 23, 2024 circular (R002) remain unchanged.

commencement.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall come into effect from 30th day of issuance of this circular.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI Master Circular SEBI/HO/MRD2/PoD-2/CIR/P/2023/171 dated October 16, 2023 (paragraph 19 of Chapter 1) specifies the OFS-through-stock-exchange framework; SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2024/6 dated January 23, 2024 issued the Framework for OFS of Shares to Employees, whose paragraph 5(i) creates an 'Employee' category with OFS on T+1 day and paragraph 5(vi) provides that employees shall place bids only at cut-off price of T+1 day with allotment price based on the retail-category cut-off, subject to discount.

Based on stakeholder feedback and deliberations in SEBI's Secondary Market Advisory Committee, it has been decided that employees shall place bids on T+1 day at cut-off price of T day; accordingly paragraph 5(vi) of the January 23, 2024 circular is to be read as: employees shall place bids only at cut-off price of T day, with allotment price based on the cut-off of the T day, subject to discount; all other provisions of the aforesaid circulars remain unchanged.

The provisions of this circular shall come into effect from the 30th day of issuance of this circular; all MIIs are advised to put systems in place, make necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations, and bring the circular to the notice of market participants; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018, Section 26(3) of the Depositories Act, 1996 and Regulation 97 of the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018.

updates.title: Framework for considering unaffected price for transactions upon confirmation of market rumour
updates.summary: SEBI prescribes the adjusted-VWAP method for computing an 'unaffected price' that listed entities must use for pricing-normed transactions (e.g. preferential issue / QIP) where a related market rumour is confirmed within 24 hours of a material price movement, phased across the top 100 (1 June 2024) and top 250 (1 December 2024) listed entities.

events.title: Framework for computing an 'unaffected price' (adjusted VWAP) for listed-entity transactions where a market rumour is confirmed
events.summary: Prescribes the previously-unspecified method for computing the 'unaffected price' contemplated by the second proviso to LODR Regulation 30(11), with a 24-hour confirmation condition and a 60/180-day applicability window, phased across the top 100 and top 250 listed entities.
events.position: Adjusted-VWAP methodology in the Annexure: exclude the WAP variation attributable to the material price movement and rumour confirmation from the daily WAP over the look-back period; apply the resulting unaffected price for 60 or 180 days (by transaction stage) from rumour confirmation to the relevant date; re-apply on each subsequent material rumour confirmation.

parties.name: Listed entities (equity-listed), phased by market-capitalisation ranking
parties.scope: Must verify market rumours on material price movement and, where a rumour on a pricing-normed transaction is confirmed within 24 hours, compute and apply the unaffected (adjusted-VWAP) price. Top 100 from 1 June 2024; top 250 from 1 December 2024.

parties.name: Recognised Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Issue the framework for material price movement on their websites, bring the circular to listed entities' notice and ensure compliance; transaction stages and the applicability period are to be set in Industry Standards on Regulation 30(11).

actions.description: Verify market rumours upon material price movement, per Regulation 30(11) of the LODR Regulations.

Where a rumour on a pricing-normed transaction is confirmed within 24 hours of the material-price-movement trigger, compute the unaffected (adjusted-VWAP) price per the Annexure and use it for the transaction pricing for the applicable 60- or 180-day period until the relevant date.
Issue the framework for material price movement on the exchange websites, bring this circular to the notice of listed entities and ensure its compliance.

effects.description: Operationalises the second proviso to Regulation 30(11) of the LODR Regulations by prescribing the adjusted-VWAP methodology, conditions and applicability window for the 'unaffected price'.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Applies only where the rumour was confirmed within 24 hours of the material-price-movement trigger and only to transactions on which SEBI or stock-exchange pricing norms apply.

effects.description: Introduces the requirement for listed entities to compute the unaffected (adjusted-VWAP) price and use it for pricing-normed transactions for 60 or 180 days from rumour confirmation (by transaction stage) until the relevant date, re-applied on each subsequent material rumour confirmation.
effects.savings_or_limitations: The precise transaction stages and the 60- vs 180-day period are to be specified in the Industry Standards on Regulation 30(11).

evidence.supporting_text: In terms of Regulation 30(11) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, as amended by SEBI (LODR) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024, a listed entity is required to verify market rumours upon material price movement; the stock exchanges shall issue the framework for material price movement on their websites.

As per the second proviso to Regulation 30(11) of LODR Regulations, unaffected price shall be considered for transactions on which pricing norms specified by SEBI or the stock exchanges are applicable, provided the rumour pertaining to such transaction has been confirmed within 24 hours from the trigger of material price movement. The unaffected price is to be considered by excluding the effect on the price of the equity shares due to the material price movement and confirmation of the rumour. The framework for considering unaffected price is placed as Annexure and shall be applicable to the top 100 listed entities with effect from June 01, 2024 and to the top 250 listed entities (i.e. the next top 150) with effect from December 01, 2024.
The Stock Exchanges are advised to bring the contents of this circular to the notice of their listed entities and ensure its compliance.

The adjusted volume weighted average price (VWAP) for the unaffected price is computed as follows: the variation in daily WAP from the day of material price movement till the end of the next trading day after confirmation of the rumour is attributed to the rumour and its confirmation (WAP variation); the adjusted daily WAP is calculated by excluding the WAP variation from the daily WAP in the look-back period from the day of the material price movement onwards; the adjusted daily WAP from the day of material price movement till the end of the next trading day after confirmation is set equal to the daily WAP on the trading day preceding the day of material price movement; and the adjusted VWAP for the look-back period is calculated from the adjusted daily WAP.

Illustration for calculation of VWAP for a preferential issue to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018: Table 1 tabulates trading day, daily WAP, adjusted daily WAP and shares traded, marking the date of material price movement, date of rumour confirmation, next trading day after confirmation, T-1 and the Relevant Date (T) being the date of board approval to the preferential issue to QIBs. The dates in the illustration (July/August) are a worked hypothetical, not operative dates.

The worked explanation: the WAP variation in the illustration is Rs. 118.14; the adjusted daily WAP from the day of material price movement until the end of the next trading day after confirmation equals the daily WAP on the preceding trading day (Rs. 1060.76); from the following day the adjusted daily WAP is the daily WAP minus the WAP variation; VWAP in the look-back period (T-1 to T-10) using daily WAP is Rs. 1,175.78 and using the adjusted daily WAP is Rs. 1,069.80.

If the price variation due to the rumour confirmation hits the price band limit on the next trading day post confirmation, the price variation in subsequent trading days is included for adjustment until the day the price does not hit the band limit.
The unaffected price applies only if the listed entity confirmed the rumour pertaining to the transaction within 24 hours from the trigger of material price movement.

evidence.locator: Annexure - paragraph 5 (applicability period by transaction stage)
evidence.supporting_text: The unaffected price applies for a period of 60 days or 180 days, as applicable based on the stage of the transaction, from the date of confirmation of the market rumour till the 'relevant date' under the existing regulations (public announcement, board approval, etc.). The stages of transaction and the applicability period of the unaffected price shall be specified in the Industry Standards on Regulation 30(11) of LODR Regulations.

Where a rumour pertaining to a transaction has been confirmed and a subsequent rumour with a material update requiring confirmation under Regulation 30(11) is reported in the mainstream media, the unaffected price applies for each instance of confirmation of the rumour.

evidence.locator: Annexure - paragraphs 6.1 to 6.3 and Table 2 (applicability illustration)
evidence.supporting_text: Worked illustration of applicability windows for successive rumour confirmations (60 days from each confirmation based on the stage of the transaction), with Table 2 showing which confirmation's unaffected price applies for various relevant-date ranges. The dates used are the illustration's hypothetical.

updates.title: Reduction of timeline for listing of shares in Public Issue from existing T+6 days to T+3 days
updates.summary: Reduction of the public-issue share listing timeline from T+6 to T+3 working days, with a revised end-to-end process timeline in the Annexure, offer-document and advertisement disclosure, SCSB and Registrar PAN-verification steps, investor compensation for delayed unblocking computed from T+3 day, and phased applicability (voluntary from September 1, 2023; mandatory from December 1, 2023).

events.title: Public-issue share listing timeline reduced from T+6 to T+3 working days (with phased applicability)
events.summary: Public-issue share listing must occur within T+3 working days instead of T+6, with a revised process timeline and PAN-verification steps, phased in over September-December 2023.
events.position: Listing within 3 working days (T+3 days); the Annexure prescribes the revised activity timeline; the T+3 timeline is disclosed in offer documents and advertisements; SCSBs and the Registrar perform PAN-match verification; investor compensation for delayed unblocking is computed from T+3 day; lock-in is operationalized per the Depositories' SOP dated August 08, 2023.

parties.name: Issuers making a public issue of specified securities
parties.scope: Issuers must disclose the T+3 listing timeline in offer documents and advertisements and comply with the revised public-issue process timeline.

parties.name: Registered Merchant Bankers (BRLMs) to the public issue
parties.scope: Merchant bankers manage the public issue against the compressed T+3 timeline and the bid-information / UPI reporting requirements.

parties.name: Recognized Stock Exchanges
parties.scope: Stock exchanges validate bid details, approve the basis of allotment and issue trading notices within the compressed timeline.

parties.name: Depositories
parties.scope: Depositories effect the corporate action for credit of shares and operationalize lock-in per their SOP within the T+3 timeline.

parties.name: Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
parties.scope: The Registrar undertakes third-party PAN verification (demat vs bank account), finalizes rejections and the basis of allotment within the compressed timeline.

parties.name: Self Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs) / Bankers to an Issue / Sponsor Banks
parties.scope: SCSBs perform the PAN-match check before blocking ASBA monies and submit final certificates; sponsor and issuer banks handle fund transfer and unblocking within the T+3 timeline.

parties.name: Applicants / investors in the public issue
parties.scope: Investors benefit from faster listing and from compensation for delayed unblocking of ASBA monies computed from T+3 day.

actions.description: The Issuer shall disclose the T+3 listing timeline in the offer documents and prominently in the pre-issue, issue-opening and issue-closing advertisements issued under the ICDR Regulations.

SCSBs shall verify that the PAN in the application matches the PAN linked to the applicant's bank account before blocking ASBA monies (with confirmation to the Registrar), and the Registrar shall undertake third-party PAN verification matching the demat-account PAN with the bank-account PAN, treating mismatches as invalid applications.

Stock exchanges, depositories, RTAs and banks shall put in place systems and processes to complete bid validation, basis-of-allotment finalization and approval, fund transfer and unblocking, corporate action for credit of shares, and listing/trading-notice filing within the compressed T+3 timeline set out in the Annexure.

effects.description: Reduces the post-issue-closure listing timeline for specified securities from T+6 working days to T+3 working days and prescribes the corresponding revised activity timeline.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Applies notwithstanding Schedule VI of the ICDR Regulations; phased applicability (voluntary from September 1, 2023; mandatory from December 1, 2023).

effects.description: Modifies the timelines prescribed in the seven earlier SEBI circulars (dated November 1, 2018; June 28, 2019; November 8, 2019; March 30, 2020; March 16, 2021; June 2, 2021; April 20, 2022) to the extent stated, and partially modifies the March 16, 2021 and April 20, 2022 circulars so that investor compensation for delayed unblocking is computed from T+3 day.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the timeline and compensation-computation aspects are modified.

effects.description: Introduces the SCSB PAN-match check before blocking ASBA monies (with confirmation to the Registrar) and the Registrar's third-party PAN verification (demat vs bank account), treating mismatches as invalid applications.

commencement.raw_text: Applicability is phased: on a voluntary basis for public issues opening on or after September 1, 2023 and mandatory for public issues opening on or after December 1, 2023; there is no single commencement date.

deadlines.obligation: The T+3 listing provisions may be adopted on a voluntary basis for public issues opening on or after this date.

timing.raw_text: On voluntary basis for public issues opening on or after September 1, 2023
conditions: voluntary adoption

deadlines.obligation: The T+3 listing provisions are mandatory for public issues opening on or after this date.

timing.raw_text: Mandatory for public issues opening on or after December 1, 2023

deadlines.obligation: Trading in the specified securities starts on T+3 day (T = issue closing date), per the Annexure indicative timeline.

conditions: indicative timeline in the Annexure

transitions.affected_cohort: Public issues opening between September 1, 2023 and December 1, 2023
transitions.condition: The public issue opens on or after September 1, 2023 but before December 1, 2023.
transitions.rule: The T+3 listing provisions apply on a voluntary basis; they become mandatory for public issues opening on or after December 1, 2023.

evidence.supporting_text: Following extensive consultation and public comments on a consultation paper, SEBI decides to reduce the time taken for listing of specified securities after the closure of a public issue to 3 working days (T+3), against the present 6 working days (T+6), 'T' being the issue closing date; the revised timelines for listing and the various public-issue-process activities are set out in the Annexure; the T+3 timeline shall be disclosed in the offer documents and prominently in the pre-issue, issue-opening and issue-closing advertisements issued by the Issuer under the ICDR Regulations, 2018.

For Direct Bank ASBA and Syndicate ASBA applications, prior to blocking application monies the SCSBs shall ensure the PAN in the application matches the PAN linked to the applicant's bank account (with a confirmation to the Registrar with the Final Certificate) and that this PAN is part of the bidding data on the Stock Exchange platform; the Registrar to an Issue shall undertake third-party verification by matching the PAN in the demat account with the PAN in the bank account, treating mismatches as invalid applications; lock-in of pre-issue shares shall be effected per the ICDR Regulations and operationalized per the Depositories' SOP dated August 08, 2023; in partial modification of circulars dated March 16, 2021 and April 20, 2022, investor compensation for delay in unblocking ASBA monies shall be computed from T+3 day.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 9-11 (applicability and modification of prior circulars)
evidence.supporting_text: Notwithstanding Schedule VI of the ICDR Regulations, the provisions of this circular are applicable on a voluntary basis for public issues opening on or after September 1, 2023 and mandatory for public issues opening on or after December 1, 2023; the timelines prescribed in SEBI circulars dated November 1, 2018, June 28, 2019, November 8, 2019, March 30, 2020, March 16, 2021, June 2, 2021 and April 20, 2022 stand modified to the extent stated in this circular; the circular is issued under sections 11 and 11A of the SEBI Act, 1992.

evidence.locator: Annexure - indicative timeline of activities for T+3 listing
evidence.supporting_text: The Annexure sets out an indicative timeline of public-issue activities for listing within T+3 days (T = issue closing date), covering application submission cut-offs, bid modification and validation, UPI mandate reconciliation and acceptance, issue closure times, third-party checks on UPI and non-UPI applications, submission of final certificates, finalization of basis and its approval by the Stock Exchange, fund-transfer and unblock instructions, corporate action for credit of shares, filing of the listing application and trading notice, publication of the allotment advertisement, and commencement of trading on T+3 day.

updates.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-Back of Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026
updates.summary: Amendments to the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018: merchant banker engagement made discretionary with obligation re-assignment (regulation 24A); ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during buy-back (regulation 24(i)(ea)); a <15% standalone-and-consolidated quantum limit and a four-/sixty-six-working-day open/close timeline for open-market buy-backs (regulations 4(iv)(b), 17); and a Companies-Act cooling-off, an MPS-breach prohibition, faster public announcement and electronic shareholder intimation, plus numerous drafting corrections (regulations 4(vii), 4(xi), 16, 22A and others). In force August 1, 2026.

topics.name: Minimum public shareholding / minimum public offer

events.title: Merchant banker engagement made discretionary for buy-backs; obligations re-assigned (new regulation 24A, Schedule V)
events.summary: Engaging a merchant banker for a buy-back is now optional; if not engaged, its obligations are re-assigned to named persons.
events.position: Notwithstanding anything in the regulations, engaging a merchant banker is discretionary for a company undertaking buy-back; if the company dispenses with the merchant banker it must ensure that the company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges and compliance officer undertake the specified obligations otherwise required of the merchant banker; consequential omissions are made in Schedule V.

parties.name: Merchant Bankers to a buy-back

parties.scope: Where a merchant banker is not engaged, specified obligations are re-assigned among the company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges and compliance officer per the regulation 24A table.

actions.description: A company undertaking a buy-back that dispenses with the merchant banker shall ensure that the persons specified in the regulation 24A table (company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges, compliance officer) undertake the obligations otherwise required to be undertaken by the merchant banker.

effects.description: Inserts a new regulation 24A and makes consequential omissions in Schedule V of the Buy-Back Regulations, 2018.
effects.savings_or_limitations: Where a merchant banker is not engaged, the merchant banker's obligations must be undertaken by the specified substitute persons.

effects.description: Removes the mandatory requirement to engage a merchant banker for a buy-back, making it a discretionary choice for the company.

commencement.raw_text: They shall come into force on August 1, 2026.

evidence.supporting_text: After the existing regulation 24, a new regulation 24A is inserted: notwithstanding anything in the regulations, engaging a merchant banker is discretionary for a company undertaking buy-back; if the company dispenses with the merchant banker, it must ensure that the persons in column 4 of the table (company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges, compliance officer) undertake the obligations otherwise required to be undertaken by the merchant banker (filing of letter of offer and public announcement, due-diligence certification, oversight of escrow accounts, VWAP and sell-order certification, presence at and verification of extinguishment, final report, funds/firm-financial-arrangement assurance, and Companies Act, 2013 compliance).

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.X (new regulation 24(i)(ea) - promoter-holding ISIN freeze) and 3.XII (Schedule V)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 24, after clause (e) of sub-regulation (i), a new clause (ea) is inserted: shares or other specified securities held by the promoter(s) and promoter group including their associates, for which buy-back is undertaken, shall remain frozen at the ISIN level during the period from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till the closing of the offer; the freeze does not apply for the limited purpose of tendering in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of encumbrances created prior to the commencement of the buy-back period may be allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to conditions specified by the Board; the company shall instruct the depositories to give effect to the freeze. In Schedule V, the words, numerals and symbols '8(i)(c),' and 'and 22(iv)' are omitted.

events.title: ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during buy-back (new regulation 24(i)(ea))
events.summary: Promoter and promoter-group holdings for which buy-back is undertaken must be frozen at ISIN level for the buy-back period.
events.position: Shares or other specified securities held by the promoter(s) and promoter group including their associates, for which buy-back is undertaken, shall remain frozen at the ISIN level from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till the closing of the offer, subject to the tender-offer and encumbrance-invocation carve-outs, with the company instructing the depositories to give effect to the freeze.

parties.name: Companies undertaking buy-back of shares or other specified securities
parties.scope: Companies undertaking a buy-back, whose obligations, quantitative limits, timelines, disclosure requirements and merchant-banker engagement are changed.

parties.name: Promoter(s) and promoter group (including associates) of the company undertaking buy-back
parties.scope: Promoter holdings for which buy-back is undertaken are frozen at ISIN level from the resolution date until closing of the offer, subject to the tender-offer and encumbrance carve-outs.

actions.description: The company shall provide the necessary instructions to the depositories to give effect to the ISIN-level freeze of the promoter and promoter-group holdings for which buy-back is undertaken.

effects.description: Inserts a new clause (ea) in regulation 24(i) of the Buy-Back Regulations, 2018 providing for an ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during the buy-back period.
effects.savings_or_limitations: The freeze does not apply for tendering in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of pre-buy-back encumbrances may be allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to Board-specified conditions.

effects.description: Requires promoter and promoter-group holdings for which buy-back is undertaken to be frozen at ISIN level from the resolution date until closing of the offer, and requires the company to instruct the depositories to give effect to the freeze.

commencement.raw_text: They shall come into force on August 1, 2026.

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.X (new regulation 24(i)(ea) - promoter-holding ISIN freeze) and 3.XII (Schedule V)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 24, after clause (e) of sub-regulation (i), a new clause (ea) is inserted: shares or other specified securities held by the promoter(s) and promoter group including their associates, for which buy-back is undertaken, shall remain frozen at the ISIN level during the period from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till the closing of the offer; the freeze does not apply for the limited purpose of tendering in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of encumbrances created prior to the commencement of the buy-back period may be allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to conditions specified by the Board; the company shall instruct the depositories to give effect to the freeze. In Schedule V, the words, numerals and symbols '8(i)(c),' and 'and 22(iv)' are omitted.

events.title: Open-market buy-back quantitative limit and offer timeline tightened (regulation 4(iv)(b), regulation 17)
events.summary: Open-market buy-backs are capped at <15% of paid-up capital and free reserves on both standalone and consolidated bases, and must open within four and close within sixty-six working days.
events.position: With effect from August 1, 2026, an open-market buy-back through the stock exchange shall be less than fifteen per cent of the paid-up capital and free reserves based on both standalone and consolidated financial statements; the earlier provisos apply only until July 31, 2026; regulation 17(i) is omitted; and a new regulation 17(iii) requires the offer to open within four working days from the public announcement and close within sixty-six working days from the date of opening.

parties.name: Companies undertaking buy-back of shares or other specified securities
parties.scope: Companies undertaking a buy-back, whose obligations, quantitative limits, timelines, disclosure requirements and merchant-banker engagement are changed.

actions.description: A company proposing an open-market buy-back through the stock exchange shall ensure the buy-back is less than fifteen per cent of its paid-up capital and free reserves, based on both standalone and consolidated financial statements.

effects.description: Amends regulation 4(iv)(b) (adding a time limit to the second proviso and a new third proviso) and regulation 17 (omitting sub-regulation (i), time-limiting the sub-regulation (ii) proviso and inserting a new sub-regulation (iii)).
effects.savings_or_limitations: The pre-existing proviso arrangements apply only until July 31, 2026; the new quantum limit and timeline apply with effect from August 1, 2026.

effects.description: Sets the open-market-through-stock-exchange buy-back quantum at less than fifteen per cent of paid-up capital and free reserves on both standalone and consolidated bases, and imposes a four-working-day open and sixty-six-working-day close window.

commencement.raw_text: with effect from August 1, 2026, the buy-back from the open market through the stock exchange shall be less than fifteen per cent ... ; They shall come into force on August 1, 2026.

deadlines.obligation: From August 1, 2026, an open-market buy-back offer shall open within four working days from the date of the public announcement.

conditions: with effect from August 1, 2026

conditions: with effect from August 1, 2026

transitions.condition: The pre-existing provisos (referencing April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2025) apply.
transitions.rule: Those provisos apply only until July 31, 2026; from August 1, 2026 the new <15% (standalone and consolidated) quantum limit and the four-/sixty-six-working-day open/close timeline apply.

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.I and 3.VI (open-market buy-back limit and timeline)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 4(iv)(b), in the second proviso, after 'April 1, 2025' the words 'till July 31, 2026' are inserted, and after that proviso a new third proviso is inserted: with effect from August 1, 2026, a buy-back from the open market through the stock exchange shall be less than fifteen per cent of the paid-up capital and free reserves of the company, based on both standalone and consolidated financial statements. In regulation 17, sub-regulation (i) is omitted; in the proviso to sub-regulation (ii) after 'March 31, 2025' the words 'till July 31, 2026' are inserted; and a new sub-regulation (iii) is inserted: with effect from August 1, 2026, a buy-back offer shall open within four working days from the date of the public announcement and close within sixty-six working days from the date of opening of the offer.

events.title: Buy-back cooling-off and MPS-breach prohibition, faster public announcement and shareholder intimation, and textual corrections (regulations 4(vii), 4(xi), 16, 22A and others)
events.summary: New cooling-off and MPS-breach prohibitions for buy-backs, faster public announcement and electronic shareholder intimation, plus drafting corrections.
events.position: A company shall not make any buy-back offer within the period prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 from the closure of the preceding offer; a company shall not propose a buy-back that results in the breach of the minimum public shareholding requirements under the SCRR, 1957 or the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015; the public announcement shall be made within two working days from the board resolution or postal-ballot result and shall contain the Schedule IV disclosures; and the company shall, within one working day from the public announcement, send an electronic intimation of the open-market buy-back offer to persons who were its shareholders as on the public-announcement date (regulation 16(iv)(ba) and regulation 22A(v)); numerous drafting corrections are also made.

topics.name: Minimum public shareholding / minimum public offer

parties.name: Companies undertaking buy-back of shares or other specified securities
parties.scope: Companies undertaking a buy-back, whose obligations, quantitative limits, timelines, disclosure requirements and merchant-banker engagement are changed.

The company shall make the public announcement within two working days from the date of passing of the board resolution or the date of declaration of the postal-ballot results for the special resolution, containing the Schedule IV disclosures.

The company shall not propose a buy-back that results in the breach of the minimum public shareholding requirements under the SCRR, 1957 or the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, and shall not make a buy-back offer within the Companies-Act-prescribed period from the closure of the preceding offer.

effects.description: Substitutes regulation 4(vii), inserts regulation 4(xi), substitutes regulation 16(iv)(b), inserts regulation 16(iv)(ba) and regulation 22A(v), and makes textual and grammatical amendments across regulations 8, 9, 11, 16, 20, 21 and 24.

Introduces a Companies-Act-linked cooling-off between successive buy-back offers, a prohibition on buy-backs that would breach minimum public shareholding, a two-working-day public-announcement deadline and a one-working-day electronic shareholder-intimation duty for open-market buy-backs.

Makes numerous small textual and grammatical corrections across regulations 8, 9, 11, 16, 20, 21 and 24 (marginal head) and revises the regulation 20(iv) bank-guarantee validity/return wording, without changing their substantive effect (regulation 20(ii) substitutes 'may' with 'shall').

timing.raw_text: within one working day from the date of public announcement

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.I (regulation 4(vii), 4(xi)) and 3.V/3.IX (regulation 16, 22A - public announcement and shareholder intimation)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 4, sub-regulation (vii) is substituted so that a company shall not make any offer of buy-back within such period as may be prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 from the date of closure of the preceding offer of buy-back; a new sub-regulation (xi) is inserted so that a company shall not propose any buy-back of shares or other specified securities that results in the breach of the minimum public shareholding requirements prescribed under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957 or specified under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. In regulation 16(iv), clause (b) is substituted so that the public announcement shall be made within two working days from the date of passing of the board resolution or the date of declaration of results of the postal ballot for special resolution, and a new clause (ba) is inserted requiring the company, within one working day from the date of the public announcement, to send an electronic intimation of the open-market buy-back offer to persons who were its shareholders as on the date of the public announcement; the same one-working-day electronic-intimation requirement is inserted as regulation 22A(v).

Regulations 8(i), 9(xi)(c)-(g), 11, 16, 20, 21(iii), 22A(i) and 24 (marginal head) are amended by numerous small textual and grammatical substitutions and insertions (for example changing 'until' to 'till', 'may' to 'shall', inserting connecting words, and marginal-head wording), that clarify and correct the drafting without changing the substantive effect of those provisions; regulation 20(ii) also substitutes 'may' with 'shall' and regulation 20(iv) revises the bank-guarantee validity and return wording.

updates.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
updates.summary: Amendment to the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 inserting regulation 9A, under which an employee identified as a promoter or promoter-group member in an IPO draft offer document may continue to hold and exercise pre-IPO scheme benefits granted at least one year before the draft offer document was filed.

events.title: New regulation 9A - promoter-identified employees may retain and exercise pre-IPO share benefits
events.summary: A new regulation 9A permits employees identified as promoters/promoter group in an IPO draft offer document to retain and exercise pre-IPO share-based benefits granted at least one year earlier.
events.position: An employee identified as a 'promoter' or part of the 'promoter group' in the draft offer document filed for an IPO, and granted options / SAR / any other benefit under any scheme at least one year prior to filing of the draft offer document, is eligible to continue to hold and/or exercise such benefits in accordance with their terms and subject to compliance with the SBEB Regulations and other applicable laws.

parties.name: Employee identified as a promoter or part of the promoter group in an IPO draft offer document
parties.scope: An employee so identified who was granted options / SAR / other benefit at least one year before filing of the draft offer document becomes eligible to continue to hold and/or exercise those benefits.

parties.name: Company filing a draft offer document with SEBI for an initial public offering
parties.scope: The issuer whose draft offer document identifies the employee as a promoter or promoter-group member; the eligibility rule applies in the context of its IPO scheme benefits.

actions.description: A promoter-identified employee may continue to hold and/or exercise pre-existing scheme benefits granted at least one year before the draft offer document filing, in accordance with their terms and subject to compliance with the SBEB Regulations and other applicable laws.

effects.description: Amends the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 by inserting a new regulation 9A after regulation 9.
effects.savings_or_limitations: The amendment inserts a new provision only; existing regulations are otherwise unaffected.

effects.description: Clarifies that a promoter-identified employee's pre-existing scheme options / SAR / other benefits, granted at least one year before the draft offer document was filed, may continue to be held and exercised, subject to their terms and to compliance with the regulations and other applicable laws.

commencement.raw_text: They shall come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
conditions: date of Gazette publication is 8th September, 2025

evidence.supporting_text: In exercise of the powers conferred by sections 11, 11A and 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with sections 54 and 62 of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules 8 and 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, the Board makes these regulations to amend the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021.

These regulations may be called the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 and shall come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

In the 2021 Regulations, after the existing regulation 9, a new regulation 9A is inserted: an employee who is identified as a 'promoter' or part of the 'promoter group' in the draft offer document filed by a company with the Board in relation to an initial public offering, and who was granted options, SAR or any other benefit under any scheme at least one year prior to filing of the draft offer document, shall be eligible to continue to hold and/or exercise such options, SAR or any other benefit, in accordance with its terms and subject to compliance with these regulations and other applicable laws.

updates.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025
updates.summary: Second amendment to the SBEB Regulations, 2021: regulation 34 valuation to be performed by an independent registered valuer (not a merchant banker), 'valuer' defined by reference to section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013, regulation 34(2)-(3) omitted, with a nine-month completion window for merchant bankers' pre-existing assignments; in force on the thirtieth day from Gazette publication.

events.title: Regulation 34 valuation to be done by an independent registered valuer; 'valuer' redefined; sub-regulations 34(2)-(3) omitted
events.summary: The regulation 34 valuation must be performed by an independent registered valuer instead of a merchant banker, 'valuer' is tied to section 247 of the Companies Act, and regulation 34(2)-(3) are omitted.
events.position: The valuation under regulation 34(1) is to be made by an independent registered valuer; 'valuer' has the meaning under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended from time to time; regulation 34(2) and (3) are omitted; a merchant banker must complete any ongoing pre-September 8, 2025 valuation assignment within nine months of the commencement of the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations.

parties.name: Companies undertaking valuation for share-based employee benefits / sweat equity under the SBEB Regulations
parties.scope: Companies that must obtain the regulation 34 valuation now from an independent registered valuer (as defined by section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013) rather than a merchant banker.

parties.name: Merchant bankers previously performing regulation 34 valuations
parties.scope: Merchant bankers are removed from the regulation 34 valuation function but must complete valuation assignments already undertaken before the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations came into force, within nine months of that commencement.

parties.name: Independent registered valuers (as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013)
parties.scope: Independent registered valuers become the persons who perform the regulation 34 valuation under the SBEB Regulations; no dedicated V1 entity tag corresponds to this role.

actions.description: The valuation required under regulation 34(1) of the SBEB Regulations shall be carried out by an independent registered valuer as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013.

effects.description: Amends the SBEB Regulations, 2021 by substituting the definition of 'valuer' in regulation 2(1)(ww), substituting 'a merchant banker' with 'an independent registered valuer' in regulation 34(1) and inserting a transitional proviso, and omitting regulation 34(2) and (3).
effects.savings_or_limitations: A merchant banker must complete a valuation assignment already undertaken before the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations came into force, within nine months of that commencement.

effects.description: Changes who performs the regulation 34 valuation for share-based employee benefits and sweat equity from a merchant banker to an independent registered valuer as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013.

commencement.raw_text: They shall come into force on the thirtieth day from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

deadlines.obligation: A merchant banker shall complete an ongoing regulation 34 valuation assignment undertaken prior to the coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025.

timing.raw_text: within a period of nine months from the date of coming into force of the said regulations
timing.anchor_event: coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
conditions: assignment undertaken before that commencement

transitions.affected_cohort: Merchant bankers with a regulation 34 valuation assignment undertaken before the coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
transitions.condition: The valuation assignment was undertaken prior to that commencement and is not yet complete.
transitions.rule: The merchant banker must complete that assignment within nine months from the date of coming into force of those regulations.

evidence.supporting_text: In exercise of the powers conferred by sections 11, 11A and 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with sections 54 and 62 of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules 8 and 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, the Board makes these regulations to amend the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021.

These regulations may be called the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 and shall come into force on the thirtieth day from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

In the 2021 Regulations, in regulation 2, sub-regulation (1), the existing clause (ww) is substituted so that 'valuer' shall have the same meaning as assigned to it under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended from time to time.

case_characterisation.allegation: That during two SEBI inspections of Jainam Broking Limited (IP1: 1 April 2021-30 September 2022; IP2: 1 November 2022-30 November 2023), the Noticee committed nine categories of non-compliance with SEBI/MIRSD circulars and the SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 1992: (i) misreporting margin utilised for credit-balance clients; (ii) funding clients beyond the T+2+5 debit-balance limit; (iii) delayed KYC/KRA registration for 13 clients; (iv) email/mobile-number mismatches between UCC and back-office records; (v) misreporting bank and client-ledger balances in weekly enhanced-supervision data; (vi) wrongly reporting AP/terminal user details for 11 terminals; (vii) misreporting brokerage income in risk-based-supervision data; (viii) non-compliance with prescribed cyber-security requirements; and (ix) using the client bank account for purposes other than those specified, contrary to client-fund segregation norms.
case_characterisation.finding_in_this_disposition: AO finds all nine violations established. No quantifiable gain or exact investor loss could be ascertained; this does not establish zero loss. Corrective steps, no complaint brought on record and prior penalty history were considered.
case_characterisation.disposition: By order dated 2 September 2026, the AO imposed an aggregate monetary penalty of Rs. 7,00,000 on the Noticee -- Rs. 5,00,000 under section 15HB of the SEBI Act and Rs. 2,00,000 under section 23D of the SCRA Act -- payable within 45 days of receipt of the order via SEBI's online payment portal, with recovery proceedings under section 28A of the SEBI Act and section 23JB of the SCRA Act available to SEBI on non-payment. Recovery is a conditional power on non-payment, not an order that attachment has already commenced.

evidence.supporting_text: Nine allegations were made against the Noticee in the SCN: (6.1) misuse of clients' funds -- incorrect Margin-utilised-for-Credit-Balance-Clients (MC) reporting, alleged violation of Clause 3.2 of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95; (6.2) client funding beyond T+2+5, alleged violation of Clause 2.6 of the same circular r/w Clause 2(d) of CIR/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2017/64; (6.3) KRA details not updated for 13 clients, alleged violation of Clause 2 of MIRSD/Cir-26/2011 r/w Clause 3 of MIRSD/Cir-23/2011 and Clause 3 of MIRSD/Cir-5/2012; (6.4) email/mobile-number mismatches between the UCC database and back-office records, alleged violation of Clause 2(B) of CIR/MIRSD/15/2011; (6.5) incorrect weekly enhanced-supervision reporting of bank and client-ledger balances as on 30.09.2022, alleged violation of Clause 3.2 of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95; (6.6) wrongly reported AP/terminal user details for 11 terminals, alleged violation of Clause A(5) of Schedule II r/w Regulation 9(f) of the Stock Brokers Regulations; (6.7) wrongly reported brokerage income in risk-based supervision, alleged violation of Clause 6.1.1.j of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95; (6.8) cyber-security non-compliance (no STQC certification, no VAPT plan/execution, not registered with CERT-IN, CISO details not shared, no SOC), alleged violation of Clauses 36 & 41 of Annexure-1 to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/CIR/PB/2018/147; (6.9) client bank account used for purposes other than specified, alleged violation of Clause 2.4.2 of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95 and clauses 15.4.4.2, 23.1.3 & 23.1.4 of Master Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/71.

evidence.extraction_note: All twenty-eight pages source-reviewed; funding, brokerage, gross-transfer and penalty tables visually checked.

The AO rejected the Noticee's methodology, institutional/inactive-client and unposted-charge explanations for most instances as unsubstantiated/not tenable (accepting only the explanation for one client, J43, as a technical non-inclusion with a correct underlying balance) and found a violation of Clause 3.2 of Annexure to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD2/CIR/P/2016/95.

evidence.supporting_text: Internal audit found the trading/back-office vendor lacked STQC certification, no VAPT plan/schedule or completed VAPT for all critical IT assets, no CERT-IN registration or shared CISO details, and no Security Operations Centre. The AO found a violation of Clauses 36 & 41 of Annexure-1 to SEBI/HO/MIRSD/CIR/PB/2018/147 dated 3 December 2018.

events.title: Alignment of SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal with the FSB's FIRE format and introduction of staged incident-lifecycle reporting

events.title: Introduction of the IT Resilience Index (ITRI) framework for MIIs
events.scope_description: SEBI introduces a system-driven IT Resilience Index for all stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories, with a parameter/weightage scheme, half-yearly computation and board reporting, an Early Warning System, continuous service-delivery monitoring systems, and a phased operationalisation timetable running to February 28, 2027.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular regulates the operations, governance and technology resilience of Market Infrastructure Institutions (stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories); this is intermediary/infrastructure regulation, i.e. Financial Regulatory (FR).

affected_entities.scope_note: Stock exchanges as Market Infrastructure Institutions required to compute ITRI, build the Early Warning System and service-delivery monitoring systems.
Clearing corporations as MIIs subject to the same ITRI computation, Early Warning System and monitoring obligations.

classification_support.reason: Every assigned tag maps to an express provision of the circular: FR/FR_MII_OPS/FR_MII_GOV and the MII entity tags to the addressees and the ITRI/EWS/monitoring obligations; the topic tags to the resilience, cyber, governance, risk, capacity and surveillance content; the framework families to the enabling power and the frameworks under which the addressee MIIs are regulated and directed to amend rules.

legal_effects.description: Creates the IT Resilience Index framework for MIIs, including the parameter/weightage scheme, the requirement of system-driven computation, and the requirement to build an Early Warning System and continuous service-delivery visibility systems.

Introduces new recurring obligations for MIIs to compute ITRI half-yearly within 60 days of each half-year end and to report the comparative analysis and corrective actions to their SCOT and Governing Board.

operative_change.summary: A new IT Resilience Index framework is stipulated for MIIs with system-driven half-yearly computation, board reporting, an Early Warning System and service-delivery monitoring, to be fully operationalised by February 28, 2027.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: MIIs must compute a system-driven ITRI measuring robustness of their Critical Systems across nine weighted parameters, on a half-yearly basis within 60 days of each half-year end, report comparative analysis and corrective actions to SCOT and the Governing Board, develop an Early Warning System, and build systems (including consolidated dashboards) giving continuous visibility into service delivery.

actions.description: MIIs shall build system-driven ITRI computation without manual intervention, an Early Warning System, and systems providing continuous visibility into service delivery to market participants including consolidated dashboards.

MIIs shall compute ITRI half-yearly within 60 days of each half-year end and submit the comparative analysis of two consecutive half-years and corrective actions to their Standing Committee on Technology and Governing Board; the first submission is for the half-year ending March 31, 2027.

MIIs shall provide insights to their Governing Boards on the overall health of IT systems, route manual-intervention exceptions through SCOT, and formulate SOPs for monitoring availability and continuity of service delivery.

effective_from.raw_text: The circular contains no express commencement clause; Section E prescribes a phased operationalisation timetable instead.

evidence.locator: Header; circular reference number and date
evidence.supporting_text: The document is a SEBI circular numbered HO/47/18/11(1)2026-MRD-TPD1/I/19509/2026 dated August 24, 2026, on the subject 'IT Resilience Index for Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs)'.

The circular is addressed to all Stock Exchanges, all Clearing Corporations and all Depositories (except AMC Repo Clearing Ltd.), and is issued in exercise of powers conferred under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 to protect investors and to develop and regulate the securities market.

IT systems of MIIs are the backbone of the securities market; MIIs must ensure availability, reliability, performance and cyber resilience of their IT systems; a framework for oversight of IT-system resilience, early identification of weaknesses and timely corrective measures has been formulated.

evidence.locator: Section B, paragraphs 4-5.2 including the ITRI parameter/weightage table
evidence.supporting_text: Pursuant to discussion with SEBI's Technical Advisory Committee and the consultation paper dated March 25, 2026, SEBI decides to create the IT Resilience Index (ITRI); a system-driven framework for computing ITRI is stipulated for MIIs; ITRI measures robustness of Critical Systems (as defined in the referenced Master Circulars) with parameters and weightages Availability 20, Security 20, Integrity 10, Governance 10, Reliability and Monitoring 10, Business Continuity 10, Modularity and Flexibility 10, Scalability 5, Others 5 (total 100).
The Industry Standards Forum (ISF) of MIIs constituted by SEBI shall finalize sub-parameters and detailed measurement criteria for each ITRI parameter by November 30, 2026.

MIIs shall compute ITRI on a half-yearly basis within a period of 60 days from the end of each half-year and submit the comparative analysis of two consecutive half-years and corrective actions taken or proposed to their Standing Committee on Technology (SCOT) and the Governing Board; computation of ITRI shall be system-driven without manual intervention, and any exception requiring manual retrieval requires prior discussion with SCOT.

The ISF shall formulate baseline parameters, acceptable threshold scores and the SOP for calculating ITRI with an objective system-driven scoring methodology for comparability across MIIs; the framework functions as a self-operating model requiring MIIs to periodically compute ITRI and provide insights to their Governing Boards.
MIIs shall develop an Early Warning System to detect possible deterioration in any ITRI parameter leading to possible performance issues and a framework to remedy these.

In addition to existing continuous performance monitoring, MIIs shall build systems providing continuous visibility into service delivery to market participants, including consolidated dashboards, and shall formulate SOPs to monitor availability of systems and continuity of service delivery and flag any disruption or deviation.

Implementation timeline: MIIs have already implemented the beta version of the ITRI framework; MIIs shall operationalize the ITRI framework including the Early Warning System and Real Time Monitoring of Service Delivery by February 28, 2027; the detailed SOP after finalization of sub-parameters by ISF shall be submitted to SEBI after review by SCOT by January 31, 2027; the first submission of ITRI computation shall be for the half-year ending March 31, 2027.

MIIs are required to take necessary steps to put in place systems for implementation, including necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations, if any; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992.
Issued by the Deputy General Manager, Division of Policy and Development - 4, Market Regulation Department, SEBI.

events.title: Amendment of the InvIT NDCF framework (Para 3.19) to permit add-back of debt-funded major maintenance expense for road projects, with Note 12 conditions
events.scope_description: Amends Section F (Para 3.19) of Chapter 3 of the Master Circular for InvITs. A new line item is added to the NDCF computation tables at both HoldCo/SPV level and Trust level to add back payments towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt (subject to new Note 12). Notes 4 and 6 are substituted so that surplus cash arising from such debt-funded major-maintenance payments may be distributed subject to Note 12 and disclosures, while otherwise no Trust/SPV may distribute cash flows obtained by external debt. New Note 12 sets the conditions: definitions of 'Road Project' (per the MoF notification of 19 September 2025) and 'Major maintenance expense'; prior unitholder approval under Regulation 22(5) (>=60% of votes cast) for each project; prescribed explanatory-statement disclosures; one-time or per-expense approval with fresh approval for deviations; a statutory auditor certificate (auditor may rely on an independent expert); and periodic disclosures in the financial results and Annual/Half-yearly/Quarterly reports (Net Borrowing Ratio segregation, NDCF-statement notes and debt-maturity-profile segregation). The circular comes into force with immediate effect.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular changes the InvIT distribution framework (Net Distributable Cash Flow computation at SPV/HoldCo and Trust level) and the related leverage and disclosure rules for InvITs, which is squarely CM trust-lifecycle (InvIT borrowing and distributions). evidence.supporting_text: Circular HO/17/11/17(5)2026-DDHS-POD2/I/18791/2026 dated August 14, 2026, issued by SEBI.
Addressed to All Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), All Parties to InvITs, All Depositories and All Recognized Stock Exchanges.
Subject: Framework for Calculation of Net Distributable Cash Flows for InvITs.

Section F (Para 3.19) titled 'Framework for calculation of Net Distributable Cash Flows (NDCFs)' of Chapter 3 of the Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) dated July 11, 2025 provides the framework for computation of NDCF for SPV/Holdco and InvIT.

On a request from an industry association to review the NDCF computation to allow addition of debt-funded major maintenance expenses, and based on recommendations of the Hybrid Securities Advisory Committee (HySAC) and public consultation, the following changes are made in Section F (Para 3.19) of Chapter 3 of the Master Circular for InvITs.

Under Para 3.19, in Table S.No. (I.) 'Computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow at HoldCo/SPV Level', a new line item is added to allow add back of payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt (shown as '(+) Payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external borrowing subject to Note 12 below').

Under Para 3.19, in Table S.No. (II.) 'Computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow at Trust Level', the same new line item is added to allow add back of payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt, subject to Note 12.

In S. No. (III.) 'Notes/Other Rules', Note No. 4 and Note No. 6 are substituted. Note 4 deals with surplus cash available in InvITs/HoldCos/SPVs (10% withheld NDCF; surplus in a newly acquired HoldCo/SPV; any other reason excluding surplus due to a debt raise) and provides that surplus cash on account of payments made for major maintenance expenditure for road projects to the extent funded by external debt may be distributed subject to the conditions in Note 12 and adequate disclosures. Substituted Note 6 provides that no Trust or SPV can distribute any cash flows by obtaining external debt, except to the extent clarified in Notes 2, 7 and 12 (excluding working capital / OD facilities obtained for treasury / working-capital purposes and squared off within the quarter).

A new Note 12 is added: any payments made towards major maintenance expense for road projects to the extent funded by external debt shall be added back subject to conditions - (i) 'Road Project' means a project in the 'Roads and bridges' infrastructure sub-sector as per the Ministry of Finance notification dated September 19, 2025 (including amendments/additions); (ii) 'Major maintenance expense' means non-routine maintenance expenditure on a road project in accordance with the obligations and requirements specified in the concession agreement; (iii) unitholder approval pursuant to Regulation 22(5) of the InvIT Regulations (votes cast in favour at least sixty per cent of total votes cast) shall be undertaken before adding back payments made for major maintenance expense for road projects funded by external borrowing, for each Project (whether held at InvIT or SPV/HoldCo level) for which the investment manager proposes to raise borrowing.

The explanatory statement to the notice convening the unitholder meeting shall disclose: (a) names and details of the projects/SPVs/Holdcos for which the major-maintenance debt is proposed or already raised (may be raised at Trust or SPV/HoldCo level); (b) categories of expenses treated as major maintenance; (c) indicative year-wise and project-wise estimates of the major-maintenance expenses per the latest valuation report; (d) possible impact on future growth potential of the InvIT (with a suggested disclaimer); (e) present and future impact on distributions to unitholders; (f) other funding alternatives if debt is not available in future.

(v) The unitholder approval may be taken on a one-time basis (for debt already availed or proposed for the entire project life cycle) or for a specific major maintenance expense; any deviation requiring additional debt from the previously approved proposal requires unitholder approval prior to availing the debt. (vi) A certificate of the statutory auditor shall be obtained certifying that the major maintenance expenses incurred are in line with the obligations and requirements stated under the concession agreements and that payments for such expenses are funded by external borrowings; only such auditor-certified payments will be allowed to be added back for NDCF calculation; the statutory auditor may rely on an independent expert.

(vii) Disclosures to be made as part of the financial results and the Annual, Half-yearly and Quarterly Reports of the InvIT: the Net Borrowing Ratio under Chapter 4 shall segregate the amount and percentage of borrowing taken for major maintenance expenses; the notes to the NDCF statement shall disclose, for each project/SPV/HoldCo and the InvIT, the aggregate borrowing raised in the period for major maintenance and the aggregate outstanding debt for major maintenance as on the date. (viii) The debt maturity profile required under the InvIT Regulations shall specifically segregate and highlight borrowing taken for major maintenance expenses.
This circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

Issued in exercise of powers under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 and Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014; issued with the approval of the competent authority.
Recognised stock exchanges are advised to disseminate the contents of the circular on their websites; the circular is available on the SEBI website under 'Legal Circulars'.
Signed by Ritesh Nandwani, Deputy General Manager, Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities.
