events.title: Expansion of the OBPP permissible product list (IFSCA-regulated products; 54EC bonds) with conduct and disclosure conditions
events.scope_description: SEBI modifies clause 5.2 of Chapter XXI of the NCS Master Circular so that OBPP platforms may also offer products/securities/services regulated by any financial sector regulator (SEBI, RBI, IRDAI, IFSCA, PFRDA) and bonds under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 or section 85 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, subject to conditions: separate-tab / other-platform offering, governance by the relevant regulator's directions, OBPP-specified grievance redressal, and for IFSCA products offering in the GIFT-IFSC stock-broker manner with FEMA/LRS compliance and international-instrument labelling; for 54EC bonds an issuer-not-SEBI grievance disclaimer and prescribed feature and purpose disclosures. Effective with immediate effect.

SEBI's November 09, 2022 notification prescribed the OBPP framework under Regulation 51A of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021, further streamlined by subsequent circulars; based on stakeholder suggestions, this circular modifies Chapter XXI of the NCS Master Circular dated October 15, 2025 to permit OBPPs to offer IFSCA-regulated products/securities/services, to permit offering of bonds issued under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 or section 85 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and to change compliance-officer requirements for OBPPs.

Clause 5.2 of the NCS Master Circular is modified so that the permissible list for OBPP platforms includes, in addition to existing items, products/securities/services regulated by a financial sector regulator (SEBI, RBI, IRDAI, IFSCA or PFRDA) and bonds issued under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 or section 85 of the Income-tax Act, 2025; for financial-sector-regulator products they may be offered under a separate tab or other platform, are governed by that regulator's directions, require an OBPP-specified grievance-redressal mechanism, and for IFSCA products must be offered in the manner specified for SEBI-registered stock brokers operating within GIFT-IFSC in compliance with FEMA (including Overseas Investment Rules and LRS limits) and clearly labelled as international/overseas instruments; for 54EC bonds the OBPP must give a disclaimer that grievance redressal lies with the issuer and not SEBI, disclose the features (eligible issuers, lock-in, investment limit, non-transferability, tax features, application size, LODR listing-requirement exemption) and prominently disclose that the instruments are intended for investors seeking the associated tax benefits.

Clause 1.1 of Annexure-XXIA of the NCS Master Circular is modified so that the OBPP entity has appointed a Compliance officer as per the SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 2026, who shall comply with the certification requirement (NISM-Series-III-A: Securities Intermediaries Compliance (Non-Fund) Certification Examination) for stock brokers; the footnote records that the earlier provision required appointment of a Company Secretary as compliance officer.

All other provisions of the NCS Master Circular remain unchanged; the circular shall come into force with immediate effect; the Stock Exchanges are directed to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations and bring the circular to the notice of stock brokers; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 55(1) of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021; issued by the General Manager, Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities, SEBI.

events.title: Reduction of the stress-testing Z-score threshold from 10 to 5 (commodity derivatives)
events.scope_description: SEBI amends Part A (Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O of the Master Circular for the Commodity Derivatives Segment so that, in the Peak Historical Return standardized stress-testing scenario, price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 (rather than 10) replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities; the change takes immediate effect.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular changes a risk-management parameter (stress-testing Z-score) used by clearing corporations for the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in the commodity derivatives segment - infrastructure risk-management regulation within the Financial Regulatory (FR) practice.

affected_entities.scope_note: Clearing corporations that conduct standardized stress testing for their Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in the commodity derivatives segment and must apply the revised Z-score threshold.

legal_effects.description: Amends Part A (Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O of the Master Circular for the Commodity Derivatives Segment, replacing the Z-score threshold of 10 with 5 for capping extreme price movements in peak historical returns.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the Z-score value in Part A of paragraph 22 of Annexure O is changed; the mean-and-sigma methodology and the 15-year MPOR window are unchanged.

legal_effects.description: Lowers the Z-score cap applied in peak-historical-return stress testing, reducing the severity of the historical stress scenario, stated to be for the objective of facilitating Ease of Doing Business.

operative_change.summary: The Z-score threshold used to cap extreme price movements in peak-historical-return stress testing for commodity derivatives is reduced from 10 to 5.

operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities; mean and sigma of returns over the applicable MPOR period across 15 years are still used for the Z-score calculation.

actions.description: Clearing corporations having a commodity derivatives segment shall apply a Z-score of 5 (instead of 10) when capping extreme price movements in peak-historical-return standardized stress testing for the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund.

effective_from.raw_text: The circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

operative_status.reason: As issued on August 12, 2026 the circular is stated to come into force with immediate effect.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Amendment confined to Part A (Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O.

notification.importance_reason: A single, narrowly scoped change to one risk-management parameter used by a small set of clearing corporations; it changes a stress-testing calculation but imposes no new process or deadline.

confidence.reason: Both the old and new text of the amended provision are reproduced verbatim in the circular and the change takes immediate effect.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/47/16/14(1)2026-MRD-POD1/I/18580/2026 dated August 12, 2026, addressed to the Managing Directors / CEOs of all Recognised Clearing Corporations having a Commodity Derivatives Segment, on 'Review of Inclusion of Historical Scenarios in Stress Testing for Commodity Derivatives Segment'.

The SEBI Master Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/136 for Commodity Derivatives Segment dated August 04, 2023 prescribes Core Settlement Guarantee Fund norms; paragraph 22 of Annexure O, Part A (Historical Scenarios, Peak Historical Return) currently provides that price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 10 will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities.

Based on stakeholder representations, the recommendation of the Risk Management Review Committee and public comments, and with the objective of facilitating Ease of Doing Business, SEBI modifies Part A (with respect to Z-score) of paragraph 22 of Annexure O so that price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 (instead of 10) will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities.

The circular shall come into force with immediate effect; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018, and with the approval of the competent authority.
Issued by the Deputy General Manager, Market Regulation Department, SEBI.

events.title: Specification of face value denominations for privately placed municipal debt securities under Regulation 22 of the ILMDS Regulations
events.scope_description: Pursuant to Regulation 22 of the ILMDS Regulations (which delegates to the Board the manner of face-value disclosure), specifies that privately placed municipal debt securities may have a face value of Rs. 1,00,000 or Rs. 10,000; a Rs. 10,000-denomination security must have fixed maturity and no structured obligations; and the exchange-traded lot must equal the face value. Applies only to privately placed municipal debt securities, not public issues.

evidence.supporting_text: Circular No. HO/17/11/24(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/18526/2026 dated August 11, 2026, addressed to all issuers who have listed/propose to list municipal debt securities, all Recognized Stock Exchanges, all Recognized Depositories and all Registered Merchant Bankers. Subject: Amendment to SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) Regulations, 2015 ('ILMDS Regulations').
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI constituted a Working Group in August 2024 on the regulatory framework for municipal debt securities. Based on its recommendations and public comments, amendments to the ILMDS Regulations were notified vide Gazette Notification SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2026/305 dated July 8, 2026 (the 'SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026'). Further changes to the extant framework in respect of certain operational aspects are being specified through this circular.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Paragraph 2 (face value of municipal debt securities)
evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 22 of the ILMDS Regulations requires face value to be disclosed 'in the manner as specified by the Board'. Accordingly, for municipal debt securities issued on private placement basis: (i) face value shall be Rs. 1,00,000 or Rs. 10,000, as deemed fit; (ii) a security issued at Rs. 10,000 face value shall have fixed maturity and no structured obligations; (iii) the exchange-traded lot of such a listed security shall always equal its face value; (iv) these face-value requirements apply only to privately placed municipal debt securities, not public issues.
evidence.extraction_note: Clause crosses the page boundary and header; supporting text source-reviewed across pages 1–2, not asserted as a contiguous extracted quote.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/CIR/P/134/2019 dated November 13, 2019 (the 'Circular') specifies the escrow payment mechanism for municipal debt issuers. Where the listed entity is a pooled finance vehicle/Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) set up under the Government's Pooled Finance Development Fund Scheme, a 'two-step escrow account mechanism' shall ensure timely repayment to investors. New paragraphs 4.1.5 and 4.1.6 are inserted into the Circular after paragraph 4.1.4.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: New paragraph 4.1.5: where the listed entity is a pooled finance vehicle/SPV under the Pooled Finance Development Fund Scheme, the constituent municipalities must create all the escrow-related accounts and comply with the applicable requirements. The SPV/pooled finance vehicle must additionally maintain its own 'Interest payment account' and 'Sinking fund account', funded by transfers from the constituent municipalities' corresponding accounts per their inter-se agreement, and must maintain an amount equal to one year's interest obligation in its Interest payment account throughout the securities' tenure.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: New paragraph 4.1.6: the SPV/pooled finance vehicle may include forms of credit enhancement -- additional cash collateral; program equity by the state government; access to state finance commission devolutions to ULBs; full/partial credit guarantee from a high-rated DFI or multilateral institution; or any other appropriate credit-enhancement structure -- to enhance credit rating and investor protection.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: The 2019 Circular's paragraphs 2.1.1(a) and 2.1.2(a) previously required listed municipal-debt entities to submit half-yearly unaudited financial results within 45 days of the end of the first half-year, and annual audited financial results (with audit report) within 60 days of the financial year end. Considering the practical challenges municipalities face in data collection, interdepartmental coordination and meeting disclosure requirements, these timelines are relaxed: first-half-year unaudited results must now be prepared and submitted as soon as available, within 60 days of the end of the first half year, and annual audited results within 90 days of the financial year end.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: The provisions of this circular are applicable with immediate effect. The circular is issued in exercise of powers under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 29 of the ILMDS Regulations, 2015. It is available on www.sebi.gov.in under 'Legal -> Circulars'.
evidence.quote: The provisions of this circular shall be applicable with immediate effect.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: If FPI position remains at close of T-1, execute system transfer after market close before clearing EOD at exchange closing/daily settlement price to designated TM/TCM proprietary account. evidence.supporting_text: Consultation paper seeking stakeholder views on two proposals: (1.1) FPI participation in non-agricultural index derivatives contracts, and (1.2) FPI participation in non-cash settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives contracts.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI previously permitted Cat-III AIFs, MFs and PMS in ETCDs (2017/2019 circulars); the SEBI Board decided on 29 June 2022 to allow FPI participation, implemented via a September 2022 circular now folded into the Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives Segment (SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/136 dated 4 August 2023). Para 4.2.2(i) of that Master Circular currently limits FPIs to cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts and indices comprising such commodities.
evidence.quote: To begin with, FPIs will be allowed to participate in cash settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts and indices comprising such non-agricultural commodities.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Currently FPIs may trade only cash-settled non-agri derivative contracts whose underlying is also cash-settled. Since index derivatives are always cash-settled regardless of the underlying, SEBI proposes allowing FPIs to trade non-agri index derivatives irrespective of whether the underlying is cash-settled. The CDAC agreed and recommended the proposal.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: FPI participation has boosted crude oil/natural gas options liquidity. Internationally (Japan OSE/TOCOM, China QFIs, US CME, EU ICE) foreign investors trade physically settled commodity derivatives with delivery-capacity safeguards. In India FPIs cannot take/make delivery (no permanent establishment; GST-registration burden even via a delegated TM), so SEBI proposes permitting non-cash based non-agri derivative trading conditional on FPIs squaring off/rolling over before the tender period.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: FPIs may take positions in non-cash non-agri commodity derivatives, compulsorily squaring off/rolling over by T-3 (close of market hours); if not done voluntarily by T-1, the position devolves automatically post-close on T-1 to the designated TM/TCM's proprietary account at Closing/Daily Settlement Price via a pre-agreed tripartite (FPI-PCM-TM) or bipartite (FPI-TCM) agreement, treated as a Normal Market trade (attracting SEBI turnover fees, CTT, stamp duty, GST); PCM informs the TM of the open position by T-2 EOD for margin arrangement; no fresh FPI position increase is allowed on T-1 in the near-month contract; the TM/TCM gets up to T+2 trading days to reduce any resulting position-limit breach; a Proprietary Risk Absorption Charge, disclosed at onboarding, may be levied on the FPI for the involuntary transfer, without prejudice to other position-limit penalties.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.locator: Flowchart of the proposed safeguard mechanism
evidence.supporting_text: Flowchart depicts T-3 decision, T-2 PCM notice, T-1 position restriction and EOD transfer, tender start then TM two-trading-day reduction; the draft/body caveats are separately recorded.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Day-wise indicative timeline of the safeguard mechanism from T-3 (voluntary exit window opens) through T-2 EOD (PCM informs TM), T-1 (no fresh position increase; then EOD cut-off transfer at closing price), start of Tender period (T), to T to T+2 (TM permitted to reduce transferred position in excess of limits).
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: The CDAC agreed with Proposal 2, subject to the proposed safeguards preventing delivery obligation on FPIs. Views are sought on paras 3.4 (Proposal 1), 4.18 (whether to allow Proposal 2) and 4.19 (agreement with the proposed safeguard framework).
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: A draft circular modifying Para 4.2 of Chapter 4 of the Master Circular (dated 4 August 2023) is at Annexure-A. Comments on paras 3.4, 4.18, 4.19 and Annexure-A are invited via SEBI's online public-comments form, to be submitted by 1 September 2026. Issued on 11 August 2026.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Draft circular (Ref. HO/47/16/13(17)2026-MRD-POD1, date shown as placeholder '#IssuedDate#') would revise Para 4.2.2(i) to exclude deliverable options and insert 4.2.2(i)(a)-(c) (FPIs may trade deliverable commodity contracts up to the start of the tender/staggered-delivery period and must unwind before it; no fresh near-month position increase on the day before tender-period start; the pre-tender FPI-to-TM transfer is deemed a Trade, not an OTC derivative or a client-code/error-account/off-market transfer, for levy purposes); insert Para 4.2.2(iii)(c) (up to two trading days for the TM to bring an over-limit proprietary position within limits); and insert new Para 4.2.3 'Operational Framework for FPI Participation in Non-Cash Settled Contracts' setting out onboarding (tripartite/bipartite agreement, TM/TCM choice granularity, Exchange notification), the voluntary square-off/rollover primary obligation, the compulsory safeguard mechanism (T-3/T-2/T-1 mechanics, Closing Price transfer, Normal Market trade treatment), post-transfer position-limit reduction (up to two trading days, no penal action under Annexure J solely for the transfer), and the Proprietary Risk Absorption Charge (disclosed at onboarding).
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Exchanges must standardise the onboarding agreement's format/terms and notify a detailed post-closure-window scheme; the draft circular states it 'shall come into force from DD/MM/YYYY' (placeholder, not yet fixed); MIIs must implement systems, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations as needed, and publicise the circular; it would be issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SEBI (SECC) Regulations, 2018, with the approval of the competent authority.
evidence.quote: The circular shall come into force from DD/MM/YYYY.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Before trading, execute PCM/TM/FPI tripartite or TCM/FPI bipartite agreement as applicable. FPI may choose one TM/TCM across exchanges/commodities, per exchange or per commodity/group within an exchange. TM/CM informs exchange/clearing corporation of the arrangement before permitting trading. Exchange enables FPI trading only after arrangement confirmation.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed voluntary square-off/rollover remains available through close of T-1; absence of exit at T-3 activates safeguard preparation. Do not replace the T-1 exit opportunity with an absolute T-3 last exit date. PCM informs designated TM of open positions by end of T-2 to arrange margin. Clearing member must not accept/clear trades increasing FPI near-month deliverable open positions on T-1; indicative table also identifies the trading member. If FPI position remains at close of T-1, execute system transfer after market close before clearing EOD at exchange closing/daily settlement price to designated TM/TCM proprietary account. After transfer, all position rights, obligations and delivery exposure vest solely in TM/TCM; FPI exposure is extinguished. Treat transfer as normal market trade attracting exchange charges, SEBI turnover fee, CTT, stamp duty and GST on turnover charges. Draft says special transfer is not OTC and excludes specified client-code/error-account/off-market transfer rules, notwithstanding the named master circulars.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

evidence.supporting_text: Reduce transfer-caused excess proprietary positions within the proposed up-to-two-trading-day allowance. Source body anchors at tender start; draft 4.2.3(iv) anchors at transfer date. These are not silently reconciled. Draft permits up to two trading days; within that period, excess solely caused by the transfer would not attract Annexure J penalty. Other extant penalties are not waived. Agreement may include a pre-agreed risk absorption charge in addition to transfer service fees for involuntary transfer; charge is optional, not automatically payable by every FPI. If used, disclose and agree quantum/computation at onboarding, without prejudice to other penalties. Exchange would prescribe conditions for collecting the charge. Commodity exchanges would agree standard onboarding format/material terms; exchange/CC would notify detailed post-close window guidelines. MIIs would implement systems and amend relevant bye-laws/rules where required. MIIs would inform market participants and disseminate on websites. Draft effective date remains DD/MM/YYYY.
evidence.extraction_note: All fourteen pages reviewed, including the rendered page 7 flowchart and page 8 table.

events.title: Revision of MF Master Circular paragraph 21.10: new NISM Series-V-D certification for SIF distribution, sunset of NISM Series XIII requirement with transitional savings
events.scope_description: Amends paragraph 21.10 of the MF Master Circular (SIF/MF distribution certification): introduces a mandatory 'NISM Series-V-D' certification for persons distributing SIF products (also covering MF distribution without a separate 'NISM Series V-A'); leaves the existing 'NISM Series V-A' requirement for MF-only distributors unchanged; sunsets the prior 'NISM Series XIII' requirement for SIF distribution after 21 September 2026, subject to a cohort-specific transitional/savings provision for existing valid NISM Series XIII holders; and assigns AMFI and AMCs a duty to ensure distributor/agent compliance. Takes immediate effect.

classification.practice_rationale: AF (Asset Management and Funds) via AF_MF_OPS ('Operations, distribution and investor servicing'), whose own definition explicitly includes 'distribution' within MF/SIF operations -- an exact match, since this circular amends the MF Master Circular's distribution-certification paragraph. Not FR: this is not a change to the intermediary registration regime (FR_INTERMED) itself, but to a distribution-channel certification requirement embedded in the MF/SIF operational framework.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Persons/entities distributing SIF and/or Mutual Fund products (distributors and agents)
affected_entities.scope_note: The direct subject of the certification requirement: persons/entities employed or engaged in the sale/distribution of SIF products (new NISM Series-V-D requirement) and, separately, those distributing only Mutual Fund products (continuing NISM Series V-A requirement, unchanged).
Explicitly assigned a duty (with AMFI) to ensure compliance with the certification requirements by distributors and agents (paragraph 21.10.5).
MF addressee; no separate duty is imposed on the fund vehicle. Paragraph 21.10.5 expressly names AMCs and AMFI.

affected_entities.scope_note: Named addressee of the circular; no RTA-specific operative duty is stated in the body text beyond being addressed.

affected_entities.scope_note: Industry self-regulatory association explicitly assigned (with AMCs) a duty to ensure compliance with the certification requirements by distributors and agents (paragraph 21.10.5). No entity_type or role tag in the v1.1 taxonomy corresponds to a mutual-fund self-regulatory/industry association; left untagged rather than forcing an ill-fitting tag (see uncertainty U001).

affected_instruments.description: Units of Mutual Fund schemes and Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs), the latter structured under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 and distributed subject to the certification requirements addressed by this circular.

legal_effects.description: Modifies paragraph 21.10 of the MF Master Circular dated 20 March 2026, restating the certification requirements for SIF/MF distribution.

Introduces a new mandatory 'NISM Series-V-D - Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors Certification' for any person distributing SIF products, which also qualifies the holder to distribute Mutual Fund products without separately holding NISM Series V-A.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Subject to paragraph 21.10.4: qualifying Series XIII holders are exempt from Series-V-D until their existing certificate expires and must keep valid Series V-A during that period.

legal_effects.description: Removes the prior requirement of holding 'NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification' for SIF distribution, effective after 21 September 2026, subject to the transitional savings provision for existing valid certificate holders.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Paragraph 21.10.4 preserves the position of distributors holding a valid NISM Series XIII certification obtained on or before 21 September 2026 until that certification's own expiry.

operative_change.summary: Replaces the SIF-distribution certification pathway (previously 'NISM Series XIII') with a dedicated 'NISM Series-V-D' certification that also covers MF distribution, while leaving the MF-only 'NISM Series V-A' pathway unchanged and providing a cohort-specific transition for existing NISM Series XIII holders.
operative_change.previous_position: Paragraph 21.10 of the MF Master Circular required holding of 'NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification' (in addition to NISM Series V-A) for the sale/distribution of SIF products; MF-only distribution required NISM Series V-A alone.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: SIF distribution now requires a dedicated 'NISM Series-V-D' certification (which also covers MF distribution); the NISM Series XIII pathway for SIF distribution ceases to apply after 21 September 2026, subject to a savings provision for existing valid Series XIII holders until their certification's expiry; MF-only distribution continues to require NISM Series V-A, unchanged.

actions.description: Hold valid NISM Series-V-D for SIF distribution, subject to paragraph 21.10.4: qualifying valid Series XIII obtained on/before 21 September 2026 remains usable until its expiry with continuing valid Series V-A.
Continue to hold a valid 'NISM Series V-A - Mutual Fund Distributors Certification' where distributing only Mutual Fund products (unchanged requirement).
Ensure compliance with the revised certification requirements by distributors and agents.
Distributors relying on grandfathered valid Series XIII obtained on/before 21 September 2026 must continue to hold valid Series V-A during the saved period until their Series XIII expiry.

effective_from.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

transitional_provisions.affected_cohort: SIF distributors holding a valid 'NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification' obtained on or before 21 September 2026
transitional_provisions.condition: Their existing NISM Series XIII certification remains valid and unexpired.
transitional_provisions.rule: Not required to obtain the 'NISM Series-V-D' certification until expiry of their existing NISM Series XIII certification, provided they continue to hold a valid 'NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors Certification' during that period.

operative_status.reason: The circular's core requirements take immediate effect, but a cohort-specific transitional/savings mechanism (paragraph 21.10.4) governs existing NISM Series XIII certificate holders until the expiry of their existing certification, making OS_TRANSITIONAL more precise than a simple OS_OPERATIVE for this event.

events.title: Operational framework for the ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings during buy-back
events.scope_description: SEBI operationalises Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the Buy-back Regulations by directing the depositories to build an operational framework and system enhancements for freezing promoter and promoter-group holdings at ISIN level from the buy-back resolution date until closing of the offer, with carve-outs for tendering in tender-offer buy-backs and for invocation of pre-buy-back encumbrances, and by requiring listed companies, exchanges, merchant bankers and RTAs to comply.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular operationalises a buy-back regulation (control-transaction / capital-return regulation, i.e. Corporate practice CO); it also imposes operational and system duties on depositories, stock exchanges, merchant bankers and RTAs, giving a Financial Regulatory (FR) secondary workflow.

affected_entities.scope_note: Listed companies must issue freezing instructions to depositories in the prescribed format and ensure compliance with the operational framework.
Depositories must build the operational framework and system enhancements for the ISIN-level freeze and issue operational guidelines / communiques.
Stock exchanges are addressees required to ensure compliance with the circular and the depositories' operational framework.
Merchant bankers managing the buy-back are required to ensure compliance with the circular and the operational framework.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
affected_entities.scope_note: RTAs are required to ensure compliance with the circular and the operational framework issued by the depositories.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Promoter and promoter group (including associates) of the company undertaking buy-back
affected_entities.scope_note: Promoter holdings are frozen at ISIN level from the resolution date until closing of the offer, subject to the tender-offer and encumbrance-invocation carve-outs.

affected_instruments.description: Shares or other specified securities held by the promoter and promoter group (including associates) that are subject to the ISIN-level freeze during the buy-back period.

classification_support.reason: CO/CO_BUYBACK and TX_BUYBACK follow from the buy-back subject-matter; FR_MII_OPS and the depository/exchange entities from the operational-framework and system-enhancement duties; the promoter role tags and IN_EQUITY from the freeze on promoter shares; TP_BUYBACK_ROUTE, TP_PROMOTER_STATUS, TP_PROCEDURE and TP_CONTROL from the freeze mechanism and its procedural modalities; FW_BUYBACK from Regulation 24(i)(ea); FW_DEP_ACT and FW_SEBI_ACT from the cited enabling powers.

legal_effects.description: Operationalises Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the Buy-back Regulations by directing the depositories to establish the operational framework and system enhancements needed to give effect to the ISIN-level freeze of promoter holdings.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Freeze does not apply to shares tendered in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of pre-buy-back encumbrances is allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to Board-specified conditions.

legal_effects.description: Sets the procedural content the depositories' operational framework must cover: freezing-instruction format for listed companies, ISIN-level freeze modalities, tender-offer tendering, encumbrance invocation/release, and other operational and system requirements.

operative_change.summary: The depositories must build and operate an ISIN-level freeze mechanism for promoter holdings during buy-backs, and market participants must comply with it.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Depositories must establish an operational framework and system enhancements to freeze promoter and promoter-group holdings at ISIN level from the buy-back resolution date until closing of the offer, with defined carve-outs, and issue operational guidelines; listed companies issue freezing instructions in a prescribed format; exchanges, merchant bankers and RTAs ensure compliance.

actions.description: Depositories shall put in place the operational framework and necessary system enhancements for the ISIN-level freeze and issue the necessary operational guidelines / communiques.
Listed companies shall issue instructions to the depositories for freezing of promoter holdings in the format provided in the operational framework.
Listed companies, recognised stock exchanges, depositories, merchant bankers and RTAs shall ensure compliance with this circular and with the operational framework issued by the depositories.

effective_from.raw_text: This Circular shall come into force with immediate effect from date of issuance of this circular.

deadlines.obligation: The Depositories shall ensure the operational framework and the necessary system enhancements are put in place.

operative_status.reason: As issued on July 21, 2026 the circular is stated to come into force with immediate effect; only the depositories' framework build carries a short forward deadline of August 1, 2026.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Implements Regulation 24(i)(ea) only; other buy-back provisions are unaffected.

notification.importance_reason: Imposes new mandatory system-build and compliance duties on depositories, listed companies and buy-back intermediaries with a near-term implementation deadline, and changes how promoter holdings are handled during every buy-back.

confidence.reason: The operative direction, actors, carve-outs, deadline and enabling provisions are all stated expressly.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/49/14/13(11)2026-CFD-POD1/I/16864/2026 dated July 21, 2026 on operationalisation of freezing of promoter and promoter group (including associates) holdings at ISIN level under Regulation 24(i)(ea) of the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018, addressed to all Listed Companies, Recognised Stock Exchanges, Depositories and Registered Merchant Bankers.

SEBI by notification dated July 01, 2026 amended the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 inserting Regulation 24(i)(ea), under which promoter holdings shall remain frozen at ISIN level from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till closing of the offer, while permitting tendering of shares in a tender-offer buy-back and invocation of encumbrances created prior to the commencement of the buy-back period.

To operationalise the amendment, the Depositories shall put in place an operational framework including necessary system enhancements and issue operational guidelines / communiques; the framework shall provide for the format of freezing instructions by listed companies, operational modalities for the ISIN-level freeze, for permitting tendering in tender-offer buy-backs, for permitting invocation or release of pre-buy-back encumbrances with the freeze continuing on invoked/released securities, and any other necessary operational procedures or system requirements.
The Depositories shall ensure that the operational framework and the necessary system enhancements are put in place before August 01, 2026.

Listed Companies, Recognised Stock Exchanges, Depositories, Merchant Bankers and Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents shall ensure compliance with this circular and the operational framework issued by the Depositories.

This circular shall come into force with immediate effect from the date of issuance of this circular; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Section 26(3) of the Depositories Act, 1996.
Issued by the Deputy General Manager, Corporation Finance Department, Policy and Development-1, SEBI.

events.title: Conditions for intraday borrowing by mutual funds
events.scope_description: Following the July 3, 2026 amendment to the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026, SEBI specifies the purposes for which mutual funds may avail intraday borrowings, the quantum limits, AMC responsibility for end-of-day repayment, mandatory board-approved policy, scheme-wise record keeping, and allocation of borrowing cost and shortfall to the AMC, in supersession of the earlier borrowing guidelines.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular governs the operation of mutual fund schemes - permitting and conditioning intraday borrowings, board policy approval, record keeping and cost allocation - which is fund operation regulation within the Asset & Fund Management (AF) practice.

affected_entities.scope_note: Mutual funds permitted to avail intraday borrowings for the specified purposes and subject to the quantum limits.
AMCs bear responsibility for end-of-day repayment, regulatory-limit compliance, policy implementation, scheme-wise record keeping and the cost of borrowing and of any shortfall.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Trustee Companies / Boards of Trustees of Mutual Funds
affected_entities.scope_note: Boards of Trustees, together with Boards of the AMC, must approve the policy for use of the intraday borrowing facility.

classification_support.reason: Each tag maps to an express provision: AF/AF_MF_OPS and the MF/AMC/Trustee entities to the addressees and operating conditions; TP_LEVERAGE to intraday borrowing, TP_GOVERNANCE/TP_FUND_GOVERNANCE to board policy approval, TP_RECORDS to scheme-wise records, TP_REDEMPTION to unitholder pay-outs, TP_RISK to the liquidity-mismatch and cost-of-shortfall provisions; FW_MF to the cited Regulations and Fourth Schedule; FW_SEBI_ACT to the Section 11(1) enabling power.

legal_effects.description: Supersedes the mutual fund borrowing guidelines in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated March 20, 2026 and SEBI Circular dated March 25, 2026, for intraday borrowings.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Paragraphs 11.10 and 17.7 of the Master Circular and Fourth Schedule clauses 6 and 7 continue to apply.

legal_effects.description: Introduces conditions on the newly permitted intraday borrowing facility: permitted purposes, quantum limits, end-of-day repayment responsibility, mandatory board-approved and published policy, scheme-wise record keeping, and AMC bearing of cost and shortfall.

operative_change.summary: Mutual funds may now avail intraday borrowings for specified purposes subject to quantum limits and AMC controls, replacing the earlier borrowing guidance.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Intraday borrowings are permitted for unitholder pay-outs, scheme pay-in, MTM/forex settlement and repayment of existing borrowings, limited to guaranteed and sighted non-guaranteed receivables; AMCs must ensure end-of-day repayment, obtain board approval for a published policy, keep scheme-wise records, and bear the cost and any shortfall.

actions.description: Boards of the AMC and Trustees shall approve the policy for use of the intraday borrowing facility, which shall be published on the AMC website and include approval processes and monitoring mechanism.
AMCs shall maintain scheme-wise records detailing the underlying liquidity mismatch and the expected source of repayment for each intraday borrowing.
AMCs shall ensure intraday borrowings are repaid by end of day and that any borrowing converted to overnight borrowing stays within regulatory limits and permitted purposes under Regulation 42(1).

effective_from.raw_text: This circular shall come into effect from September 1, 2026.

operative_status.reason: As issued on July 10, 2026 the circular states it comes into effect from September 1, 2026, a future date at the assessment date.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Only clause 5.9.1 (borrowing guidelines) is superseded; paras 11.10 and 17.7 are preserved.

notification.importance_reason: Creates a new operating facility and mandatory governance, record-keeping and cost-allocation duties for all mutual funds and AMCs, with a defined commencement date.

confidence.reason: Purposes, limits, responsibilities, commencement date and enabling provisions are all stated expressly.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/(92)2026-IMD-POD-2/I/16006/2026 dated July 10, 2026, subject 'Intraday borrowing facility availed by mutual funds', addressed to all Mutual Funds, AMCs, Trustee Companies / Boards of Trustees and AMFI.

To address liquidity mismatches from differing market settlement timings, SEBI by Gazette Notification No. CG-MH-E-07072026-274229 dated July 3, 2026 amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 to permit intraday borrowings by mutual funds for purposes specified in this circular.

In supersession of the guidelines on borrowings of mutual funds specified in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated March 20, 2026 and of SEBI Circular No. HO/(92)2026-IMD-POD-2/I/7885/2026 dated March 25, 2026, intraday borrowings by mutual funds shall be subject to the conditions that follow.

Mutual Funds may avail intraday borrowings for unitholder pay-outs (redemptions, IDCW, interest), pay-in for scheme investments, MTM and forex settlement obligations, and repayment of existing borrowings; the quantum is limited to guaranteed receivables and to sighted non-guaranteed receivables to be received by end of day, with additional borrowing by AMCs solely for redemption and other unitholder pay-outs under Regulation 42(1) of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

AMCs are responsible for ensuring intraday borrowings are repaid by end of day and that any conversion to overnight borrowing stays within regulatory limits and permitted purposes under Regulation 42(1); Boards of the AMC and Trustees shall approve the policy for use of the facility, which shall be published on the AMC website and include approval processes and monitoring mechanism; AMCs shall maintain scheme-wise records of the underlying liquidity mismatch and expected source of repayment.

AMCs shall ensure compliance with clauses 6 and 7 of the Fourth Schedule of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 and para 17.7 of the Master Circular; in line with para 11.10 of the Master Circular the cost of intraday borrowing, and any loss or cost from an unforeseen event or delay in receiving funds from receivables, shall be borne by the AMC.

This circular shall come into effect from September 1, 2026; it is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 42(2) and Regulation 84 of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.
Issued by the General Manager, Investment Management Department, SEBI.

events.title: Revised IPF contribution and interest/income utilization norms for depositories
events.scope_description: SEBI modifies clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 of the December 03, 2024 Master Circular for Depositories: depositories must contribute at least 95% of annual IPF investment income to the IPF and plough back at least 95% of interest/income received, and may utilise a maximum of 5% for dedicated IPF Trust employees' expenses and other administrative and statutory expenses, bearing any excess and ploughing back unutilised amounts; the change replaces the earlier requirement that 100% of interest or income from the IPF be treated as corpus, and applies with effect from September 01, 2026.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular revises how depositories must contribute and utilise interest and income from their Investor Protection Fund - a depository governance and investor-protection-fund rule within the Financial Regulatory (FR) practice.

affected_entities.scope_note: Depositories must contribute at least 95% of IPF investment income to the IPF, plough back at least 95% of interest/income received, and may use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses, bearing any excess.

legal_effects.description: Amends clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 of the December 03, 2024 Master Circular for Depositories with revised contribution and utilisation norms for IPF interest and income.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the two identified clauses are modified; the balance of paragraph 4.46 and the Master Circular is unaffected.

legal_effects.description: Replaces the requirement that 100% of IPF interest or income be treated as corpus with a requirement to plough back at least 95% and a permission to use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses.

operative_change.summary: Depositories must plough back at least 95% (not 100%) of IPF interest/income and may use up to 5% for specified IPF Trust and administrative expenses.
operative_change.previous_position: To further strengthen the corpus, 100% of interest or income from IPF shall be treated as corpus of IPF.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: At least 95% of the interest or income received every year from IPF investments shall be contributed to the IPF; at least 95% of interest or income from IPF received every year shall be ploughed back to the IPF; a maximum of 5% may be utilized during the financial year for dedicated IPF Trust employees' expenses and other administrative and statutory expenses (taxes, audit fees, charity commissioner's fee), with excess expenses borne by the depository and non-utilised amounts ploughed back.

actions.description: Depositories shall contribute at least 95% of annual IPF investment income to the IPF, plough back at least 95% of interest/income received, restrict utilisation for specified expenses to a maximum of 5%, bear any excess expenses and plough back unutilised amounts.
Depositories shall take necessary steps and put in place necessary systems for implementation and make necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations wherever applicable.

effective_from.raw_text: Applicability: The provisions of the circular shall be applicable with effect from September 01, 2026.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Only clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 are modified.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/47/14/13(4)2026-MRD-POD3/I/15577/2026 dated July 07, 2026 addressed to all Depositories, on review of norms for utilization of interest or income from the Investor Protection Fund (IPF) of the Depositories.

Paragraph 4.46 of Section 4 of SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/168 for Depositories dated December 03, 2024 prescribes comprehensive IPF guidelines; paragraph 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) currently provides that, to strengthen the corpus, 100% of interest or income from the IPF shall be treated as corpus of the IPF.

Following SMAC recommendations, public consultation comments and internal deliberations, and to bring uniformity with stock exchanges, clauses 4.46.1.1(B)(i)(c) and 4.46.1.1(C)(i)(2) of Section 4 of the December 03, 2024 Master Circular for Depositories are modified: under Contribution to IPF, at least 95% of the interest or income received every year from IPF investments shall be contributed to the IPF; under Utilization, at least 95% of interest or income from IPF received every year shall be ploughed back to the IPF, and a maximum of 5% of such interest or income may be utilized for expenses of dedicated IPF Trust employees and other administrative and statutory expenses (taxes, audit fees, charity commissioner's fee) during the financial year, with excess expenses borne by the depository and unutilised amounts ploughed back.

Applicability: the provisions of the circular shall be applicable with effect from September 01, 2026; the MIIs are directed to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations wherever applicable and bring the circular to the notice of market participants.

The circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Section 26(3) of the Depositories Act, 1996 and Regulation 97 of the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018; issued by the General Manager, SEBI (Market Regulation Department).

events.title: Revised Paragraph 46.1-46.11: CUSPA auto-pledge framework for clients' unpaid securities
events.scope_description: For cash-segment trades not under margin trading facility, unpaid securities are paid out to the client's demat account and auto-pledged to a client unpaid securities pledgee account (CUSPA) opened by the trading member. The revised paragraphs require client communication on pledge creation, a written TM policy communicated to clients before implementation with a maximum client payment window not exceeding five trading days from pay-out, daily determination of the maximum pledge value with release of any excess on or before the next trading day, a bar on giving the client exposure on such securities, invocation and market liquidation with reasonable prior notice and crediting of surplus to the client, depository verification of early-pay-in blocks against the client-level obligation, automatic release by the depositories at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out where the pledge is neither invoked nor released within five trading days, and a prohibition on re-pledging or transferring CUSPA securities to Banks/NBFCs. Stock exchanges must issue implementing operational guidelines within 30 days of this circular in consultation with depositories.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular revises intermediary (stock-broker/trading-member) obligations for handling clients' unpaid securities - a market-conduct / client-asset control - so FR is primary, with FR_INTERMED_BROKER for the broker duties and FR_MII_OPS as a parallel leaf for the operative depository functions (early-pay-in verification and automatic pledge release).

evidence.supporting_text: Circular numbered HO/38/11/(9)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/15382/2026 dated July 03, 2026, issued by SEBI.
Addressed to All recognized Stock Exchanges, All Depositories and All Stock Brokers.
Subject: Handling of Client's Unpaid Securities by Trading Members.

Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers dated June 17, 2025 specifies provisions on Handling of Client's Securities by Trading Members (TM)/Clearing Members (CM); these provisions were introduced vide SEBI Circular Nos. CIR/HO/MIRSD/DOP/CIR/P/2019/75 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/153 dated June 20, 2019 and November 11, 2022; since then there have been regulatory developments such as mandatory pay-out of securities directly to clients' demat accounts and changes in market practice.

Representations were received from the Brokers' Industry Standards Forum (ISF) seeking revisions to align the provisions with the current regulatory and market environment and to address operational challenges.
In order to enhance ease of doing business for stockbrokers and ease of investing for clients, it has been decided to amend Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular as under.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.1-46.2 (Creation of pledge for unpaid securities)
evidence.supporting_text: For trades not under margin trading facility, pay-out of unpaid securities is made directly to the client's demat account followed by creation of an auto-pledge (without specific client instruction) with reason 'unpaid' in favour of a 'client unpaid securities pledgee account (CUSPA)' opened by the TM; after pledge creation the TM must send an email/SMS informing the client of the funds obligation and the TM's right to sell the securities on the client's failure to meet the obligation.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.3-46.5 (Policy by TM for handling unpaid securities)
evidence.supporting_text: The TM must formulate and maintain a policy (standalone or part of its Risk Management Policy) for handling unpaid securities and communicate it to all clients prior to implementation; the policy must set out processes, reasons, manner and timing for invocation/release of pledge and liquidation, and must specify the maximum period - not exceeding five trading days from the pay-out date - within which the client must meet the payment obligation; while CUSPA-pledged unpaid securities may be counted for reporting client margin collection to the Clearing Corporation, the TM must not allow the client exposure on the basis of such securities.

During the period the client's funds obligation continues, the TM must, on a daily basis, determine the maximum value of securities that may remain pledged per the exchanges' operational guidelines (based on ledger balance, overall margin obligations or other specified factors); if the value of pledged securities exceeds this maximum, the TM must release the pledge on the excess quantity on or before the next trading day.

If the client fails to meet the payment obligation within the prescribed timeline, the TM must, per its policy, invoke the pledge and liquidate the unpaid securities after giving the client reasonable notice; on invocation the securities are blocked for early pay-in in the client's demat account with a trail in the TM's CUSPA account, the depositories verify the block details against the client-level obligation, the securities are sold with the client's Unique Client Code, and any surplus after settling the obligation is credited to the client's ledger.

If the pledge on unpaid securities is neither invoked nor released within five trading days after pay-out, the depositories automatically release it at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out and the securities become free balance for the client; the TM may request release any time before auto-release.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.11 (Prohibition on further pledging/transferring CUSPA securities)
evidence.supporting_text: Securities pledged in favour of the TM's CUSPA must not be pledged or transferred to Banks/NBFCs for raising funds.

evidence.locator: Revised Paragraph 46.12 (Extension of pledge in exceptional circumstances)
evidence.supporting_text: In exceptional circumstances where the unpaid pledged securities cannot be liquidated within 5 trading days after pay-out due to (a) the security being in lower circuit with only sellers, (b) suspension or trading halt due to surveillance or other reasons, or (c) any other valid reasons recognized by MIIs including unforeseen circumstances beyond the TM's control, the TM may make a request by 6 PM on the fifth trading day after pay-out to extend the pledge by up to one additional calendar week; if the conditions continue, further extensions of similar period may be sought; once the circumstances no longer exist the TM must not seek any further extension.

On each extension of pledge the TM must send a communication to the client; failure by the TM to request a pledge extension within the stipulated timeframe results in automatic system-based release of the pledged securities.
Paragraph 46 of the Master Circular stands amended to the extent of Paragraph 3 as detailed above; all other provisions specified in the Master Circular continue to remain applicable.
Stock exchanges must issue operational guidelines for implementation of the provisions of this circular, in consultation with depositories, within 30 days from the date of issuance of this circular.
The amended provisions of Paragraph 46.1 to 46.11 of the Master Circular come into force with effect from three months from the date of issuance of operational guidelines by stock exchanges.
The amended provisions of Paragraph 46.12 to 46.14 of the Master Circular come into force with effect from six months from the date of issuance of this circular.

Stock exchanges/depositories are directed to bring the circular to the notice of their members/participants and disseminate it on their websites, make necessary amendments to relevant Bye-laws, Rules and Regulations, and have in place appropriate systems and arrangements to effect the provisions.

Issued in exercise of powers under Section 11(1) of Chapter IV of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 50 of SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 2026, Regulation 51 of Securities Contracts (Regulation) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations) Regulations, 2018 and Regulation 97 of SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018, to protect the interests of investors and to promote the development of and to regulate the securities markets.
Signed by Kumar Abhishek, Deputy General Manager, Market Intermediaries Regulation and Supervision Department.

events.title: Revision of Master Circular paragraph 11.3.1: early pay-in facility and margin-exemption terms for the Commodity Derivatives Segment
events.scope_description: Revises paragraph 11.3.1 (Chapter 11, Early Pay-in Facility) of the 2023 SEBI Master Circular for the Commodity Derivatives Segment: Clearing Corporations must provide an early pay-in facility permitting market participants to deposit certified goods to the CC's accredited warehouse against derivatives contracts; based on risk perception, CCs may exempt such positions from all types of margins, but must continue to collect mark-to-market margins. Takes effect from 21 September 2026; Stock Exchanges/CCs must implement system changes and notify/disseminate to members; no separate interim deadline is stated.

classification.practice_rationale: FR (Financial Regulatory) via FR_MARKETS_COMMOD ('Commodity contracts, participant access, position limits, delivery and electronic gold receipts'), which explicitly covers delivery mechanics for commodity derivatives -- an exact match for an early pay-in/physical-delivery and margin-treatment rule scoped specifically to the Commodity Derivatives Segment.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Recognized Stock Exchanges having a Commodity Derivatives Segment
affected_entities.scope_note: Addressee directed to implement system changes for the revised early pay-in provision, notify members, and disseminate the circular on its website.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Clearing Corporations having a Commodity Derivatives Segment
affected_entities.scope_note: The direct duty-bearer of the revised paragraph 11.3.1: provides the early pay-in facility, may exempt margins on such positions based on risk perception, but must continue to collect mark-to-market margins; also directed (with exchanges) to implement system changes and notify/disseminate.

affected_entities.scope_note: Market participants may use the facility on qualifying certified-goods positions. The source does not establish that every such participant is a SEBI-registered regulated entity; no entity-type tag is inferred.

affected_instruments.description: Commodity derivatives contracts traded on the Commodity Derivatives Segment, against which certified goods may be deposited under the early pay-in facility.

legal_effects.description: Expressly revises paragraph 11.3.1 of the 2023 Commodity Derivatives Master Circular. The new early-pay-in and margin text is provided; the complete previous position was not inspected.

operative_change.summary: Paragraph 11.3.1 of the 2023 Master Circular is explicitly stated to be revised, and its new text is fully quoted, but the pre-revision text is not reproduced in this source. Whether the revision is a substantive change (e.g. to the scope of the margin exemption or the mark-to-market carve-out) or a restatement/clarification of the pre-existing rule cannot be determined from this document alone.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Clearing Corporations shall provide an early pay-in facility permitting market participants to deposit certified goods to the CC's accredited warehouse against relevant derivatives contracts; based on risk perception, CCs may exempt such positions from all types of margins, but must continue to collect mark-to-market margins from such participants.

actions.description: Make necessary changes to systems for implementation of the revised early pay-in provision.
Bring the provisions of this circular to the notice of members.
Disseminate the circular on the exchange's/clearing corporation's website.
Continue to collect mark-to-market margins from market participants on early-pay-in positions, notwithstanding any discretionary exemption of other margin types.
Provide early pay-in facility permitting certified goods to be deposited at CC-accredited warehouses against relevant derivatives contracts.
Based on risk perception, CCs may exempt margins on qualifying early-pay-in positions, but mark-to-market margins must continue to be collected.

effective_from.raw_text: This circular shall come into effect from September 21, 2026.

AIF Regulations 2012 were amended and notified on 18 April 2026 to provide flexibility for scheme winding up and registration surrender; the notification title/number and full text are not supplied.

Regulation 29(7) governs liquidation and distribution after liabilities; 29(10A) enables inoperative tagging subject to specified conditions; 29(11) requires surrender upon winding up. This circular specifies the modalities.

An AIF/scheme may retain proceeds beyond the applicable liquidation/dissolution period if at least one listed ground is satisfied. Ground 3.1 requires demonstrable litigation notice/demand, including official communications from stated authorities/court or investor/counterparty relating to potential liability; SCNs, reassessment notices and investigation summons can qualify without a crystallised demand.

For anticipated liability from possible/probable litigation or tax demand, consent is required from at least 75 percent of investors by value of their investment in the scheme. When seeking consent, the manager discloses the retained amount and estimated retention period.

Residual winding-up operational expenses must be substantiated by invoices, supporting documents or comparable prior-year expense records. Retention on this ground must not exceed three years from the end of permissible fund life.

The Standard Setting Forum of AIFs must formulate implementation standards standardising operational heads for retention, in consultation with SEBI. No completion date or actual standards are supplied.

All retained money satisfying paragraph 3 must be invested under AIF regulation 15(1)(f). After liabilities are satisfied and retained money distributed to investors, the scheme must be wound up under regulation 29.

An AIF with retained money and intending registration surrender may apply for inoperative status using Annexure A by email to inoperativeaif@sebi.gov.in. An AIF with no retained money may also apply if it keeps registration solely in anticipation of a favourable pending-litigation outcome. Tagging follows SEBI approval.
An Inoperative Fund must apply for surrender of its certificate only after liabilities are satisfied and pending retained money is distributed in all schemes.
From obtaining the tag, retained money must follow regulation 15(1)(f), no new scheme may launch, and no management fee may be charged for any scheme.
Annexure B identifies requirements not applicable to AIFs tagged Inoperative Funds.

AIFs with paragraph-3 retained money and tagged Inoperative Funds must provide an annual status report on retained money and outstanding liabilities to SEBI and relevant scheme investors in Annexure C format, with submission on the SEBI Intermediary portal within 30 calendar days from each financial year’s March end.

The retention and inoperative-status facility also applies to VCFs registered under the erstwhile SEBI VCF Regulations 1996. Tagged legacy VCFs have the same regulatory framework described in paragraphs 12–14.
The circular has immediate effect. It cites SEBI Act section 11(1) and AIF Regulations 29/36 as enabling powers. Competent-authority approval and website availability are administrative statements.
The 3 June 2026 Master Circular for AIFs has also been updated with these provisions; the current document supplies its title/date and website navigation, not its full updated text.
Signed by a Deputy General Manager; no full department name is printed in the signature block. The AFD-POD1 code is in the header.

events.title: Revised ETF norms - base price, dynamic/fixed price bands, close-out procedure and Commodity ETF pre-open call auction
events.scope_description: SEBI prescribes revised trading-mechanism norms for ETFs, supplementing/modifying the Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations: a T-1 day Closing Price base price (with fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment), dynamic price bands for Equity/Debt ETFs (initial +10% flexed to +20% after cooling-off) and Commodity ETFs (initial +6% flexed by 3% with DPL relaxation), a fixed +5% band for Overnight/Liquid ETFs, a specific close-out procedure for Overnight/Liquid ETFs, and a pre-open-session call auction for Commodity (Gold/Silver) ETFs. Effective from 1st September, 2026, with a joint Stock Exchange-AMC implementation of the T-1 day closing NAV base price from April 01, 2027.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular prescribes exchange trading-mechanism norms for ETFs - base price, dynamic/fixed price bands, pre-open call auction and close-out - which is cash-market trading-mechanism and MII-operations regulation within the Financial Regulatory (FR) practice; because ETFs are mutual fund schemes and AMCs must act jointly on the NAV base price, an Asset & Fund Management (AF) secondary workflow is retained.

affected_entities.scope_note: Stock exchanges compute the ETF base price, operate the dynamic/fixed price bands and cooling-off, conduct the Commodity ETF pre-open call auction, apply the close-out procedure and (with AMCs) implement the T-1 day closing NAV base price by April 01, 2027.
Clearing corporations apply the ETF close-out and auction/proceeds procedures and make consequential rule amendments.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Asset Management Companies of Mutual Funds
affected_entities.scope_note: AMCs of Mutual Funds jointly with Stock Exchanges must address the operational challenges to implement use of T-1 day closing NAV as the ETF base price with effect from April 01, 2027.

affected_instruments.description: Units of Exchange Traded Funds (Equity, Debt, Commodity/Gold-Silver, Overnight and Liquid ETFs) traded on stock exchanges, whose base price, price bands, pre-open call auction and close-out procedure are prescribed.

classification_support.reason: FR/FR_MARKETS_CASH and TX_SECONDARY from the ETF exchange-trading mechanism; FR_MII_OPS and the exchange/CC entities from the MII operational duties; AF secondary and EN_AMC / FW_MF (affected) from the ETFs being mutual fund schemes and the joint NAV base-price implementation; IN_MF_UNIT from the ETF units; TP_PRICING, TP_MARKET_EXECUTION and TP_RISK from the price-band and cooling-off rules; TP_VALUATION from the NAV / closing-price base price; TP_SETTLEMENT from the close-out procedure; FW_SECC from Regulation 51 and FW_SEBI_ACT from Section 11(1).

legal_effects.description: Supplements and modifies the ETF-related price-band, close-out, auction and pre-open call-auction provisions of the Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations (Chapter 1 paragraphs 2.3.1, 2.5, 17.1; Chapter 3 paragraphs 2.1-2.3).
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: For ETFs other than Overnight/Liquid ETFs the existing Chapter 3 paragraph 2.1 close-out provisions and the existing Auction and Proceeds provisions (paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3) continue to apply.

legal_effects.description: Sets the ETF base-price, dynamic/fixed price-band, cooling-off, cross-exchange flex, close-out and Commodity ETF pre-open call-auction procedures.

operative_change.summary: ETFs move from a fixed +20% price band on a T-2 day NAV base price to a T-1 day Closing Price base price with dynamic (Equity/Debt, Commodity) or fixed (+5% Overnight/Liquid) price bands, a specific close-out procedure and a Commodity ETF pre-open call auction.
operative_change.previous_position: ETFs had a fixed price band of +20% (except +5% for Overnight ETFs) applied on a base price equal to the T-2 day NAV of the ETF.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Base price is the T-1 day Closing Price (last 30-minute VWAP), with LTP and latest closing NAV fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment; Equity/Debt ETFs (other than Overnight/Liquid) have dynamic bands (initial +10%, flexed to +20% after cooling-off, 5% per flex, max two per direction, no sliding, cross-exchange); Overnight/Liquid ETFs have a fixed +5% band; Commodity ETFs have dynamic bands (initial +6%, flexed by 3%, DPL relaxation in 3% stages, no cap); Overnight/Liquid ETF close-out is the higher of the highest recorded price up to auction/close-out and 5% above the latest closing price; a pre-open-session call auction is introduced for Commodity (Gold/Silver) ETFs.

actions.description: MIIs shall put in place systems to implement the revised ETF base-price, price-band, cooling-off, close-out and Commodity ETF pre-open call-auction norms and make necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations.

Stock exchanges shall determine the ETF base price as the T-1 day Closing Price (with the specified fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment) and operate the dynamic/fixed price bands and cooling-off periods per ETF category.

effective_from.raw_text: Applicability: The provisions of the circular shall come into effect from 1st September, 2026.

deadlines.obligation: Stock Exchanges and AMCs of Mutual Funds shall jointly address the operational challenges to implement use of the T-1 day closing NAV of the ETF as the base price.

transitional_provisions.affected_cohort: All ETFs (Equity, Debt, Commodity, Overnight, Liquid)
transitional_provisions.condition: The T-1 day Closing Price is adopted as the base price 'to start with', pending resolution of operational challenges in using the T-1 day closing NAV.
transitional_provisions.rule: Stock Exchanges and AMCs must jointly implement use of the T-1 day closing NAV of the ETF as the base price with effect from April 01, 2027.

operative_status.reason: As issued on June 15, 2026 the circular comes into effect from 1st September, 2026, a future date at the assessment date, with a further NAV-base-price step from April 01, 2027.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Existing Chapter 3 paragraphs 2.1-2.3 close-out / auction / proceeds provisions continue for ETFs other than Overnight/Liquid ETFs.

notification.importance_reason: Comprehensively revises the base price, price-band, cooling-off, close-out and pre-open call-auction mechanics for all ETF categories that exchanges and clearing corporations must implement, with a phased NAV-base-price step.

confidence.reason: The prior ETF fixed-band position and the full set of revised norms and dates are stated expressly in the circular.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/47/11/11(1)2026-MRD-POD3/I/13804/2026 dated June 15, 2026, addressed to all Recognized Stock Exchanges, Recognized Clearing Corporations, all Asset Management Companies of Mutual Funds and the Association of Mutual Funds in India, on norms for base price, price bands, call auction in the pre-open session and the close-out procedure for Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs).

Paragraph 2.3.1 of Chapter 1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024 prescribes scrip-wise price bands of up to 20% for scrips without derivatives, and paragraph 2.5 prescribes dynamic price bands for scrips with derivatives; currently ETFs have a fixed price band of +20% (except +5% for Overnight ETFs) on a base price equal to T-2 day NAV; based on a Working Group and SMAC recommendations, public consultation and stakeholder discussion, revised norms are provided.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 4-7 (base price, price bands, close-out, call auction)
evidence.supporting_text: Base price for ETFs is T-1 day Closing Price (last 30-minute VWAP), with LTP and latest closing NAV fallbacks and corporate-action adjustment; Stock Exchanges and AMCs shall jointly address operational challenges to implement use of T-1 day closing NAV as base price with effect from April 01, 2027. Price bands: Equity/Debt ETFs (other than Overnight/Liquid) have dynamic bands with an initial +10% flexed up to +20% after cooling-off (15 or 5 minutes), flexed by 5% for at most two instances per direction, no sliding, cross-exchange applicability; Overnight and Liquid ETFs have a fixed +5% band; Commodity (Gold/Silver) ETFs have dynamic bands with an initial +6% flexed by 3%, with DPL relaxation in 3% stages, cooling-off, no cap and no restriction on number of flexes. Close-out for Overnight/Liquid ETFs is the higher of the highest recorded price up to the auction/close-out date and 5% above the latest available closing price; other ETFs keep the existing Chapter 3 paragraph 2.1 provisions, and existing Auction and Proceeds provisions (paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3) continue. A call auction in the pre-open session is introduced for Commodity ETFs (Gold/Silver), using the mechanism at paragraph 17.1 of Chapter 1 of the Master Circular.

Applicability: the provisions of the circular shall come into effect from 1st September, 2026; all MIIs are advised to put systems in place, amend bye-laws/rules/regulations and publicise the circular; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018.
Issued by the General Manager, SEBI (Market Regulation Department).
