events.title: One-time relaxation from Master Circular penal provisions for MPS non-compliance
events.scope_description: SEBI grants a one-time relaxation from the penal provisions of the July 11, 2023 LODR compliance Master Circular for listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026; recognised stock exchanges and depositories are directed not to take penal action against such entities during that period, and may withdraw penal actions already initiated since April 1, 2026, with the circular applicable with immediate effect.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular concerns a listed-entity continuous-obligation (Minimum Public Shareholding) and grants relief from its enforcement - a listed-entity obligation matter within Capital Markets (CM); it also directs the enforcement conduct of stock exchanges and depositories, a Financial Regulatory (FR) secondary workflow.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026
affected_entities.scope_note: Cohort of listed entities that receive the one-time relaxation from the Master Circular penal provisions for MPS non-compliance during the specified window.
Advised not to take penal action against the specified cohort during the window, may withdraw penal actions already initiated, and must publicise the circular and amend bye-laws where necessary.
Advised not to take penal action (including freezing of promoter shareholding) against the specified cohort during the window and may withdraw penal actions already initiated.

classification_support.reason: CM/CM_LISTED and TP_MPS follow from the Minimum Public Shareholding subject-matter; FR_MII_OPS and the exchange/depository entities from the direction not to take penal action; TP_PROMOTER_STATUS from the freezing-of-promoter-shareholding penal action being relaxed; TP_INVESTOR_PROTECTION from the market-conditions rationale; FW_LODR from the Master Circular being for LODR compliance; FW_SCRR and FW_SEBI_ACT from the MPS regime and the cited enabling powers.

legal_effects.description: Grants a one-time exemption from the applicability of the penal provisions of the July 11, 2023 LODR compliance Master Circular for the specified cohort of listed entities.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Limited to listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026, and to non-compliance during that period; other Master Circular provisions and MPS obligations are unaffected.

legal_effects.description: Directs recognised stock exchanges and depositories not to take penal action (fines, freezing of promoter shareholding, other consequential actions) against the specified cohort during the window, and permits withdrawal of penal actions already initiated since April 1, 2026.

operative_change.summary: Penal enforcement of MPS non-compliance under the LODR compliance Master Circular is suspended for a defined cohort and window.
operative_change.previous_position: Under the July 11, 2023 Master Circular, recognised stock exchanges and depositories apply penal provisions (fines, freezing of promoter shareholding and other consequential actions) to listed entities not complying with MPS requirements.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: For listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026, those penal provisions do not apply for non-compliance during that period, and penal actions initiated since April 1, 2026 may be withdrawn.

actions.description: Recognised stock exchanges and depositories are advised not to take penal action against the specified cohort during the window and may withdraw penal actions already initiated against such entities since April 1, 2026.

Stock exchanges shall bring the circular to the notice of all listed entities, disseminate it on their website, and make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for implementation, if necessary.

effective_from.raw_text: The circular shall be applicable with immediate effect.

effective_until.raw_text: listed entities whose due date for compliance with MPS requirements falls during the period from April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026
conditions: relief attaches to MPS due dates within this window

transitional_provisions.affected_cohort: Listed entities whose MPS compliance due date falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026
transitional_provisions.condition: Penal actions may already have been initiated by stock exchanges or depositories against such entities for MPS non-compliance during April 1, 2026 till the date of the circular.
transitional_provisions.rule: Such already-initiated penal actions may be withdrawn, and no further penal action is to be taken against the cohort for non-compliance during the window.

operative_status.reason: As issued on April 7, 2026 the circular is stated to be applicable with immediate effect; the relief is time-bound to MPS due dates falling up to September 30, 2026.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Only the penal provisions for MPS non-compliance are relaxed, and only for the specified cohort and window.

notification.importance_reason: Materially changes the enforcement position for MPS non-compliance for a defined cohort of listed entities, including suspension and potential withdrawal of fines and promoter-shareholding freezes.

confidence.reason: The relief, its cohort, window, enforcement direction and immediate effect are all stated expressly, and the prior penal position is described in the circular itself.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/49/14/14(13)2026-CFD-POD2/I/8772/2026 dated April 7, 2026 addressed to all listed entities, all recognised Stock Exchanges and all registered Depositories, on relaxation from applicability of the SEBI Master Circular for LODR compliance in respect of non-compliance with Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements.

The SEBI Master Circular dated July 11, 2023 for compliance with the LODR Regulations prescribes the procedure for recognised stock exchanges and depositories in respect of listed entities not complying with MPS requirements, including levy of fines, freezing of promoter shareholding and other consequential actions; an industry body has represented the difficulties faced by listed entities in achieving MPS compliance owing to capital-market volatility from geopolitical tensions.

Considering the representation and prevailing market conditions, SEBI grants a one-time relaxation from applicability of the penal provisions under the Master Circular for listed entities whose due date for MPS compliance falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026; recognised stock exchanges and depositories are advised not to take any penal action against such entities for non-compliance during that period, and any penal actions initiated by them against such entities for MPS non-compliance during April 1, 2026 till date may be withdrawn.

The circular is applicable with immediate effect; the stock exchanges are advised to bring the circular to the notice of listed entities and disseminate it on their website, and to make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for implementation, if necessary.
The circular is issued under Section 11 and Section 11A of the SEBI Act, 1992; issued by the Deputy General Manager, Corporation Finance Department, Policy and Development-2, SEBI.

events.title: Settlement of adjudication proceedings against the managing director of KTIL for alleged failure to maintain SDD under regulation 3(5) of the PIT Regulations
events.scope_description: This Settlement Order disposes the adjudication proceedings initiated against Mr. Ramesh Kunhikannan (managing director of KTIL) for the SEBI-alleged violation of regulation 3(5) of the PIT Regulations (failure to ensure maintenance of a Structured Digital Database for UPSI relating to KTIL's financial results), on the basis of accepted settlement terms and a paid settlement amount, without admission or denial of the allegation.

classification.practice_rationale: ED (Securities Enforcement and Disputes) is primary: this is a settlement order under the SEBI (Settlement Proceedings) Regulations, 2018 disposing adjudication proceedings. FR is a material secondary practice for the underlying market-conduct standard at issue (PIT Regulations regulation 3(5) SDD maintenance), consistent with the rule that a PIT settlement is ED primary with FR secondary for the underlying conduct.

events.title: Extension of the MII Capacity Planning and Real Time Performance Monitoring framework to the Commodity Derivatives Segment, superseding the prior single-clause capacity requirement
events.scope_description: Extends most of the 2024 MII Capacity Planning and Real Time Performance Monitoring framework (previously excluding the Commodity Derivatives Segment) to Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations with a Commodity Derivatives Segment, mutatis mutandis, with two tailored modifications (installed capacity at least 2x projected peak load; immediate MII/SCOT action above 75% utilisation), requires a Board/SCOT-approved policy document within 3 months, supersedes the prior single-clause 4x-capacity requirement for this segment, and itself comes into effect 3 months from issuance.

classification.practice_rationale: FR (Financial Regulatory) is primary and sufficient via FR_MII_OPS ('Infrastructure operations and resilience: capacity planning, surveillance systems, continuity, settlement infrastructure and operational risk'), whose own example_matters entry is 'Commodity-segment capacity planning' -- an exact match. This is purely an MII infrastructure-resilience requirement, not a rule about the commodity contracts' own terms.

legal_effects.description: Supersedes Clause 16.1.2, Chapter 16 of the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives Segment dated 4 August 2023 (the prior 4x-peak-order-load capacity requirement), for the Commodity Derivatives Segment.

Introduces, for the first time for the Commodity Derivatives Segment, the detailed capacity-planning and real-time performance-monitoring framework of the 2024 MII circular (paragraphs 3.1, 3.2, 3.4-3.12, 3.14-3.16 applied mutatis mutandis, plus two tailored provisions at 3.3 and 3.13), together with a new duty to prepare and submit a Board/SCOT-approved Capacity Planning and RTPM Policy document to SEBI within 3 months.

operative_change.summary: Applies the identified 2024 framework provisions to the commodity segment with two express modifications: at least 2x projected peak load, and immediate action when component utilisation exceeds 75%, with SCOT oversight and documented handling. Supersedes only clause 16.1.2 and requires the approved policy within three months.
operative_change.previous_position: The source quotes clause 16.1.2: exchange trading capacity at least four times peak order load encountered, performance study and upgrades. It also expressly states commodity-segment exchanges and CCs were excluded from the 10 December 2024 framework. No assertion is made that no other requirements applied.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: The Commodity Derivatives Segment is now subject to the 2024 MII framework's provisions (mutatis mutandis), with installed capacity of at least 2x projected peak load, a documented escalation procedure once utilisation exceeds 75%, and a requirement to submit a Board/SCOT-approved Capacity Planning and RTPM Policy document to SEBI within 3 months; the old Clause 16.1.2 is superseded for this segment.

actions.description: Prepare a Capacity Planning and Real Time Performance Monitoring Policy document for the Commodity Derivatives Segment, obtain SCOT and Governing Board approval, and submit it to SEBI within 3 months of this circular.

Maintain installed capacity of at least 2x projected peak load for Commodity Derivatives Segment systems, and take immediate escalated action (overseen by SCOT) whenever actual capacity utilisation of any component exceeds 75% of installed capacity.
Take necessary steps to implement the extended capacity-planning/RTPM framework, including any necessary amendments to relevant bye-laws, rules or regulations.

events.title: Proposal to allow InvIT SPVs to retain SPV status after concession-period end/termination, subject to exit/reacquisition and disclosure conditions
events.scope_description: Proposes a new proviso to the InvIT Regulations' SPV definition (Regulation 2(1)(zy)) so that an SPV does not lose its status merely because a PPP concession has ended/terminated, subject to Board-specified conditions: the Investment Manager must exit or re-acquire an infrastructure project in the SPV within one year of the latest triggering event, and enhanced InvIT/SPV-level annual-report disclosures must be made in the interim. Comments due 26 February 2026.

classification.practice_rationale: CM (Capital Markets) via CM_TRUST_INVIT ('InvIT lifecycle'), covering acquisitions and asset-holding structure -- this proposal concerns the definition and continued qualification of an InvIT's SPV holding structure, a core InvIT lifecycle/structuring matter.

affected_entities.scope_note: InvITs holding infrastructure projects through SPVs whose concession period has ended/terminated; the proposal would let such SPVs retain their SPV status subject to conditions.
Would bear the proposed exit/reacquisition-within-one-year obligation and the InvIT/SPV-level annual-report disclosure duties for such SPVs.

sebi_departments.raw_label: Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities

legal_effects.description: Proposes a proviso to the InvIT Regulations' SPV definition (Regulation 2(1)(zy)) preserving SPV status after PPP concession-period end/termination, subject to a one-year exit/reacquisition condition and enhanced disclosures.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Proposal only; subject to public comment (due 26 February 2026) and Board finalisation.

operative_change.summary: Proposes to expand the SPV definition so that concession-period end/termination does not itself disqualify an entity from SPV status, subject to a one-year exit/reacquisition condition and enhanced annual-report disclosures.
operative_change.previous_position: Under Regulation 2(1)(zy), an SPV must hold >=90% of its assets directly in infrastructure projects; an entity whose sole infrastructure project's concession has ended/terminated may no longer meet this criterion, creating uncertainty over its continued SPV status.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: A company/LLP holding a PPP project would not lose SPV status merely because the concession agreement concluded or was terminated, provided the Investment Manager exits the investment or acquires a new infrastructure project within one year of the latest of (a) concession completion/termination, (b) conclusion of pending claims/litigation, or (c) completion of the defect liability period, and provided specified InvIT-level and SPV-level annual-report disclosures are made in the interim.

actions.description: If adopted: exit (sale/liquidation/winding-up) the SPV investment, or acquire a new infrastructure project in it, within one year of the latest triggering event.

If adopted, manager reports trust-level gross/net investment breakup and each affected SPV’s project/end-date/vesting certificate, grouped audited carrying assets/liabilities/reserves, contingent liabilities, outstanding debt/repayment schedule, claims/litigation/assessments/contractual duties/defect period, asset sufficiency and funding plan if inadequate, and exit/new-project strategy with steps taken and expected completion. These disclosures continue while the InvIT holds the SPV.

deadlines.obligation: If adopted: exit the SPV investment or acquire a new infrastructure project in it.

evidence.supporting_text: Consultation Paper on Measures towards Ease of Doing Business for REITs and InvITs, issued by the Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities - POD II, dated 5 February 2026.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.locator: Contents page (four matters and comment deadline)
evidence.supporting_text: Lists four matters for consultation: (1) Continuing investment in SPV post end of concession period (InvITs); (2) Expanding the scope of investment in liquid mutual fund schemes (both REITs and InvITs); (3) Alignment of investment conditions for Private InvIT with Public InvIT re: greenfield projects (InvITs); (4) Expanding the scope of permitted use of fresh borrowings for InvITs where Net Borrowings exceeds 49% (InvITs). States 'Comments on the Consultation paper (CP) may be sent by February 26, 2026'.
evidence.quote: Comments on the Consultation paper (CP) may be sent by February 26, 2026
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Objective is to seek comments/views/suggestions on various ease-of-doing-business measures for REITs and InvITs; proposals based on inputs from the Indian REITs Association (IRA), Bharat InvITs Association (BIA), and recommendations of the Hybrid Securities Advisory Committee (HYSAC).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Under the InvIT Regulations, InvITs hold infrastructure projects via HoldCo/SPV; on expiry/termination of a concession period, the SPV's concession rights cease though the InvIT may remain invested in it. Industry associations requested clarification whether such an SPV (no longer holding any infrastructure project) still qualifies as an 'SPV' under the InvIT Regulations.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 2(1)(zy) of the InvIT Regulations defines 'SPV' as a company/LLP in which the InvIT/HoldCo holds controlling interest and >=51% equity, which holds >=90% of its assets directly in infrastructure projects and does not invest in other SPVs, and is not engaged in any activity other than those pertaining/incidental to the underlying infrastructure projects.
evidence.quote: which holds not less than ninety per cent. of its assets directly in infrastructure projects and does not invest in other SPVs
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Upon expiry/termination of the concession agreement, the InvIT continues to hold SPVs lacking an eligible/completed-and-revenue-generating infrastructure project; commercial/practical constraints (statutory/contractual obligations, litigation, defect-liability periods) prevent immediate divestment or winding-up, causing negative cash flows requiring NDCF adjustment at the Trust level; industry requested clarification that such entities remain classified as SPVs.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI's consideration: upon expiry/termination, the SPV's infrastructure-project interest ceases and it may no longer meet the 90% qualifying criterion, yet the InvIT may need to continue holding it due to continuing statutory/contractual obligations that make immediate winding-up difficult.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed new proviso to the SPV definition: conclusion/termination of a PPP concession agreement shall not affect the entity's status as an SPV, subject to conditions specified by the Board.
evidence.quote: the conclusion or termination of the concession agreement with the public concessioning authority shall not affect the status as an SPV and such company or LLP, shall continue to be classified as an SPV, subject to fulfillment of the conditions specified by the Board.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed condition: the Investment Manager shall either exit the SPV investment (sale/liquidation/winding-up) or acquire a new infrastructure project in it, within one year of the latest of: (a) completion/termination of the concession agreement, (b) conclusion of all pending claims/litigation, or (c) completion of the defect liability period.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed annual-report disclosures while such SPV investment is held: at InvIT level, a breakup of gross/net investment value in such SPVs; at SPV level, project details/concession-end date/vesting-certificate status, assets/liabilities (incl. contingent liabilities), debt repayment schedule, other material details (pending claims/litigation/assessments, defect-liability balance period), sufficiency of assets to meet liabilities, and an exit-strategy/timeline.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Comments invited, with supporting rationale, on: (a) the proposed SPV-definition amendment; (b) the proposed conditions on the Investment Manager; and (c) the proposed annual-report disclosures.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 18(5)(i) of the REIT Regulations and Regulation 18(5)(b)(vii) of the InvIT Regulations permit investment in liquid mutual fund scheme units only where the credit risk value (CRV) is at least 12 and the scheme falls under Class A-I of the Potential Risk Class (PRC) matrix; IRA/BIA represented that this restricts investment options.
evidence.quote: units of liquid mutual funds schemes where the credit risk value is at least 12 and which falls under the Class A-I in the potential risk class matrix as specified by the Board.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Only 2 of the top 15 liquid mutual fund schemes by AUM qualify for CRV>=12/Class A-I; of 38 total liquid schemes, 9 qualify under Class A-I (3 of which have AUM below Rs. 1,000 crore) while 29 (AUM Rs. 4,96,539 cr.) fall in Class B-I and none in Class C-1; IRA/BIA proposed permitting investment in schemes with CRV>=10, spanning Class A-I and Class B-I.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Explains the PRC 3x3 matrix (Class A/B/C by CRV; Class I/II/III by Macaulay Duration) and the CRV-by-credit-rating table (e.g. AAA=12, AA+=11, AA=10) from the MF Master Circular (27 June 2024); concludes that Class B-I (CRV>=10) provides additional AA-and-above-rated options while maintaining low-to-moderate credit risk.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed amendment to Regulation 18(5)(i) of the REIT Regulations and Regulation 18(5)(b)(vii) of the InvIT Regulations: 'units of liquid mutual funds schemes where the credit risk value is at least 10 and which fall under the Class A-I or Class B-I in the potential risk class matrix as specified by the Board.'
evidence.quote: units of liquid mutual funds schemes where the credit risk value is at least 10 and which fall under the Class A-I or Class B-I in the potential risk class matrix as specified by the Board.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Comments invited on expanding REIT/InvIT investment scope to liquid mutual fund schemes with CRV>=10, spanning Class A-I and Class B-I.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Under Regulation 18 of the InvIT Regulations, a publicly listed InvIT may invest up to 10% of asset value in pure greenfield (under-construction) projects, but a privately listed InvIT cannot; market participants requested parity. Regulation 14(2)/14(4) govern private/public InvIT fundraising respectively; Regulation 18(4) requires >=80% investment in 'eligible infrastructure projects' for private InvITs (with un-invested funds only in listed sub-clause instruments); Regulation 18(5) sets the public-InvIT 80%/20% split (completed-and-revenue-generating vs. under-construction, capped at 10%).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: A privately listed InvIT must invest >=80% in 'eligible infrastructure projects' (which excludes pure greenfield/50-50-test-failing projects) with the balance 20% restricted to money-market/other-investment avenues (no under-construction-project category); a publicly listed InvIT must invest >=80% in completed/revenue-generating projects with up to 10% of the balance 20% permitted in pure greenfield projects. Retail investors participate in public InvITs (1-unit lot size) while only institutional/body-corporate investors participate in private InvITs (Rs. 25 lakh minimum lot), yet only the (retail-facing) public InvIT currently has any greenfield allowance.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed amendment to Regulation 18(4) of the InvIT Regulations to add sub-clause (i) among the permitted un-invested-fund instruments, facilitating privately listed InvITs to invest up to 10% of InvIT asset value in pure greenfield projects, aligning with publicly listed InvITs.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Comments invited on permitting privately listed InvITs to invest in pure greenfield projects up to 10% of InvIT asset value, aligning with publicly listed InvITs.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii) of the InvIT Regulations requires that where Net Borrowings (aggregate consolidated borrowings/deferred payments of InvIT, HoldCo, SPV(s), net of cash) exceed 49% of InvIT asset value, further borrowing be utilised only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects (also requiring 'AAA' issuer credit rating, a 6-distribution track record, and unitholder approval); BIA requested clarification that refinancing and improvement/major-maintenance/capacity-augmentation borrowing qualify as permitted use.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: BIA represented that refinancing of SPV/HoldCo-level acquisition debt at the InvIT level, and refinancing of existing InvIT/SPV/HoldCo debt due to maturity or better terms, does not change the original development-related end-use of the debt being refinanced and should qualify as permitted use.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: BIA represented that capital expenditure/major-maintenance (MM) borrowing to enhance asset performance or meet concession-mandated requirements should also qualify as 'development'; MM expense is not eligible for capitalisation for road-sector InvITs under applicable accounting principles (unlike renewable/airport assets), creating a need for clarity on its treatment under Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI's consideration accepts that: refinancing of newly acquired SPV/HoldCo debt and of maturing/repriced InvIT/SPV/HoldCo debt does not change the underlying development-related end-use; capex for asset performance/capacity augmentation is 'development' and hence already permitted; and MM expense for road projects specifically warrants an express clarification given its non-capitalisable accounting treatment.
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Proposed enabling amendment to Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii) ('utilize the funds only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects or such other purpose as may be specified by the Board from time to time'), specifying permitted end-uses: (i) capex for asset performance/capacity augmentation; (ii) Major Maintenance expense for Road Projects (both terms defined); and (iii) refinancing of debt originally availed for a Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii)-permitted purpose, subject to no increase in aggregate Net Borrowings and refinancing of principal only.
evidence.quote: utilize the funds only for acquisition or development of infrastructure projects or such other purpose as may be specified by the Board from time to time
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Comments invited on: (a) permitting capex borrowings; (b) permitting Major Maintenance-expense borrowings for the road sector; and (c) permitting refinancing of debt, all under Regulation 20(3)(b)(ii).
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Public comments on the above-detailed proposals invited, to be submitted latest by 26 February 2026 via SEBI's online public-comments form; technical-issue contact provided. 'Issued on: February 05, 2026.'
evidence.quote: The comments/ suggestions should be submitted latest by February 26, 2026, through the online web-based form
evidence.extraction_note: All thirty pages read; PRC matrix and highlighted amendments on pages 19/27 visually checked.

events.title: Mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosures for SDIs by the trustee of the SPDE
events.scope_description: Specifying the manner of the Regulation 11B half-yearly information duty, SEBI mandates that the Trustee of a special purpose distinct entity submit the disclosures in Annexure I (SDIs backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures) or Annexure II (SDIs backed by other exposures) on a half-yearly basis to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed, within 30 days from the end of March or September, with Annexure III providing computation illustrations. Effective from March 31, 2026.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular mandates periodic pool-level disclosures for securitisation transactions (SDIs issued by special purpose distinct entities) - securitisation regulation within the Banking & Finance / structured-finance (BF) practice; because the SDIs are listed instruments and the disclosures go to the stock exchange, a Capital Markets (CM) secondary workflow (listed structured-debt disclosure) is retained.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Special purpose distinct entities (SPDEs) that have issued SDIs
affected_entities.scope_note: The securitisation vehicle on whose behalf the trustee makes the half-yearly disclosures; Regulation 11B binds the SPDE and the trustee.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Trustee of the special purpose distinct entity
affected_entities.scope_note: The trustee is the actor required to submit the Annexure I / II disclosures half-yearly to the Board and the stock exchange within 30 days from the end of March or September.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Recognised Stock Exchanges where SDIs are listed
affected_entities.scope_note: Stock exchanges where the SDIs are listed are addressees and recipients of the half-yearly disclosures.

affected_instruments.description: Securitised Debt Instruments issued by a special purpose distinct entity (backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures, or by other exposures), for which half-yearly pool-level disclosures are mandated.

sebi_departments.raw_label: Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities

classification_support.reason: BF/BF_SECURITISATION and TX_SECURITISE from the securitisation subject-matter; CM secondary and CM_DCM_STRUCTURED from the listed SDIs and stock-exchange disclosure; IN_SDI from the instrument; EN_REGULATED_ENTITY (SPDE) and the EN_TRUSTEE role from the Regulation 11B obligation and the submitting actor; EN_EXCHANGE from the listing venue recipient; TP_DISCLOSURE and TP_RECORDS from the periodic-disclosure and format requirements; TP_SECURITISATION and TP_STRUCTURING from the pool-level content; FW_SDI from Regulations 11B and 48, FW_SEBI_ACT from Section 11(1).

legal_effects.description: Specifies the manner of the half-yearly information-furnishing duty under Regulation 11B of the SDI Regulations, 2008 by prescribing the Annexure I / II disclosure formats, the recipients (Board and listing stock exchange) and the 30-day timeline.
Introduces the specific mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosure obligation on the trustee of the SPDE, with the detailed formats in Annexures I and II and the illustrations in Annexure III.

operative_change.summary: The trustee of an SPDE must make half-yearly pool-level disclosures for SDIs in the prescribed Annexure I / II formats to the Board and the listing stock exchange within 30 days of each half-year end.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: The Trustee of a special purpose distinct entity shall submit the Annexure I (loan / listed debt / credit facility exposures) or Annexure II (other exposures) disclosures on a half-yearly basis to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed, within 30 days from the end of March or September; Annexure III provides computation illustrations.

actions.description: The Trustee of the SPDE shall submit the Annexure I or Annexure II half-yearly disclosures to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed.
The disclosures shall be made within 30 days from the end of March or September on a recurring half-yearly basis, in the prescribed formats.

effective_from.raw_text: The provisions of this circular shall be effective from March 31, 2026.

deadlines.obligation: The Trustee of the SPDE shall submit the half-yearly SDI disclosures to the Board and the listing stock exchange.

timing.raw_text: within 30 days from the end of March or September
timing.anchor_event: end of March or September (each half-year)
conditions: recurring half-yearly obligation

operative_status.reason: As issued on December 16, 2025 the circular is stated to be effective from March 31, 2026, a future date at the assessment date.

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Specifies the manner of the Regulation 11B duty only; other SDI Regulation provisions are unaffected.

notification.importance_reason: Introduces a detailed mandatory half-yearly pool-level disclosure regime for all SDIs, with prescribed formats and a fixed timeline and a defined commencement date.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular HO/17/11/18(1)2025-DDHS-POD1/I/342/2025 dated December 16, 2025, addressed to special purpose distinct entities and their trustees and to Recognised Stock Exchanges, on mandating periodic disclosure requirements for Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs).

Regulation 11B of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008 (last amended on May 05, 2025) mandates a special purpose distinct entity and the trustee to furnish information to the Board on a half-yearly basis, in the manner as may be specified by the Board.

Pursuant to discussions with stakeholders, it is decided that the Trustee of a special purpose distinct entity shall submit the disclosures set out in Annexure I and Annexure II on a half-yearly basis to the Board and to the stock exchange where the SDIs are listed, within 30 days from the end of March or September; Annexure I applies to SDIs backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures, Annexure II to SDIs backed by other exposures, and Annexure III provides illustrations of weighted average maturity, weighted average rating and average default rate.

The provisions of this circular shall be effective from March 31, 2026; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulations 11B and 48 of the SDI Regulations, 2008 to protect the interests of investors and to develop and regulate the securities market.
Issued by the Deputy General Manager, Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities, SEBI.

evidence.locator: Annexure I (disclosure format - securitisation of loan / listed debt / credit facility exposures)
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure I prescribes the half-yearly disclosure format for SDIs backed by loan / listed debt securities / credit facility exposures, covering maturity characteristics of underlying assets, Minimum Retention Requirement, credit quality (overdue distribution, security cover, rating-wise distribution, default and recovery rates, LTV and DTI frequency distributions, prepayment, top-up loans, expected credit loss, recovery actions, utilisation of credit enhancement and liquidity facility), amendments, other pool characteristics and Minimum Holding Period.

evidence.locator: Annexure II (disclosure format - securitisation of other exposures)
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure II prescribes the half-yearly disclosure format for SDIs backed by other exposures, covering maturity characteristics, Minimum Retention Requirement, credit quality (deviations in collections, obligor default, prepayment, recovery actions, utilisation of credit enhancement and liquidity facility), amendments, other information and Minimum Holding Period.
Annexure III sets out illustrations for computing the weighted average maturity of the underlying assets, the weighted average rating of the pool and the average (moving average) default rate.

operative_change.summary: KYC verification methods and acceptable proofs in the draft FPI master circular.

Foreign-language documents require English translation; names and addresses must match and each address needs proof. An authorised custodian may complete forms under a power of attorney. In-person verification does not apply to non-individuals; individuals may use webcam verification. Reliable information from public regulator, exchange, SRO or registrar sources may be attested by an authorised intermediary official. Individual identity proof requires government photo identification. Address proofs include government/regulator records, utility bills no older than two months, bank statements no older than three months, and appropriately notarised, apostilled or consularised custodian powers of attorney. Multilateral institutions may use their constitutive documents. Separate address proof is unnecessary if valid address information is already in the identity proof.

Trades are not annulled; failures are referred to SEBI.

operative_change.summary: Corporate-debt eligibility, RFQ and investment-limit auctions in the draft FPI master circular.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Government securities, debt, currency derivatives and IRFs follow the referenced RBI directions. To-be-listed corporate debt is not subject to the end-use restriction otherwise applicable to unlisted debt; if it is not listed within 30 days or the applicable end-use condition fails, dispose of it immediately to a domestic investor or the issuer. At least 10% of quarterly secondary corporate-debt trade value must use RFQ quotes. Debt mutual fund holdings count towards corporate-debt limits. CDIL is available on tap until 95% utilisation; above that, stop purchases and auction unutilised limits. Auctions alternate BSE/NSE on the second trading day after intimation if at least INR 100 crore is free, or on the sixteenth day after fifteen consecutive trading days below that amount. Auction hours are 15:30–17:30; minimum bid and tick are INR 1 crore; maximum bid is 10% of the offered limit; allocation is by price-time priority and the fee is the higher of INR 1,000 and the bid amount. Use allocated limits within ten trading days. Sale/redemption permits two-trading-day reinvestment; unused limits return to the pool. Subsequent auctions are every twelve trading days subject to availability. Below 92% utilisation, on-tap access resumes; recrossing 95% does not revive the earlier reinvestment facility. Obsolete 3.8.3.4/3.8.3.7 cross-references remain disclosed as draft defects.

operative_change.summary: Interest-rate futures position limits in the draft FPI master circular.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: For eligible Category I/II FPIs other than individuals, family offices and corporates, aggregate IRF net-long positions are capped at INR 5,000 crore and each FPI at INR 1,800 crore. Net shorts are not counted in that aggregate; the government-securities investment limit is separate. Other Category I/II FPIs use trading-member position limits; Category II individuals, family offices and corporates use client limits. For the 8–11-year maturity bucket, the trading-member limit is the higher of 10% of open interest and INR 12 billion; the client limit is the higher of 3% and INR 4 billion. For 4–8 and 11–15 years, the corresponding amounts are INR 6 billion and INR 2 billion. Gross short IRFs may not exceed long government-securities and IRF positions. Exchanges enforce limits, publish aggregate net-long positions daily and issue 90%-utilisation alerts. A breaching FPI squares off excess within five trading days or contract expiry, whichever is earlier.

operative_change.summary: Voluntary write-off, escrow sale and IPEF reporting in the draft FPI master circular.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: An FPI with invalid registration or intending surrender that cannot sell may request write-off. It authorises waiver of all beneficial rights; the custodian extinguishes the holding in its books, reports a NIL-proceeds sale to SEBI/RBI, freezes the demat account and follows the surrender-NOC process. Monetary corporate benefits go to IPEF within 30 days of receipt; non-monetary benefits accumulate. Transfer written-off or deemed-written-off securities to an exchange-empanelled broker escrow within 30 days, using the sole listing exchange or otherwise NSE. The broker attempts sale at market prices; listed equity uses the regular platform, excluding the block window. Proceeds net of brokerage and statutory charges go to IPEF. The exchange monitors the broker, replaces it if needed, and reports quarterly under Annexure I within 15 days, including custodian, ISIN, quantities, movements, proceeds and IPEF transfers.

operative_change.summary: FPI granular ownership-disclosure triggers and exemptions in the draft FPI master circular.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Require full natural-person ownership/control/economic-interest disclosure without thresholds where more than 50% of Indian equity AUM is in a single corporate group (33% for the specified IFSC paragraph 7 route, tested separately for each segregated portfolio), or combined Indian-equity holdings exceed INR 50,000 crore across the FPI/group and ODI subscribers with more than 50% common ownership or common control. Count direct equity and ODI exposure without counting the underlying twice. Exemptions cover government investors, DDP-validated public retail funds, qualifying ETFs with less than 50% India-related exposure and qualifying listed entities, regulated pooled schemes meeting the less-than-25%-global-AUM group or less-than-50%-global-AUM Indian-equity tests, statutory restrictions while they last, new FPIs for 90 calendar days after first Indian-equity settlement, and wind-down to NIL within 180 days after surrender intimation. Qualifying university funds/endowments require less than 25% India exposure, global AUM above INR 10,000 crore, non-profit tax filings and an eligible jurisdiction. Deduct exempt group members for the INR 50,000 crore test; only the remaining non-exempt members disclose if still above it. Stop look-through at exempt entities. DDPs/custodians validate under a public SOP.

evidence.locator: Consultation paper Background and Public Consultation sections
evidence.supporting_text: The FPI Master Circular (last issued 30 May 2024, Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/70) consolidates SEBI's FPI/DDP guidelines. Several circulars have been issued since; SEBI proposes to update the Master Circular to incorporate them and, separately, to streamline/simplify its language and remove duplication and redundant transitory provisions. A draft of this updated and simplified Master Circular is placed at Annexure-I. Comments are invited by 26 December 2025. Issued on 5 December 2025.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Annexure-I draft Master Circular, paragraphs 1-6 (issuance, rescission and savings clause, authority)
evidence.supporting_text: On issuance, this Master Circular would rescind the Master Circular dated 30 May 2024 and all directions/instructions in the circulars listed in its Appendix (Annexure-A), to the extent relating to FPIs/DDPs. A standard savings clause preserves: (a) actions already taken under the rescinded Master Circular as if taken under the new one; (b) pending applications as if made under the new one; and (c) accrued rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties and pending investigations/proceedings/remedies under the rescinded Master Circular, unaffected by the rescission. The draft states it would be issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992.
evidence.quote:
shall not be affected by such rescission and shall be enforceable as if
the rescinded Master Circular had continued to be in force.
evidence.extraction_note: The original ellipsis quotation is replaced by a contiguous, source-verified excerpt. Savings wording expressly refers to the rescinded Master Circular.

evidence.locator: Table of Contents (Parts A-F and Annexures A-K)
evidence.supporting_text: The draft Master Circular is organised into: Part A - Registration of FPIs; Part B - Post-registration activities; Part C - KYC Requirements for FPIs; Part D - Investment Conditions for FPIs; Part E - Additional Disclosure Framework; Part F - Issuance of Offshore Derivative Instruments (ODIs); and Annexures A-K (rescinded-circulars list, CAF/declaration formats, Investor Charter, grievance mechanism, and reporting formats).
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates existing FPI registration procedure via the Common Application Form (CAF): simplified registration for related fund structures (footnoted to Circular .../2024/156, 12 Nov 2024); certificate of registration; DDP processing checks (country/FATF/fit-and-proper/category/regulatory checks); rejection-of-application handling and inter-DDP rejection database; NRI/OCI/RI constituent contribution-threshold conditions (25%/50% caps, LRS route, control restrictions, 2-year/90-day cure periods); relaxations for IFSC-based FPIs (footnoted to Circular .../2024/89, 27 Jun 2024); LEI requirements for non-individual FPIs; reliance on scanned copies pending physical verification; and guidance for specific entity types (banks, insurers, pension funds, discretionary-mandate regulated entities, IFSC applicants, Multiple-Investment-Manager structures).
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates: continuance/renewal of registration (3-year blocks, late-fee reactivation window, GS-FPI simplifications); name-change procedure; surrender of registration (NOC-based, account-closure conditions); change of Custodian/DDP; segregated-portfolio BO-disclosure triggers; reclassification of FPI category; change in jurisdiction status (Regulation 4(d)/(e)/(f), including UNSC sanctions-list handling, footnoted to Circular .../2024/77, 5 Jun 2024); change in material information (Type I/Type II material-change taxonomy and DDP reassessment duties, footnoted to Circular .../2024/76, 5 Jun 2024); post-expiry disposal of securities including the 5% IPEF financial-disincentive mechanism and compulsory write-off after the additional 180-day period (footnoted to Circular .../2024/77); GS-FPI transition provisions; DDP obligations; reporting; and Investor Charter/complaints-disclosure publication duties for DDPs.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Part C - KYC Requirements for FPIs (paragraphs 1-8)
evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates: KYC documentation requirements; sharing of KYC documents with banks for FPI bank-account opening; identification and verification of Beneficial Owners (full look-through basis); periodic KYC review timelines; data security; record-maintenance periods; general KYC guidelines; and the list of supporting documents required.
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Part D - Investment Conditions for FPIs (paragraphs 1-19)
evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates: investor-group-level investment-limit monitoring by Depositories (10% paid-up-capital aggregate cap, 2-working-day breach reporting); monitoring of investment limits of listed companies (Red Flag Alert activation, breach handling, disinvestment method); off-market transfer of securities; 'to be listed' shares; short sale; primary-market-issuance investment; transfer of rights entitlements; risk-management framework; FPI investment in debt securities and Corporate Debt Investment Limit (CDIL) allocation; position limits for stock/index derivatives, exchange-traded interest rate futures, currency derivatives and commodity derivatives (ETCDs); FPI investment in REITs/InvITs/AIFs; investment in corporate bonds under default; FPI-to-FDI reclassification procedure; write-off of securities held by FPIs; and the detailed mechanics for dealing with securities written off (escrow transfer, empanelled-broker disposal, exchange reporting).
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates the granular (full look-through, no-threshold) beneficial-ownership disclosure regime under Regulations 22(6)/22(7) of the FPI Regulations, 2019: identification criteria (>50% Indian-equity-AUM concentration in a single corporate group, or >INR 50,000 crore aggregate equity AUM; a 33% threshold applies to FPIs availing the IFSC relaxation); exemption criteria (Government/Government-related investors, Public Retail Funds, qualifying ETFs/listed entities from permissible jurisdictions); realignment timelines (10 trading days / 90 calendar days per trigger); and consequences of non-submission (footnoted in part to Circular .../2024/176, 17 Dec 2024).
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.locator: Part F - Issuance of Offshore Derivative Instruments (ODIs) (paragraphs 1-5)
evidence.supporting_text: Restates and consolidates the ODI regime (largely footnoted to Circular .../2024/176, 17 Dec 2024): dedicated ODI-only FPI registration (no proprietary investments, 'ODI' name suffix, GS exemption); prohibition on issuing ODIs with derivatives as reference/underlying, and on hedging ODIs with onshore derivative positions (fully hedged one-to-one with the same securities); the 20% non-proprietary-index threshold test; prohibition on synthetic short activity via ODIs; ODI-subscriber KYC/suspicious-transaction reporting; ODI reporting and control-system maintenance; the Additional Disclosure Framework for ODI subscribers (look-through disclosure, the 50%-single-corporate-group exposure limit, exemption criteria, Depository monitoring systems); and transitory provisions for FPIs/ODIs outstanding as of 17 December 2024 (1-year redemption/hedging/dedicated-registration windows).
evidence.extraction_note: Extracted text inspected.

evidence.supporting_text: Lists 12 circulars that would stand rescinded (to the extent relating to FPIs/DDPs) upon issuance of this Master Circular: the 30 May 2024 Master Circular itself, plus 11 subsequent amending circulars dated between 5 June 2024 and 10 September 2025 covering material-change disclosures, post-expiry security disposal, IFSC/NRI-OCI-RI participation, additional-disclosure amendments (twice), CAF annexure modification, FPI-to-FDI reclassification, simplified registration, ODI/segregated-portfolio regulatory-arbitrage measures, an implementation-timeline extension for the ODI measures, and ease of compliance for Government-Securities-only FPIs.

evidence.locator: Annexures B-K - forms, declarations, Investor Charter, grievance mechanism, illustrations and reporting formats
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure B: reference to the Common Application Form and its Annexure (Declarations/Undertakings). Annexure C: IFSC-FPI declaration format re Para 7.1 of Part A. Annexures D-H: further prescribed declaration/reporting formats referenced elsewhere in the draft (e.g. NRI/OCI/RI reporting, material-change reporting, GS-FPI declarations). Address proofs include government/regulator records, utility bills no older than two months, bank statements no older than three months, and appropriately notarised, apostilled or consularised custodian powers of attorney. Revised framework: exchanges may set trading hours 08:45 AM-05:00 PM and provide a separate block deal window(s); a Morning Block Deal Window operates 08:45-09:00 with reference price = previous day closing price, and an Afternoon Block Deal Window operates 02:05 PM-02:20 PM with reference price = VWAP of cash-segment trades executed 01:45-02:00 PM (exchanges compute and disseminate the VWAP between 02:00-02:05 PM); orders must be within +3% of the applicable reference price subject to surveillance measures and price bands; minimum order size for block deal windows is INR 25 crore; every trade must result in delivery and shall not be squared off or reversed; exchanges disseminate block deal details to the public on the same day after market hours; the provisions also apply to the block deal window under the optional T+0 settlement cycle.

events.title: Single-stock F&O risk framework - FutEq Open Interest, redefined MWPL, ban-period rule, intraday MWPL monitoring and recalibrated entity-level limits
events.scope_description: SEBI adopts portfolio-level net Delta-adjusted (FutEq) Open Interest measurement (para 5.1, already implemented), redefines the single-stock Market Wide Position Limit as the lower of 15% of free float and 65x Average Daily Delivery Value with a 10% floor recalculated quarterly (para 5.2, from October 01, 2025), requires that trading during a ban period reduce an entity's end-of-day FutEq OI (para 5.3, from October 01, 2025), requires Stock Exchanges to perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times per session with surveillance actions and SEBI reporting (para 5.4, from November 03, 2025), and recalibrates individual entity-level combined futures-and-options position limits for single stocks to the new MWPL definition (para 5.8, from October 01, 2025), with joint SOPs to be prepared with SEBI.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular strengthens risk monitoring and position-limit controls in the equity derivatives market operated by Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations - infrastructure risk-management, surveillance and trading-mechanism regulation within the Financial Regulatory (FR) practice.

affected_entities.scope_note: Stock Exchanges compute FutEq OI and MWPL, run ban-period and intraday-utilisation monitoring, apply index and single-stock position limits, extend the pre-open session, apply non-benchmark-index eligibility criteria and prepare joint SOPs with SEBI.
Clearing Corporations disseminate FutEq OI, provide Average Daily Delivery Value inputs for MWPL, monitor positions and prepare joint SOPs with SEBI.

affected_entities.scope_note: FPI category-wise position limits for index futures and single stocks are recalibrated; FPIs must report cash / securities holdings for additional-exposure monitoring.
Mutual Fund position limits for index and single-stock derivatives are recalibrated to the new formulation.

affected_entities.scope_note: Trading members (proprietary and proprietary+client) and clients are subject to the recalibrated index and single-stock position limits and the ban-period FutEq OI reduction rule.

affected_instruments.description: Equity index and single-stock futures and options (cash-settled) whose open-interest measurement, market-wide and entity-level position limits and ban-period rules are changed.

legal_effects.description: Modifies Clauses 3.3.2.1.1 (MWPL), 3.3.2.1.2.1 (ban-period test), 3.3.2 and 4.3.2 (single-stock entity limits) of Chapter 5 of the December 30, 2024 Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Passive increases in FutEq OI from scrip movement and sign changes are not treated as breaches / acceptable reductions respectively; para 5.1 (FutEq OI) is already implemented.

legal_effects.description: Tightens and re-bases the single-stock derivatives risk controls: a delivery-linked MWPL formula with a floor, a stricter end-of-day FutEq OI reduction rule during ban periods, mandatory intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring, and recalibrated entity-level position limits.

operative_change.summary: Single-stock F&O risk controls move to FutEq OI, a delivery-linked MWPL formula, a stricter ban-period rule, mandatory intraday MWPL monitoring and recalibrated entity-level limits.
operative_change.previous_position: MWPL for single stocks was 20% of the number of shares held by non-promoters (free float); Stock Exchanges tested at end of day whether market-wide Open Interest for a scrip exceeded 95% of MWPL; existing combined futures-and-options entity limits were linked to that MWPL.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Open Interest is measured as portfolio-level net Delta-adjusted FutEq OI; MWPL for single stocks is the lower of 15% of free float and 65x Average Daily Delivery Value across Clearing Corporations, floored at 10% of free float, recalculated quarterly; the 95%-of-MWPL ban test is applied to FutEq OI and any trading during a ban period must reduce end-of-day FutEq OI; Stock Exchanges perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times per session; entity-level single-stock limits are recalibrated to the new MWPL (Client/NRI 10%, TM proprietary 20%, TM proprietary+client / FPI Cat I / MF 30%, FPI Cat II tiers 20% / 10%).

actions.description: Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations shall compute FutEq OI and the redefined MWPL, apply the FutEq-OI-based ban-period test and the end-of-day FutEq OI reduction rule, and apply the recalibrated entity-level single-stock position limits.

Stock Exchanges shall perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times during each trading session, take actions such as Additional Surveillance Margin on breach of limits, and report significant utilisation / breach of MWPL to SEBI in the fortnightly Surveillance meeting.

Clearing Corporations / Stock Exchanges shall prepare joint SOPs in consultation with SEBI for monitoring end-of-day delta positions, intraday MWPL utilisation and top-entity concentration, with the associated penalty structure.

effective_from.raw_text: Effective From October 01, 2025 (per the phased implementation table for measures 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8; measure 5.1 is already implemented and measure 5.4 is effective November 03, 2025)

deadlines.obligation: Measure 5.4 (intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring for single stocks) becomes effective.

Stock Exchanges / Clearing Corporations shall prepare a joint Standard Operating Procedure in consultation with SEBI for monitoring positions and the associated penalty / additional-surveillance-margin framework.

timing.raw_text: within one month / 30 days from the date of the circular

transitional_provisions.condition: Measure 5.1 (FutEq Open Interest measurement) is already implemented at the date of the circular; measures 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8 take effect October 01, 2025 and measure 5.4 takes effect November 03, 2025.
transitional_provisions.rule: The single-stock risk-framework measures are phased in on the stated dates, generally aligned with the monthly compliance mock sessions on the first Saturday of the month.

operative_status.reason: As issued on May 29, 2025 measures 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8 take effect October 01, 2025 and measure 5.4 November 03, 2025, all future dates at the assessment date (measure 5.1 is already implemented).

earlier_document_relationships.savings_or_limitations: Modification confined to the identified Chapter 5 single-stock MWPL / ban-period / entity-limit clauses.

legal_effects.description: Modifies Clauses 1.3.2-1.3.5 (index futures) and 2.3.2-2.3.4 (index options) of Chapter 5 of the December 30, 2024 Master Circular to incorporate the new index position limits, additional-position-limit tiers, monitoring mechanics, glide-path facilitation and passive-breach protections, as reproduced in Annexure-1.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Passive breaches from a drop in market OI are not treated as violations; the glide path applies only from July 01, 2025 to December 05, 2025.

legal_effects.description: Introduces PAN-level net and gross FutEq OI limits for index options and category-wise gross-notional limits for index futures, with the July 2025 - December 2025 glide-path intimation and position-reduction obligations.

operative_change.summary: New PAN-level index options FutEq OI limits and category-wise index futures limits, phased via a July-December 2025 glide path for options.
operative_change.previous_position: There were no market-wide position limits for index futures or index options; Chapter 5 Clauses 1.3.2-1.3.5 and 2.3.2-2.3.4 set out the earlier trading-member / FPI / MF / client index position-limit arrangements.
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Index options: PAN-level net end-of-day FutEq OI limit Rs. 1,500 cr and gross FutEq OI limit Rs. 10,000 cr, with a glide path (T / T+1 intimation and position-reduction, Additional Surveillance Deposit on failure) from July 01, 2025 to December 05, 2025 and normal implementation from December 06, 2025. Additional exposure permitted only against stock holdings (short) or cash and equivalents (long).

events.title: Prudential eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices from November 03, 2025 (para 5.7)
events.scope_description: In addition to the existing eligibility criteria, Stock Exchanges must apply prudential norms before introducing derivatives on non-benchmark indices: minimum 14 constituents, top constituent weight <= 20%, combined weight of the top three constituents <= 45%, and a descending weight structure. Compliance is evaluated at the end of every calendar quarter, and exchanges must submit proposals for non-benchmark indices with existing derivatives to SEBI within 30 days of the circular. Effective from November 03, 2025.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2025/79 dated May 29, 2025, addressed to all Stock Exchanges and all Clearing Corporations (except Commodity Derivatives Exchanges and Clearing Corporations), titled 'Measures for Enhancing Trading Convenience and Strengthening Risk Monitoring in Equity Derivatives'.

Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations provide the platform, products, risk management and surveillance for the derivatives market; Regulation 28(2) read with Part-C of Schedule II of the SECC Regulations, 2018 treats risk management, surveillance and product development as core functions; SEBI deliberated with an Expert Working Group on derivatives, issued a consultation paper on February 24, 2025, examined comments and deliberated in the Secondary Market Advisory Committee, and has decided to put in place measures to strengthen the equity derivatives framework, with implementation timelines at paragraph 6.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 5.1-5.4 (OI formulation, MWPL, ban-period, intraday monitoring)
evidence.supporting_text: Open Interest is to be measured at portfolio level as net Delta-adjusted (Future Equivalent, FutEq) open positions across futures and options for an underlying; Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL) for single stocks is redefined as the lower of 15% of free float and 65x Average Daily Delivery Value across Clearing Corporations with a floor of 10% of free float, recalculated every three months; once market-wide FutEq OI exceeds 95% of MWPL the scrip enters a ban period and any trading by an entity must reduce its FutEq OI on an end-of-day basis (passive increases and sign changes are not acceptable reductions); Stock Exchanges shall perform intraday MWPL-utilisation monitoring at least four random times per session and take actions (e.g. Additional Surveillance Margin) and report significant utilisation to SEBI; Clearing Corporations / Stock Exchanges shall prepare joint SOPs in consultation with SEBI within one month / 30 days of the circular.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs 5.5-5.8 (index position limits, glide path, pre-open session, non-benchmark index eligibility, single-stock entity limits)
evidence.supporting_text: Index options: net end-of-day FutEq OI limit of Rs. 1,500 cr and gross FutEq OI limit of Rs. 10,000 cr at PAN level, with a glide path from July 01, 2025 to December 05, 2025 (T / T+1 intimation and position-reduction mechanics) and normal implementation from December 06, 2025; index futures: category-wise limits (FPI Category I / MF / TM proprietary / clients - higher of 15% of futures OI or Rs. 500 cr; FPI Category II tiers - 10% or 5% or Rs. 500 cr), measured on gross notional, effective July 01, 2025, with passive-breach protection; additional exposure permitted subject to short/long index positions not exceeding stock / cash holdings; pre-open session extended to current-month (and, in the last five days before expiry, next-month) single-stock and index futures from December 06, 2025; new prudential eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices (minimum 14 constituents, top weight <=20%, top-three combined <=45%, descending weights) from November 03, 2025, evaluated each calendar quarter; individual entity-level combined futures-and-options position limits for single stocks recalibrated to the new MWPL definition (Client/NRI 10%, TM proprietary 20%, TM proprietary+client / FPI Cat I / MF 30%, FPI Cat II tiers 20% / 10%) from October 01, 2025.

evidence.locator: Paragraph 6 (phased implementation table with an 'Effective From' column)
evidence.supporting_text: The phased implementation table at paragraph 6 states, in its 'Effective From' column, the date each measure becomes effective: measure 5.1 (FutEq Open Interest) is already implemented; measure 5.2 (MWPL definition) is effective from October 01, 2025; measure 5.3 (position creation during ban period) is effective from October 01, 2025; measure 5.4 (intraday MWPL monitoring) is effective from November 03, 2025; measure 5.5 position limits for index futures are effective from July 01, 2025, and for index options the glide path runs from July 01, 2025 to December 05, 2025 with normal implementation effective from December 06, 2025; measure 5.6 (pre-open session for the derivatives market) is effective from December 06, 2025; measure 5.7 (eligibility criteria for derivatives on non-benchmark indices) is effective from November 03, 2025; measure 5.8 (individual entity-level position limits for single stocks) is effective from October 01, 2025.

Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations are directed to put in place systems for implementation including necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) read with Section 11(2)(a) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the SECC Regulations, 2018; the circular is available on the SEBI website.
Issued by the General Manager, Technology, Process Re-engineering, Data Analytics, Market Regulation Department, SEBI.

evidence.locator: Annexure-1 (modified Chapter 5 clauses for index position limits)
evidence.supporting_text: Annexure-1 reproduces the modified Clauses 1.3.2-1.3.5 (index futures) and 2.3.2-2.3.4 (index options) of Chapter 5 of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024, incorporating the new index position limits, the additional-position-limit tiers, end-of-day and intraday monitoring mechanics, the glide-path facilitation for index options (July 01 to December 05, 2025) and the passive-breach protections.

evidence.supporting_text: A SEBI working group reviewed EBP-platform feedback; following public consultation and internal evaluation, specified provisions of Master Circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/PoD1/P/CIR/2024/54 dated 22 May 2024, Chapter VI (EBP platform), Chapter VII (listing timelines for private placement) and Chapter XV (reporting of primary issuances), are modified.
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Mandatory EBP-platform issuance thresholds for private placement of debt securities/NCRPS (under NCS Regulations) and municipal debt securities (under Municipal Debt Securities Regulations 2015): a single issue of Rs 20 crore or more (incl. green shoe), a shelf issue cumulatively Rs 20 crore or more in a financial year, or a subsequent issue where the issuer's aggregate issuances in the year equal/exceed Rs 20 crore.
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Issuers may voluntarily access the EBP platform for private placement of securitised debt instruments, security receipts, CPs or CDs, and REIT/SM REIT/InvIT unit placements, and for debt/NCRPS/municipal-debt issuances below the Rs 20 crore mandatory threshold.
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: The issuer must provide the Placement Memorandum and term sheet to the EBP at least two working days before issue opening (three working days for a first-time EBP issuer); the green shoe portion may not exceed five times the base issue size, and issue-wise green shoe exercise versus base size in the prior financial year must be disclosed in the offer document.
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Where two or more bids are at the cut-off coupon/price/spread, allotment is made pro-rata, illustrated in Annexure-VI A (illustrated further in this circular's own Annexure-A).
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: Anchor-investor allocation is capped by instrument rating (AAA/AA+/AA/AA- up to 30%, A+/A- up to 40%, others up to 50% of base issue size); anchor allocation must be disclosed in the placement memorandum/term sheet; anchor investor details and quantum must be disclosed to the EBP, with anchor investors confirming participation electronically by T-1, unconfirmed amounts reverting to the base issue.
evidence.extraction_note: All eight source pages reviewed; tables on pages 3, 5, 7 and 8 visually checked.

evidence.supporting_text: EBPs must update a specified list of issuance details (bidding date, issuer, ISIN, issue description, allotment date, face value, credit rating, pricing/yield, allotment/settlement manner, document links, issue size, coupon, tenor, bidder categories and bidding/acceptance amounts, cut-off yield/price) on their website by end of T-day or 1 p.m. on T+1 day depending on closing time.

events.title: Simplified yield-to-price computation on the RFQ platform (new clause 9, Chapter XXII)
events.scope_description: SEBI inserts a new clause 9 in Chapter XXII of the NCS Master Circular so that, for securities traded on the exchange RFQ platform, cash flow dates for interest / dividend / redemption are, for yield-to-price computation, not adjusted for day count convention and are based on the due date per the cash flow schedule rather than the date of payment. Effective with effect from August 18, 2025.

events.scope_description: SEBI inserts a new paragraph 57 in Annex-XIV-A of the NCS Master Circular requiring debt issuers to provide the cash flow schedule for interest / dividend / redemption in the centralized corporate bond database at the time of ISIN activation in a prescribed format, and to update any change within one working day. evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSPOD1/P/CIR/2025/72 dated May 13, 2025, addressed to issuers who have listed Non-convertible Securities, Securitised Debt Instruments, Municipal Debt Securities and Commercial Paper; Recognised Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations; Registered Depositories; and Stock Brokers and Depository Participants; on simplification of the operational process and clarification of cash flow disclosure in the Corporate Bond Database pursuant to a review of the Request for Quote (RFQ) Platform framework.

Chapter XXII of the SEBI NCS Master Circular dated May 22, 2024 stipulates trade execution and settlement of trades on the RFQ platform; to simplify yield-to-price computation for non-convertible securities, cash flow dates for payment of interest / dividend / redemption for securities traded on the RFQ platform shall, for yield-to-price computation, not be adjusted for day count convention and shall be based on the due date of payment as per the cash flow schedule and not the date of payment; a new clause 9 to that effect is inserted in Chapter XXII of the NCS Master Circular.

evidence.locator: Item 2 (cash flow disclosure in centralized corporate bond database)
evidence.supporting_text: Clause 3.3.34 of Schedule I of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021 requires issuers to disclose cash flow with the date of interest / dividend / redemption payment per day count convention in the offer document; Chapter XIV of the NCS Master Circular requires issuers to submit and update information in the centralized database at ISIN activation and post-listing, but the cash flow schedule is not currently captured; a new paragraph 57 is inserted in Annex-XIV-A requiring issuers to provide the cash flow schedule for interest / dividend / redemption in the centralized corporate bond database at ISIN activation in a prescribed format (particulars, due date, payment date as per day count convention), and to update any change within one working day.

The disclosure requirement is applicable for prospective issuances of debt securities and for the residual maturity of ISINs already listed; the circular shall come into force with effect from August 18, 2025.

The Stock Exchanges are directed to bring the circular to the notice of market participants, disseminate it and make necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules and regulations; the circular is issued under Section 11(1) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 55(1) of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021; issued by the General Manager, Department of Debt and Hybrid Securities, SEBI.
