events.title: Non-binding FAQ clarifying the SEBI (REIT) Regulations framework for Small and Medium REITs
events.scope_description: A 38-question FAQ that explains, without binding force, concepts and provisions of the SEBI (REIT) Regulations, 2014 as they apply to Small and Medium REITs (Chapter VIB): the reduced asset size (rupees 50 crores; rupees 50-500 crores per scheme); the multi-scheme, mutual-fund-like structure with segregation and ring-fencing; SPV sole and direct ownership of assets; Investment Manager eligibility (Regulation 26J(2)(d)), India incorporation, fee disclosure and the unitholder-approval threshold for fee changes; the bar on related-party transactions (including warehousing and AIF group-company sales); the public issue of scheme units through the stock-exchange book-building platform with a merchant banker and a 21-day public comment period for the draft offer document; the 95% completed-revenue-generating investment condition and 5% liquid-asset limit; total expense ratio disclosure; the prohibition on carried interest; delisting and winding-up where a scheme has no assets for over six months; prior SEBI and unitholder approval for a change in control of the Investment Manager; the migration of existing fractional real estate structures and the related exemptions (5% minimum unitholding, Regulation 26P(2) asset-size and 200-unitholder requirements) for structures existing as on 8 March 2024 subject to timing conditions; leverage under Regulation 26U(5); the rupees ten lakh minimum unit price and odd-value handling; and naming restrictions. The FAQ expressly states it is not a legal document, not an interpretation of law and not a binding opinion or guidance.

classification.practice_rationale: The document explains the SEBI (REIT) Regulations, 2014 framework for Small and Medium REITs - a trust issuance/lifecycle subject (asset size, scheme structure, Investment Manager eligibility, offer document, fees, leverage, delisting and migration). evidence.supporting_text: Document titled 'Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) - Framework for Small and Medium REITs (SM REITs)', issued on June 18, 2024. Disclaimer: this is not a legal document; the FAQs offer only a simplistic explanation/clarification of terms/concepts related to the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 ('REIT Regulations') and should not be regarded as an interpretation of law nor a binding opinion/guidance from SEBI; for full particulars refer to the Acts/Regulations/Circulars on the SEBI website.

Existing REITs must have assets of at least rupees 500 crores; the SM REIT framework allows a reduced asset value of rupees 50 crores. A single SM REIT can launch multiple schemes (similar to mutual funds), each holding different real estate assets and each with its own set of unitholders, unlike the single-pool existing REIT structure.

Any company, including a real estate developer, that satisfies the Investment Manager eligibility conditions under Regulation 26J(2)(d) can act as the Investment Manager of a SM REIT; however, if a developer is the Investment Manager it cannot transfer its own assets to the SM REIT because the SM REIT framework does not permit related party transactions.

The REIT Regulations do not restrict who may be a tenant, but a SM REIT shall not enter into any transaction with related parties (term defined in Regulation 2(1)(zo)); a developer may be a tenant if not a related party. The Investment Manager may launch multiple schemes under a single SM REIT provided the assets, bank accounts, investment/demat accounts and books of accounts of each scheme are segregated and ring-fenced.

A 'scheme' is a distinct and separate scheme of a SM REIT for owning real estate assets through special purpose vehicles (SPVs), structurally similar to distinct schemes in a mutual fund, with segregation/ring-fencing of scheme assets and accounts. A single scheme can invest in multiple SPVs; each SPV must directly and solely own all assets acquired by the scheme of which it is a wholly owned subsidiary; multiple SPVs cannot jointly own a single property.

There is no limit on the number of real estate assets a single SPV can hold; the collective value of assets under a single scheme must be at least rupees fifty crores and not exceed rupees five hundred crores. Multiple schemes may exist under a SM REIT with no cap on the collective value of assets across schemes (e.g. three schemes of rupees 450 crores each, totalling rupees 1350 crores, is permitted).

For the purpose of SM REITs (Chapter VIB), the definition of 'SPV' under Regulation 26H(f) applies (per Regulation 26H). A SM REIT cannot acquire any asset from an entity within the definition of 'related party'; warehousing a property in a related entity of the Investment Manager, or an AIF Category II fund whose Investment Manager is a group company of the SM REIT's Investment Manager selling assets to the SM REIT, is not permitted.

There is no guideline capping the Investment Manager's fees as on the date of the FAQ; at the initial offer of the scheme the Investment Manager must disclose the fees charged to the scheme, and any change in the Investment Manager's fees requires unitholder approval where votes cast in favour are not less than one and a half times the votes cast against.

The Investment Manager must apply for delisting of the scheme's units if there are no projects or assets under the scheme for a period exceeding six months (extendable by a further six months with unitholder approval as specified in Regulation 26ZM); the scheme is subject to delisting and winding up if all assets are gradually sold and proceeds distributed. Prior approval of SEBI and of unitholders is required for a shareholding change in the Investment Manager amounting to a change in control ('change in control' defined in Regulation 2(1)(g)) and for any change in the Investment Manager by removal or otherwise.

The REIT Regulations do not restrict the shareholders or promoters of the Investment Manager, but the Investment Manager must be a company incorporated in India and meet the eligibility criteria, and its shareholding pattern and other prescribed details must be submitted to SEBI at the time of the registration application. The REIT Regulations do not envisage a separate distributor; the public issue of scheme units is made through the stock exchange platform with appointment of a merchant banker. The draft scheme offer document, once filed with SEBI, must be hosted for public comments on the websites of SEBI, designated stock exchanges and associated merchant bankers for a minimum period of twenty-one days; marketing by the merchant banker is permitted after the draft is filed and made public, and public communications must not be misleading.

The scheme offer document must disclose the total expense ratio; the REIT Regulations do not prescribe a threshold ratio of 'Other Expenses' to Asset Cost, nor a minimum cap rate (net rental yield), but the scheme must invest at least ninety-five per cent of the value of the scheme's assets in completed and revenue-generating properties. The Investment Manager must use the book building platform of the stock exchanges to accept bids; a fixed-price issue is not envisaged. Migration of existing fractional real estate structures is not mandatory if the structure does not fall within the REIT definition; an applicant must undertake due migration of existing structures and submit a migration plan with the registration application; the SM REIT's trademark, brand name, website and other communication media must be used exclusively for SM REIT activities.

The SM REIT's trademark, brand name and website must be used exclusively for the SM REIT and cannot be used for other SEBI-regulated entities such as an AIF. On migration, the Investment Manager's five per cent minimum unitholding is exempt for units issued against a swap of securities allotted prior to the notification of the SM REIT framework (March 08, 2024), subject to the applicant applying for registration within six months of the notification and completing migration within six months of the grant of registration; the Regulation 26P(2) asset-size and minimum-200-unitholder requirements are likewise not applicable to such migration. The REIT Regulations prescribe no approval threshold from existing security holders for migration, which must follow the extant legal and contractual rights (including drag-along, buy-back, buy-out or redemption).

The Investment Manager (or its group company) must segregate its SM REIT management activity from its other activities, and must have adequate infrastructure and sufficient key personnel; while doing other activities it must comply with the exclusive-use rule for the SM REIT's trademark, brand name, website and communication media. Performance-linked fees such as 'carried interest' are not allowed for SM REITs.

Any asset falling under 'infrastructure' cannot be treated as 'real estate' or 'property' for SM REIT purposes, so a warehousing facility classified as infrastructure cannot be held by a SM REIT unless it is common infrastructure forming part of composite real estate projects, industrial parks and SEZ. The scheme must invest at least ninety-five per cent of the value of its assets in completed and revenue-generating properties, with up to five per cent in unencumbered liquid assets; tenant security deposits do not form part of scheme assets; reserves created out of profits may be distributed; where reserves/other investments exceed five per cent the Investment Manager must reallocate to maintain the ninety-five per cent threshold. The total expense ratio encompasses all annual operating expenses, including management, advisory, trustee and audit fees, and must be disclosed in the scheme offer document.

Residential properties can be held by a SM REIT if they satisfy the definition of 'real estate'/'property' in Regulation 2(1)(zi) and are completed and revenue-generating; under-construction or non-revenue-generating properties and vacant land cannot be held. The Investment Manager may undertake facility and property management of SM REIT properties directly (or through appointed agents), but not through a related party; payment of fees by the SM REIT to the Investment Manager and Trustee for carrying out SM REIT activities is permitted.

The value of real estate assets in each scheme of a SM REIT must remain at least fifty crore rupees, and the Investment Manager must apply for delisting to SEBI and the stock exchanges if there are no assets under the scheme for a period exceeding six months (extendable by six months with unitholder approval). The minimum price of each unit of a scheme is rupees ten lakhs; on migration, existing structures must align investment value to multiples of rupees ten lakhs before migration, for example by inter-se sale/purchase, by SPV buy-back or redemption of a portion of existing securities, or by establishing a trust to consolidate odd-value units and dispose of them in the market within one year of migration, distributing net proceeds to the affected holders.

For convertible debentures issued by an existing SPV being migrated to a SM REIT, the applicant may convert them to equity of the SPV before migration; if not converted, they may be swapped for units of the scheme of SM REIT (which then holds the convertible debentures), and the existing debenture holders receive scheme units. Borrowings made by the SPV through convertible debentures held by the scheme of SM REIT are not included in the leverage limit under Regulation 26U(5), which applies at scheme level. An applicant seeking registration as a SM REIT may apply under a name that is not suggestive of Government of India patronage; the proposed name must not contain the words 'India', 'Indian', 'National' or 'Bharat' etc.

events.title: Employee OFS bids to be placed at cut-off price of T day (was T+1 day)
events.scope_description: SEBI amends paragraph 5(vi) of the January 23, 2024 Framework for OFS of Shares to Employees so that employees place bids on T+1 day at the cut-off price of T day, with the allotment price based on the T-day cut-off (subject to discount), replacing the earlier reference to the T+1-day cut-off; all other provisions of the OFS framework and the OFS-to-employees framework remain unchanged. The change takes effect from the 30th day after issuance.

events.title: Framework for computing an 'unaffected price' (adjusted VWAP) for listed-entity transactions where a market rumour is confirmed
events.scope_description: Operationalises the second proviso to LODR Regulation 30(11): where a listed entity confirms, within 24 hours of the trigger of material price movement, a market rumour pertaining to a transaction on which SEBI or stock-exchange pricing norms apply, an 'unaffected price' must be used. The Annexure prescribes the method - exclude the WAP variation attributable to the material price movement and rumour confirmation from the daily WAP over the look-back period, compute the adjusted VWAP, handle price-band hits, apply the unaffected price for 60 or 180 days by transaction stage until the relevant date, and re-apply on each subsequent material rumour confirmation. Applicable to the top 100 listed entities from 1 June 2024 and to the top 250 from 1 December 2024.

classification.practice_rationale: The dominant subject is a listed-entity disclosure obligation - verifying market rumours under LODR Regulation 30(11) and deriving an 'unaffected price' for the entity's own pricing-normed transactions (e.g. preferential issue / QIP) - which is CM (listed-entity obligations and issuer fundraising pricing). FR is a material secondary practice because recognised stock exchanges must issue the material-price-movement framework and the transaction stages / applicability period are to be fixed in Industry Standards on Regulation 30(11).

evidence.supporting_text: Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/51 dated May 21, 2024, issued by SEBI.
Addressed to All listed entities and All the recognized Stock Exchanges.
Subject: Framework for considering unaffected price for transactions upon confirmation of market rumour.

In terms of Regulation 30(11) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, as amended by SEBI (LODR) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024, a listed entity is required to verify market rumours upon material price movement; the stock exchanges shall issue the framework for material price movement on their websites.

As per the second proviso to Regulation 30(11) of LODR Regulations, unaffected price shall be considered for transactions on which pricing norms specified by SEBI or the stock exchanges are applicable, provided the rumour pertaining to such transaction has been confirmed within 24 hours from the trigger of material price movement. The unaffected price is to be considered by excluding the effect on the price of the equity shares due to the material price movement and confirmation of the rumour. The framework for considering unaffected price is placed as Annexure and shall be applicable to the top 100 listed entities with effect from June 01, 2024 and to the top 250 listed entities (i.e. the next top 150) with effect from December 01, 2024.
The Stock Exchanges are advised to bring the contents of this circular to the notice of their listed entities and ensure its compliance.
Issued in exercise of powers under Section 11(1) and 11A of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with Regulation 101 of the LODR Regulations.
Signed by Raj Kumar Das, Deputy General Manager, Corporation Finance Department.

The adjusted volume weighted average price (VWAP) for the unaffected price is computed as follows: the variation in daily WAP from the day of material price movement till the end of the next trading day after confirmation of the rumour is attributed to the rumour and its confirmation (WAP variation); the adjusted daily WAP is calculated by excluding the WAP variation from the daily WAP in the look-back period from the day of the material price movement onwards; the adjusted daily WAP from the day of material price movement till the end of the next trading day after confirmation is set equal to the daily WAP on the trading day preceding the day of material price movement; and the adjusted VWAP for the look-back period is calculated from the adjusted daily WAP.

Illustration for calculation of VWAP for a preferential issue to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018: Table 1 tabulates trading day, daily WAP, adjusted daily WAP and shares traded, marking the date of material price movement, date of rumour confirmation, next trading day after confirmation, T-1 and the Relevant Date (T) being the date of board approval to the preferential issue to QIBs. The dates in the illustration (July/August) are a worked hypothetical, not operative dates.

The worked explanation: the WAP variation in the illustration is Rs. 118.14; the adjusted daily WAP from the day of material price movement until the end of the next trading day after confirmation equals the daily WAP on the preceding trading day (Rs. 1060.76); from the following day the adjusted daily WAP is the daily WAP minus the WAP variation; VWAP in the look-back period (T-1 to T-10) using daily WAP is Rs. 1,175.78 and using the adjusted daily WAP is Rs. 1,069.80.

If the price variation due to the rumour confirmation hits the price band limit on the next trading day post confirmation, the price variation in subsequent trading days is included for adjustment until the day the price does not hit the band limit.
The unaffected price applies only if the listed entity confirmed the rumour pertaining to the transaction within 24 hours from the trigger of material price movement.

Where a rumour pertaining to a transaction has been confirmed and a subsequent rumour with a material update requiring confirmation under Regulation 30(11) is reported in the mainstream media, the unaffected price applies for each instance of confirmation of the rumour.

events.title: Public-issue share listing timeline reduced from T+6 to T+3 working days (with phased applicability)
events.scope_description: SEBI reduces the time to list specified securities after closure of a public issue from 6 working days (T+6) to 3 working days (T+3), with 'T' being the issue closing date, prescribing a revised end-to-end process timeline in the Annexure, an offer-document and advertisement disclosure of the T+3 timeline, SCSB and Registrar PAN-verification steps, computation of investor compensation for delayed unblocking from T+3 day, and lock-in operationalization per the Depositories' SOP. The provisions apply on a voluntary basis for public issues opening on or after September 1, 2023 and mandatorily for those opening on or after December 1, 2023, and modify the timelines in seven earlier SEBI circulars to that extent.

classification.practice_rationale: The circular compresses the timeline for listing shares after a public issue and its associated process (a public-equity-issue / offer-process matter within Capital Markets, CM); it also imposes process, verification and reporting duties on stock exchanges, depositories, RTAs, SCSBs and sponsor banks, giving a Financial Regulatory (FR) secondary workflow.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Issuers making a public issue of specified securities
affected_entities.scope_note: Issuers must disclose the T+3 listing timeline in offer documents and advertisements and comply with the revised public-issue process timeline.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Registered Merchant Bankers (BRLMs) to the public issue
affected_entities.scope_note: Merchant bankers manage the public issue against the compressed T+3 timeline and the bid-information / UPI reporting requirements.
Stock exchanges validate bid details, approve the basis of allotment and issue trading notices within the compressed timeline.
Depositories effect the corporate action for credit of shares and operationalize lock-in per their SOP within the T+3 timeline.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
affected_entities.scope_note: The Registrar undertakes third-party PAN verification (demat vs bank account), finalizes rejections and the basis of allotment within the compressed timeline.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Self Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs) / Bankers to an Issue / Sponsor Banks
affected_entities.scope_note: SCSBs perform the PAN-match check before blocking ASBA monies and submit final certificates; sponsor and issuer banks handle fund transfer and unblocking within the T+3 timeline.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Applicants / investors in the public issue
affected_entities.scope_note: Investors benefit from faster listing and from compensation for delayed unblocking of ASBA monies computed from T+3 day.

affected_instruments.description: Specified securities (shares) offered in a public issue whose post-issue-closure listing timeline is reduced from T+6 to T+3 working days.

classification_support.reason: CM/CM_ECM_PUBLIC and TX_IPO/TX_FPO/TX_IPO_OFS from the public-issue listing subject-matter; FR_MARKETS_CASH and the exchange/depository/RTA/bank entities from the process, verification and settlement duties; IN_EQUITY from the specified securities; TP_ALLOTMENT and TP_MARKET_EXECUTION from the basis-of-allotment and listing process; TP_OFFER_DOCUMENT from the disclosure requirement; TP_KYC from the PAN-match verification; TP_LOCK_IN from the pre-issue-share lock-in operationalization; TP_INVESTOR_PROTECTION from the faster listing and the compensation-from-T+3 rule; FW_ICDR from Schedule VI and the advertisement provisions, FW_SEBI_ACT from sections 11 and 11A.

legal_effects.description: Reduces the post-issue-closure listing timeline for specified securities from T+6 working days to T+3 working days and prescribes the corresponding revised activity timeline.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Applies notwithstanding Schedule VI of the ICDR Regulations; phased applicability (voluntary from September 1, 2023; mandatory from December 1, 2023).

legal_effects.description: Modifies the timelines prescribed in the seven earlier SEBI circulars (dated November 1, 2018; June 28, 2019; November 8, 2019; March 30, 2020; March 16, 2021; June 2, 2021; April 20, 2022) to the extent stated, and partially modifies the March 16, 2021 and April 20, 2022 circulars so that investor compensation for delayed unblocking is computed from T+3 day.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Only the timeline and compensation-computation aspects are modified.

legal_effects.description: Introduces the SCSB PAN-match check before blocking ASBA monies (with confirmation to the Registrar) and the Registrar's third-party PAN verification (demat vs bank account), treating mismatches as invalid applications.

operative_change.summary: Public-issue share listing must occur within T+3 working days instead of T+6, with a revised process timeline and PAN-verification steps, phased in over September-December 2023.
operative_change.previous_position: Listing of specified securities after closure of a public issue was required within 6 working days (T+6 days), 'T' being the issue closing date; investor compensation for delayed unblocking of ASBA monies was computed under the March 16, 2021 and April 20, 2022 circulars (not from T+3 day).
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Listing within 3 working days (T+3 days); the Annexure prescribes the revised activity timeline; the T+3 timeline is disclosed in offer documents and advertisements; SCSBs and the Registrar perform PAN-match verification; investor compensation for delayed unblocking is computed from T+3 day; lock-in is operationalized per the Depositories' SOP dated August 08, 2023.

actions.description: The Issuer shall disclose the T+3 listing timeline in the offer documents and prominently in the pre-issue, issue-opening and issue-closing advertisements issued under the ICDR Regulations.

SCSBs shall verify that the PAN in the application matches the PAN linked to the applicant's bank account before blocking ASBA monies (with confirmation to the Registrar), and the Registrar shall undertake third-party PAN verification matching the demat-account PAN with the bank-account PAN, treating mismatches as invalid applications.

Stock exchanges, depositories, RTAs and banks shall put in place systems and processes to complete bid validation, basis-of-allotment finalization and approval, fund transfer and unblocking, corporate action for credit of shares, and listing/trading-notice filing within the compressed T+3 timeline set out in the Annexure.

notification.importance_reason: Halves the post-issue listing timeline for every public issue and re-times the entire issue-process workflow for issuers, merchant bankers, exchanges, depositories, RTAs and banks, with new PAN-verification duties and a phased mandatory date.

evidence.supporting_text: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/TPD1/CIR/P/2023/140 dated August 09, 2023, addressed to Recognized Stock Exchanges, Depositories, Registered Stock Brokers, Registered Merchant Bankers, Registered Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents, Registered Depository Participants, Registered Bankers to an Issue, Self Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs) and the National Payments Corporation of India, on reduction of the timeline for listing of shares in a public issue from T+6 days to T+3 days.

Following extensive consultation and public comments on a consultation paper, SEBI decides to reduce the time taken for listing of specified securities after the closure of a public issue to 3 working days (T+3), against the present 6 working days (T+6), 'T' being the issue closing date; the revised timelines for listing and the various public-issue-process activities are set out in the Annexure; the T+3 timeline shall be disclosed in the offer documents and prominently in the pre-issue, issue-opening and issue-closing advertisements issued by the Issuer under the ICDR Regulations, 2018.

For Direct Bank ASBA and Syndicate ASBA applications, prior to blocking application monies the SCSBs shall ensure the PAN in the application matches the PAN linked to the applicant's bank account (with a confirmation to the Registrar with the Final Certificate) and that this PAN is part of the bidding data on the Stock Exchange platform; the Registrar to an Issue shall undertake third-party verification by matching the PAN in the demat account with the PAN in the bank account, treating mismatches as invalid applications; lock-in of pre-issue shares shall be effected per the ICDR Regulations and operationalized per the Depositories' SOP dated August 08, 2023; in partial modification of circulars dated March 16, 2021 and April 20, 2022, investor compensation for delay in unblocking ASBA monies shall be computed from T+3 day.

Issued by the General Manager, SEBI (Corporation Finance Department).

events.title: Merchant banker engagement made discretionary for buy-backs; obligations re-assigned (new regulation 24A, Schedule V)
events.scope_description: A new regulation 24A makes engaging a merchant banker discretionary for a company undertaking a buy-back; where the company dispenses with the merchant banker, the obligations otherwise performed by the merchant banker are re-assigned among the company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges and compliance officer per a table. Consequential omissions are made in Schedule V. In force on August 1, 2026.

classification.practice_rationale: The instrument amends the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 - buy-back being a capital-return / control-transaction matter within the Corporate (CO) practice.

affected_entities.scope_note: Companies undertaking a buy-back, whose obligations, quantitative limits, timelines, disclosure requirements and merchant-banker engagement are changed.

affected_entities.scope_note: Where a merchant banker is not engaged, specified obligations are re-assigned among the company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges and compliance officer per the regulation 24A table.

affected_instruments.description: Shares or other specified securities of the company that are bought back and, in the case of promoter holdings, frozen at ISIN level during the buy-back period.

legal_effects.description: Inserts a new regulation 24A and makes consequential omissions in Schedule V of the Buy-Back Regulations, 2018.
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: Where a merchant banker is not engaged, the merchant banker's obligations must be undertaken by the specified substitute persons.

legal_effects.description: Removes the mandatory requirement to engage a merchant banker for a buy-back, making it a discretionary choice for the company.

operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: Notwithstanding anything in the regulations, engaging a merchant banker is discretionary for a company undertaking buy-back; if the company dispenses with the merchant banker it must ensure that the company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges and compliance officer undertake the specified obligations otherwise required of the merchant banker; consequential omissions are made in Schedule V.

actions.description: A company undertaking a buy-back that dispenses with the merchant banker shall ensure that the persons specified in the regulation 24A table (company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges, compliance officer) undertake the obligations otherwise required to be undertaken by the merchant banker.

events.title: Open-market buy-back quantitative limit and offer timeline tightened (regulation 4(iv)(b), regulation 17)
events.scope_description: With effect from August 1, 2026, a buy-back from the open market through the stock exchange must be less than fifteen per cent of the paid-up capital and free reserves of the company, based on both standalone and consolidated financial statements; the earlier proviso arrangement is limited to 'April 1, 2025 till July 31, 2026'. events.title: Buy-back cooling-off and MPS-breach prohibition, faster public announcement and shareholder intimation, and textual corrections (regulations 4(vii), 4(xi), 16, 22A and others)
events.scope_description: Regulation 4(vii) is substituted so a company shall not make any buy-back offer within the period prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 from the closure of the preceding offer; a new regulation 4(xi) prohibits a buy-back that results in breach of the minimum public shareholding requirements under the SCRR, 1957 or the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015; regulation 16(iv)(b) is substituted to require the public announcement within two working days of the board resolution or postal-ballot result, and a new regulation 16(iv)(ba) and regulation 22A(v) require the company to send an electronic intimation of an open-market buy-back offer to shareholders as on the public-announcement date within one working day. Numerous small textual and grammatical amendments are also made across regulations 8, 9, 11, 16, 20, 21 and 24 (marginal head), including substituting 'may' with 'shall' in regulation 20(ii) and revising the bank-guarantee validity/return wording in regulation 20(iv). In force on August 1, 2026.

legal_effects.description: Substitutes regulation 4(vii), inserts regulation 4(xi), substitutes regulation 16(iv)(b), inserts regulation 16(iv)(ba) and regulation 22A(v), and makes textual and grammatical amendments across regulations 8, 9, 11, 16, 20, 21 and 24.

Introduces a Companies-Act-linked cooling-off between successive buy-back offers, a prohibition on buy-backs that would breach minimum public shareholding, a two-working-day public-announcement deadline and a one-working-day electronic shareholder-intimation duty for open-market buy-backs.

Makes numerous small textual and grammatical corrections across regulations 8, 9, 11, 16, 20, 21 and 24 (marginal head) and revises the regulation 20(iv) bank-guarantee validity/return wording, without changing their substantive effect (regulation 20(ii) substitutes 'may' with 'shall').

evidence.supporting_text: The Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III Section 4, SEBI Notification dated the 1st July, 2026, titled 'Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-Back of Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026', No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2026/306, e-Gazette code CG-MH-E-06072026-274199.

In exercise of the powers conferred by sections 11(1) and (2) and section 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with section 68(2)(f) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Board makes these regulations to further amend the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018.
These regulations may be called the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 and shall come into force on August 1, 2026.

After the existing regulation 24, a new regulation 24A is inserted: notwithstanding anything in the regulations, engaging a merchant banker is discretionary for a company undertaking buy-back; if the company dispenses with the merchant banker, it must ensure that the persons in column 4 of the table (company, secretarial auditor, statutory auditor, stock exchanges, compliance officer) undertake the obligations otherwise required to be undertaken by the merchant banker (filing of letter of offer and public announcement, due-diligence certification, oversight of escrow accounts, VWAP and sell-order certification, presence at and verification of extinguishment, final report, funds/firm-financial-arrangement assurance, and Companies Act, 2013 compliance).

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.X (new regulation 24(i)(ea) - promoter-holding ISIN freeze) and 3.XII (Schedule V)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 24, after clause (e) of sub-regulation (i), a new clause (ea) is inserted: shares or other specified securities held by the promoter(s) and promoter group including their associates, for which buy-back is undertaken, shall remain frozen at the ISIN level during the period from the date of passing of the board resolution or the special resolution, as the case may be, till the closing of the offer; the freeze does not apply for the limited purpose of tendering in a tender-offer buy-back; transfer on invocation of encumbrances created prior to the commencement of the buy-back period may be allowed with the freeze continuing, subject to conditions specified by the Board; the company shall instruct the depositories to give effect to the freeze. In Schedule V, the words, numerals and symbols '8(i)(c),' and 'and 22(iv)' are omitted.

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.I and 3.VI (open-market buy-back limit and timeline)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 4(iv)(b), in the second proviso, after 'April 1, 2025' the words 'till July 31, 2026' are inserted, and after that proviso a new third proviso is inserted: with effect from August 1, 2026, a buy-back from the open market through the stock exchange shall be less than fifteen per cent of the paid-up capital and free reserves of the company, based on both standalone and consolidated financial statements. In regulation 17, sub-regulation (i) is omitted; in the proviso to sub-regulation (ii) after 'March 31, 2025' the words 'till July 31, 2026' are inserted; and a new sub-regulation (iii) is inserted: with effect from August 1, 2026, a buy-back offer shall open within four working days from the date of the public announcement and close within sixty-six working days from the date of opening of the offer.

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.I (regulation 4(vii), 4(xi)) and 3.V/3.IX (regulation 16, 22A - public announcement and shareholder intimation)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 4, sub-regulation (vii) is substituted so that a company shall not make any offer of buy-back within such period as may be prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 from the date of closure of the preceding offer of buy-back; a new sub-regulation (xi) is inserted so that a company shall not propose any buy-back of shares or other specified securities that results in the breach of the minimum public shareholding requirements prescribed under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957 or specified under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. In regulation 16(iv), clause (b) is substituted so that the public announcement shall be made within two working days from the date of passing of the board resolution or the date of declaration of results of the postal ballot for special resolution, and a new clause (ba) is inserted requiring the company, within one working day from the date of the public announcement, to send an electronic intimation of the open-market buy-back offer to persons who were its shareholders as on the date of the public announcement; the same one-working-day electronic-intimation requirement is inserted as regulation 22A(v).

Regulations 8(i), 9(xi)(c)-(g), 11, 16, 20, 21(iii), 22A(i) and 24 (marginal head) are amended by numerous small textual and grammatical substitutions and insertions (for example changing 'until' to 'till', 'may' to 'shall', inserting connecting words, and marginal-head wording), that clarify and correct the drafting without changing the substantive effect of those provisions; regulation 20(ii) also substitutes 'may' with 'shall' and regulation 20(iv) revises the bank-guarantee validity and return wording.

Signed by Amit Pradhan, Executive Director; the Note records that the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 were published in the Gazette of India on September 11, 2018 vide notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2018/32 and were last amended on November 20, 2024 by the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2024 vide notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2024/210.

events.title: New regulation 9A - promoter-identified employees may retain and exercise pre-IPO share benefits
events.scope_description: The SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 are amended to insert regulation 9A: an employee identified as a 'promoter' or part of the 'promoter group' in the draft offer document filed for an initial public offering, who was granted options / SAR / any other benefit under a scheme at least one year before the draft offer document was filed, is eligible to continue to hold and/or exercise those benefits in accordance with their terms and subject to compliance with the regulations and other applicable laws. The amendment comes into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

events.title: Regulation 34 valuation to be done by an independent registered valuer; 'valuer' redefined; sub-regulations 34(2)-(3) omitted
events.scope_description: The SBEB Regulations, 2021 are amended: regulation 2(1)(ww) is substituted so 'valuer' has the meaning under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 (as amended from time to time); in regulation 34(1) 'a merchant banker' is replaced by 'an independent registered valuer', with a proviso that a merchant banker must complete an ongoing valuation assignment undertaken before the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations came into force within nine months of that commencement; and regulation 34(2) and (3) are omitted. The amendment comes into force on the thirtieth day from Gazette publication.

classification.practice_rationale: The amendment changes the definition of 'valuer' and who performs the regulation 34 valuation for share-based employee benefits and sweat equity (a listed-entity / issuer employee-equity matter within Capital Markets, CM); it also removes a function from merchant bankers, an intermediary-scope change giving a Financial Regulatory (FR) secondary workflow.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Companies undertaking valuation for share-based employee benefits / sweat equity under the SBEB Regulations
affected_entities.scope_note: Companies that must obtain the regulation 34 valuation now from an independent registered valuer (as defined by section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013) rather than a merchant banker.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Merchant bankers previously performing regulation 34 valuations
affected_entities.scope_note: Merchant bankers are removed from the regulation 34 valuation function but must complete valuation assignments already undertaken before the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations came into force, within nine months of that commencement.

affected_entities.name_or_scope: Independent registered valuers (as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013)
affected_entities.scope_note: Independent registered valuers become the persons who perform the regulation 34 valuation under the SBEB Regulations; no dedicated V1 entity tag corresponds to this role.

classification_support.reason: CM/CM_LISTED_EMP and TP_EMPLOYEE_EQUITY from the share-based employee benefit / sweat equity subject-matter; TP_VALUATION and the EN_ISSUER role from the regulation 34 valuation requirement; FR_INTERMED and EN_MERCHANT_BANKER from the removal of the valuation function from merchant bankers; FW_SBEB from the amended regulations; FW_COMPANIES (section 247) and FW_SEBI_ACT from the cited enabling and definitional provisions.

legal_effects.description: Amends the SBEB Regulations, 2021 by substituting the definition of 'valuer' in regulation 2(1)(ww), substituting 'a merchant banker' with 'an independent registered valuer' in regulation 34(1) and inserting a transitional proviso, and omitting regulation 34(2) and (3).
legal_effects.savings_or_limitations: A merchant banker must complete a valuation assignment already undertaken before the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations came into force, within nine months of that commencement.

legal_effects.description: Changes who performs the regulation 34 valuation for share-based employee benefits and sweat equity from a merchant banker to an independent registered valuer as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013.

operative_change.summary: The regulation 34 valuation must be performed by an independent registered valuer instead of a merchant banker, 'valuer' is tied to section 247 of the Companies Act, and regulation 34(2)-(3) are omitted.
operative_change.previous_position: Under regulation 34(1) the valuation was to be made by a merchant banker; regulation 34 had sub-regulations (2) and (3).
operative_change.new_or_proposed_position: The valuation under regulation 34(1) is to be made by an independent registered valuer; 'valuer' has the meaning under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended from time to time; regulation 34(2) and (3) are omitted; a merchant banker must complete any ongoing pre-September 8, 2025 valuation assignment within nine months of the commencement of the September 8, 2025 Amendment Regulations.

actions.description: The valuation required under regulation 34(1) of the SBEB Regulations shall be carried out by an independent registered valuer as defined under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013.

effective_from.raw_text: They shall come into force on the thirtieth day from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

deadlines.obligation: A merchant banker shall complete an ongoing regulation 34 valuation assignment undertaken prior to the coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025.

timing.anchor_event: coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
conditions: assignment undertaken before that commencement

transitional_provisions.rule: The merchant banker must complete that assignment within nine months from the date of coming into force of those regulations.

notification.importance_reason: Changes who performs a required valuation under the SBEB Regulations and redefines 'valuer', with a transitional window; it materially changes a professional-services requirement but affects a defined set of transactions and adds no ongoing filing obligation.

evidence.supporting_text: The Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III Section 4, SEBI Notification dated the 3rd December, 2025, titled 'Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025', F. No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2025/284, gazette code CG-MH-E-04122025-268233.

In exercise of the powers conferred by sections 11, 11A and 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with sections 54 and 62 of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules 8 and 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, the Board makes these regulations to amend the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021.

These regulations may be called the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 and shall come into force on the thirtieth day from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

In the 2021 Regulations, in regulation 2, sub-regulation (1), the existing clause (ww) is substituted so that 'valuer' shall have the same meaning as assigned to it under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended from time to time.

evidence.locator: Regulation 3.II (regulation 34 - valuation by independent registered valuer, proviso, omissions)
evidence.supporting_text: In regulation 34: in sub-regulation (1), 'a merchant banker.' is substituted with 'an independent registered valuer:' and a proviso is inserted that a merchant banker shall complete an ongoing valuation assignment undertaken prior to the coming into force of the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 within a period of nine months from the date of coming into force of the said regulations; the existing sub-regulations (2) and (3) of regulation 34 are omitted.

Signed by Amit Pradhan, Executive Director; footnotes record that the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 were published in the Gazette on 13th August, 2021 vide No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2021/40 and were amended on September 8, 2025 by the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 vide notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2025/262.
